rashi.heb:
*גם אני.* 
את בגדת עלי וגם אני הנני עליך:
rashi.eng: *I too.* You betrayed Me, and I too, behold I am upon you.

notes.145: (tn): In context “you” refers to the city of Jerusalem. To make this clear for the modern reader, “Jerusalem” has been supplied in the translation in apposition to “you.” This cannibalism would occur as a result of starvation due to the city being besieged. It is one of the judgments threatened for a covenant law violation (Lev 26:29; see also Deut 28:53; Jer 19:9; Lam 2:20; Zech 11:9).

notes.148: (tn): The meaning of the Hebrew term is primarily emotional: “to pity,” which in context implies an action, as in being moved by pity in order to spare them from the horror of their punishment.

notes.149: (sn): The judgment of plague and famine comes from the covenant curse (Lev 26:25-26). As in v. 10, the city of Jerusalem is figuratively addressed here.
notes.150: (sn): Judgment by plague, famine, and sword occurs in Jer 21:9; 27:13; Ezek 6:11, 12; 7:15.

notes.152: (tn): The Hebrew noun translated “jealousy” is used in the human realm to describe suspicion of adultery (Num 5:14ff.; Prov 6:34). Since Israel’s relationship with God was often compared to a marriage this term is appropriate here. The term occurs elsewhere in Ezekiel in 8:3, 5; 16:38, 42; 23:25.

rashi.heb:
*והניחותי חמתו.* 
כשאנקם בם תנוח חמתי ולא תציקני רוחי:
rashi.eng: *and I shall cause My fury against them to subside.* When I avenge Myself against them, My fury will subside, and My spirit will not oppress Me.

rashi.heb:
*והנחמתי.* 
ואתנחם על הצער שצערתם אותי:
rashi.eng: *and I shall be comforted.* Heb. וְהִנֶחָמְתִּי. And I shall be comforted from the pain that you inflicted upon Me.

rashi.heb:
*ולחרפה.* 
דישטרוי"ר בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *a ruin.* Heb. לְחָרְבָּה, destroyer in Old French, to make desolate, destroy.

notes.153: (tc): This reading is supported by the versions and by the Dead Sea Scrolls (11QEzek). Most Masoretic Hebrew mss read “it will be,” but if the final he (ה) is read as a mater lectionis, as it can be with the second masculine singular perfect, then they are in agreement. In either case the subject refers to Jerusalem.
notes.154: (tn): The Hebrew word occurs only here in the OT. A related verb means “revile, taunt” (see Ps 44:16).
notes.155: (tn, Heb): “discipline and devastation.” These words are omitted in the Old Greek. The first term pictures Jerusalem as a recipient or example of divine discipline; the second depicts her as a desolate ruin (see Ezek 6:14).
notes.156: (tn, Heb): “in anger and in fury and in rebukes of fury.” The heaping up of synonyms emphasizes the degree of God’s anger.

rashi.heb:
*וגדופה.* 
בזיון:
rashi.eng: *and a taunt.* A disgrace.

rashi.heb:
*מוסר.* 
יסורין:
rashi.eng: *a chastisement.* Heb. מוּסָר torments.

rashi.heb:
*ומשמה.* 
תמהון:
rashi.eng: *and an astonishment.* A wonder.

notes.157: (tn): The Hebrew word carries the basic idea of “bad, displeasing, injurious,” but when used of weapons has the nuance “deadly” (see Ps 144:10).
notes.159: (tn): The language of this verse may have been influenced by Deut 32:23.
notes.160: (tn): Or “which were to destroy those whom I will send to destroy you” (cf. NASB).
notes.161: (tn): Heb, “break the staff of bread.” The bread supply is compared to a staff that one uses for support. See 4:16, as well as the covenant curse in Lev 26:26.

rashi.heb:
*ורעב אוסיף עליכם.* 
הוא רעב הפרוטה הכלה מן הכיס כך שמעתי:
rashi.eng: *and I shall add a famine upon you.* This is the famine of the penny depleted from the pocket. So I heard.

rashi.heb:
*מטה לחם.* 
משען לחם:
rashi.eng: *your staff of bread.* Support of bread.

notes.163: (tn, Heb): “will pass through you.” This threat recalls the warning of Lev 26:22, 25 and Deut 32:24-25.

notes.164: (tn, Heb): “set your face against.” The expression occurs at the beginning of Ezekiel’s prophetic oracles in Ezek 13:17; 20:46; 21:2; 25:2; 28:21; 29:2; 35:2; 38:2.�Based on comparison to a similar expression in Ugaritic, the phrase may imply that Ezekiel was to actually go to these locations to deliver his message.

notes.165: (tn): The phrase “mountains of Israel” occurs only in the book of Ezekiel (6:2, 3; 19:9; 33:28; 34:13, 14; 35:12; 36:1, 4, 8; 37:22; 38:8; 39:2, 4, 17). The expression refers to the whole land of Israel. The mountainous terrain of Israel would contrast with the exiles’ habitat in the river valley of Babylonia.
notes.166: (tn): The introductory formula “Hear the word of the sovereign Lord” parallels a pronouncement delivered by the herald of a king (2 Kgs 18:28).
notes.167: (tn, Heb): “Look I, I am bringing.” The repetition of the pronoun draws attention to the speaker. The construction also indicates that the action is soon to come; the Lord is “about to bring a sword against” them.
notes.168: (tn): The Hebrew term refers to elevated platforms where pagan sacrifices were performed.

rashi.heb:
*ולגבעות.* 
לשון רמה:
rashi.eng: *and to the hills.* [Heb. [ולגבעות is] a term expressing height.

rashi.heb:
*ולגאיות.* 
לשון גיא:
rashi.eng: *and to the valleys.* [ולגאיות is] a term expressing valleys.

notes.169: (tn): Thirty-nine of the forty-eight biblical occurrences of this Hebrew word are found in the book of Ezekiel.�This verse is probably based on Lev 26:30 in which God forecasts that he will destroy their high places, cut off their incense altars, and set their corpses by the corpses of their idols.

rashi.heb:
*חמניכם.* 
מין תבנית צלמי עכו"ם העשויין על הגגות לחמה:
rashi.eng: *your sun gods.* חַמָּנֵיכֶם, a class of pagan idols made on the roofs [dedicated] to the sun.

notes.170: (tc): This first sentence, which explains the meaning of the last sentence of the previous verse, does not appear in the LXX and may be an instance of a marginal explanatory note making its way into the text.

notes.171: (tn): The Hebrew verb translated “wiped out” is used to describe the judgment of the Flood (Gen 6:7; 7:4, 23).

rashi.heb:
*ויאשמו.* 
יהיו נכרים באשמתם:
rashi.eng: *and shown to be guilty.* Heb. ויאשמו [lit. they be made guilty.] They will be recognized for their guilt.

notes.172: (sn): The phrase you will know that I am the Lord concludes over sixty oracles in the book of Ezekiel and indicates the ultimate goal of God’s action. The phrase is often used in the book of Exodus as well (Exod 7:5; 14:4, 18). By Ezekiel’s day the people had forgotten that the Lord (Yahweh) was their covenant God and had turned to other gods. They had to be reminded that Yahweh alone deserved to be worshiped because only he possessed the power to meet their needs. Through judgment and eventually deliverance, Israel would be reminded that Yahweh alone held their destiny in his hands.

notes.173: (tn, Heb): “when you have fugitives from the sword among the nations, when you are scattered among the lands.”

notes.174: (tn): The words “they will realize” are not in the Hebrew text; they are added here for stylistic reasons since this clause assumes the previous verb “to remember” or “to take into account.”
notes.175: (tn, Heb): “how I was broken by their adulterous heart.” The image of God being “broken” is startling, but perfectly natural within the metaphorical framework of God as offended husband. The idiom must refer to the intense grief that Israel’s unfaithfulness caused God. For a discussion of the syntax and semantics of the Hebrew text, see M. Greenberg, Ezekiel (AB), 1:134.

rashi.heb:
*וזכרו פליטיכם אותי.* 
את חסדי ואת רחמי שהייתי מרחם עליהם בהעוותם לפני בארצם:
rashi.eng: *And those of you that escape will remember Me.* My kindnesses and My compassion, that I had compassion on them when they committed iniquities before Me in their land.

rashi.heb:
*אשר נשברתי את לבם הזונה.* 
אשר נכנעתי אצלם אע"פ שזונה לבם וסר מעלי הייתי מבקש מהם ע"י נביאי לשוב אלי ואטיב להם ולא אבו:
rashi.eng: *that I yielded to their straying heart.* That I yielded to them. Although their heart went astray and they turned away from Me, I begged of them, through My prophets, to return to Me, and [promised] that I will [then] do good for them, but they were unwilling.

rashi.heb:
*ונקוטו בפניהם.* 
מנחם חברו עם ראיתי בוגדים ואתקוטט' (שם קי"ט) יתקוטטו על עצמם על אשר לא שמעו אלי וי"ת וידנקון ואינון יהון חזן וכן תרגם הנאנקים דמדנקים ובכי ואנק' דמדנקן דמוניי"ר בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *and they will quarrel with themselves.* Heb. וְנָקֹטוּ. Menachem associated it with (Ps. 119:158): “I saw traitors, and I quarreled (וָאֶתְקוֹטָטָה).” They will quarrel with themselves for not listening to Me. Jonathan renders: וְידַנְקוּן and they will see, and so does he translate (below 9:4): “those who groan (הַנֶאֶנָקִים),” דְּמִדַנְקִין, and (Mal. 2:13): “weeping… and groaning (וַאֲנָקָה),” דְּמִדַנְקָן, demonir in Old French, to groan.

notes.177: (tn, Heb): “not in vain did I speak to do to them this catastrophe.” The wording of the last half of v. 10 parallels God’s declaration after the sin of the golden calf (Exod 32:14).

notes.178: (sn): By the sword and by famine and by pestilence. A similar trilogy of punishments is mentioned in Lev 26:25-26. See also Jer 14:12; 21:9; 27:8, 13; 29:18).

rashi.heb:
*ורקע.* 
עניינו יורה עליו מכה רגלו על הארץ ומרדד את הטיט והוא דרך אבל:
rashi.eng: *and stamp.* Its context implies that it means to stamp one’s foot on the ground to flatten out the mud, and this is a custom of a mourner.

rashi.heb:
*ואמר אח.* 
צעקת יגון ואוי:
rashi.eng: *and say, Ah!.* A cry of grief and woe.

notes.179: (tn, Heb): “the one who is left, the one who is spared.”

rashi.heb:
*והנצור.* 
הנאסף אל העיר ויצורו עליו:
rashi.eng: *and who is in the siege.* Heb. והנצור, one who is gathered into the city when they besiege it.

rashi.heb:
*וכליתי חמתי.* 
אשלי' כל חרוני וחפצי ברעתם:
rashi.eng: *and I shall spend My fury.* I shall finish all My fury and My desire to do evil to them.

notes.180: (sn): By referring to every high hill…all the mountaintops…under every green tree and every leafy oak Ezekiel may be expanding on the phraseology of Deut 12:2 (see 1 Kgs 14:23; 2 Kgs 16:4; 17:10; Jer 2:20; 3:6, 13; 2 Chr 28:4).

rashi.heb:
*אלה.* 
פלנצו"ן בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *terebinth.* Heb. אֵלָה, planzon in Old French, a branch.

rashi.heb:
*עבתה.* 
לשון עץ עבות (לקמן כ) שענפיו מרובין:
rashi.eng: *branchy.* עֲבֻתָּה, an expression of (below 20:28): “a branchy (עָבוֹת) tree,” i.e., whose branches are many.

notes.181: (sn): I will stretch out my hand against them is a common expression in the book of Ezekiel (14:9, 13; 16:27; 25:7; 35:3).
notes.182: (tc): The Vulgate reads the name as “Riblah,” a city north of Damascus. The MT reads Diblah, a city otherwise unknown. The letters resh (ר) and dalet (ד) may have been confused in the Hebrew text. The town of Riblah was in the land of Hamath (2 Kgs 23:33) which represented the northern border of Israel (Ezek 47:14).

rashi.heb:
*שממה.* 
מאין יושב:
rashi.eng: *a desolation.* Heb. שְּׁמָמָה, without an inhabitant.

rashi.heb:
*משמה.* 
תמהון שיתמהו עליה רואיה:
rashi.eng: *and an astonishment.* Heb. ומשמה, a wonder, i.e., that all who see it will wonder about it.

notes.183: (tn): Or “earth.” Elsewhere the expression “four corners of the earth” figuratively refers to the whole earth (Isa 11:12).

rashi.heb:
*בא הקץ.* 
שאמרתי ונושנתם בארץ והשחתם וגו' העידותי בכם היום כי אבוד תאבדון (דברים ד׳:כ״ה) ונושנתם בגי' תתנ"ב והם נשתהו בה תת"ן ד' מאות ומ' משנכנסו לה עד שנבנה הבית ות"י שנים עמד הבית:
rashi.eng: *The end has come.* Because I had said (Deut. 4:25): “and you will have grown old (וְנוֹשַּׁנְתֶּם) in the land, and you will practice corruption, etc., so that you will be lost.” [The word] וְנוֹשַּׁנְתֶּם has the numerical value of 852, but they stayed there for [only] 850 years: 440 from the time they entered it until the Temple was built, and [then] the Temple stood 410 years.

notes.187: (tn): The meaning of the Hebrew term is primarily emotional: “to pity,” which in context implies an action, as in being moved by pity in order to spare them from the horror of their punishment.
notes.188: (tn): The pronoun “you” is not in the Hebrew text, but is implied.
notes.189: (tn): “I will set your behavior on your head.”
notes.190: (tn, Heb): “and your abominable practices will be among you.”

notes.191: (tn): The Hebrew term often refers to moral evil (see Ezek 6:10; 14:22), but in many contexts it refers to calamity or disaster, sometimes as punishment for evil behavior.
notes.192: (tc): So most Hebrew mss; many Hebrew mss read “disaster after disaster” (cf. NAB, NCV, NRSV, NLT).

rashi.heb:
*רעה אחת רעה.* 
רעה שלימה ומיוחדת למעלה מכל הרעות והוא חורבן הבית:
rashi.eng: *An evil, a singular evil.* Heb. רָעָה אַחַתרָעָה, a total, special evil, worse than all evils; that is the destruction of the Temple.

rashi.heb:
*הנה באה.* 
טעמו באל"ף הוא לשון פועלת:
rashi.eng: *behold it comes.* Heb. בָאָה. Its accent is on the ‘aleph.’ It is in the present tense.

notes.195: (tc): With different vowels the verb rendered “it has awakened” would be the noun “the end,” as in “the end is upon you.” The verb would represent a phonetic wordplay. The noun by virtue of repetition would continue to reinforce the idea of the end. Whether verb or noun, this is the only instance to occur with this preposition.
notes.196: (tc): For this entire verse, the LXX has only “the end is come.” In each of the three cases of the verb translated with forms of “to come,” the form may either be a participle (“comes/is coming”) or a perfect (“has come”). Either form would indicate that the end is soon to arrive. This last form appears also to be feminine, although “end” is masculine. This shift may be looking ahead to the next verse, whose first noun (“Doom”) is feminine.

notes.197: (sn): The day refers to the day of the Lord, a concept which, beginning in Amos 5:18-20, became a common theme in the OT prophetic books. It refers to a time when the Lord intervenes in human affairs as warrior and judge.
notes.198: (tc): The LXX reads “neither tumult nor birth pains.” The LXX varies at many points from the MT in this chapter. The context suggests that one or both of these would be present on a day of judgment, thus favoring the MT. Perhaps more significant is the absence of “the mountains” in the LXX. If the ר (resh) in הָרִים (harim, “the mountains” not “on the mountains”) were a ד (dalet), which is a common letter confusion, then it could be from the same root as the previous word, הֵד (hed), meaning “the day is near – with destruction, not joyful shouting.”

rashi.heb:
*באה הצפירה.* 
טעמו למעלה בבי"ת והוא לשון פעלה כבר באה הצפירה כמו בא ושקע מאור השחר והתפארת בא:
rashi.eng: *The dawn has set.* Heb. בָּאָה הַצְפִירָה. Its accent is at the beginning of the word, and it is in the past tense. The צְפִירָה has already set. The light of the dawn and the glory has already set.

rashi.heb:
*ולא הד הרים.* 
ולא לאישתיזבא במצדי טוריא והד לשון צעקת הכרזה לקום לברוח אל ראשי ההרים כמו הידד השבתי (ישעיה יז) וענו עליו הידד (ירמיה כא) השמעת קול נושא משא ענבים אל הגת וטועני הקורה:
rashi.eng: *and not the shout of the mountains.* [Jonathan renders:] And not to escape into the strongholds of the mountains. [The word] הֵד means the cry of the announcement to rise and flee to the mountaintops, like (Isa. 16:10): “the shout [of joy] (הֵידָד) have I abolished.” Also (Jer. 51:1): “and they shall raise a battle-cry (הֵידָד) against you.” The shout of those who carry the load of grapes to the winepress and those who load on the beam.

notes.199: (tn): The expression “to pour out rage” also occurs in Ezek 9:8; 14:19; 20:8, 13, 21; 22:31; 30:15; 36:18.

rashi.heb:
*מקרוב.* 
במהרה:
rashi.eng: *Speedily.* Heb. מקרוב, [lit. from close.] Quickly.

notes.200: (tn): The meaning of the Hebrew term is primarily emotional: “to pity,” which in context implies an action, as in being moved by pity in order to spare them from the horror of their punishment.
notes.201: (tn, Heb): “According to your behavior I will place on you.”
notes.202: (tn): The MT lacks “you.” It has been added for clarification.

rashi.heb:
*הנה היום.* 
הנה בא היום:
rashi.eng: *Behold the day.* Behold the day has come.

rashi.heb:
*הנה באה.* 
הרעה:
rashi.eng: *behold it is coming.* The evil.

rashi.heb:
*יצאה הצפירה.* 
עלה השחר של יום הרעה:
rashi.eng: *the dawn has gone forth.* The dawn of the day of the evil.

rashi.heb:
*צץ המטה.* 
להכות אתכם:
rashi.eng: *the staff has budded.* to strike you.

rashi.heb:
*פרח הזדון.* 
נתגלה נבוכדנצר הרשע:
rashi.eng: *the willful wickedness has blossomed.* The wicked Nebuchadnezzar has revealed himself.

notes.204: (tc): The LXX reads “he will crush the wicked rod without confusion or haste.” The verb has been supplied for the Hebrew text to clarify the sense.
notes.205: (tn): The Hebrew word occurs only here in the OT.

rashi.heb:
*החמס קם וגו'.* 
החמס אשר בידכם הוא קם עליכם למטה רשע לשחתכם:
rashi.eng: *The violence has arisen, etc..* The violence in your hands has risen upon you as a staff of wickedness to destroy you.

rashi.heb:
*לא מהם.* 
כך אמר הקב"ה למשחית אינך זקוק להשאיר נפש מרשעי ישראל כי אין טובה יוצאת לא מהם ולא מבניהם ולא מהמונם:
rashi.eng: *neither from them.* So said the Holy One, blessed be He, to the Destroyer: You are not required to spare a soul [from the wicked of Israel], for no good will come from them or from their children or from their multitude.

rashi.heb:
*ולא נה בהם.* 
אין בהם נוהה אחרי מגעגע ונותן לב אלי כמו וינהו כל בית ישראל אחרי ה' (שמואל א ו) ולשון ארמי הוא ואיתנהיאו לפולחנא ל' תאוה וגעגועין ומנח' חברו לשון יללה וכן וינהו כל בית ישראל פירש לשון יללה ואין בתיבה רק ה"א יסוד:
rashi.eng: *and no one among them longs.* No one among them longs or gives thought to Me, as in (I Sam. 7:2): “and all the house of Israel longed (וַיִנָהוּ) for the Lord.” This is an Aramaism: “And they longed (וְאִתְנְהִיאוּ) for My worship,” an expression of desire and longing. Menachem (p. 69) associated it with יללה, an expression of wailing, and the word retains only the ‘hey’ as a radical.

notes.206: (tn, Heb): “wrath.” Context clarifies that God’s wrath is in view.

rashi.heb:
*והמוכר אל יתאבל.* 
אע"פ שדרך המוכר שדהו להיות עצב אל יתעצב כי סופכם לגלות:
rashi.eng: *neither will the seller mourn.* Although one who sells his field usually grieves, he will not grieve because you are destined to go into exile.

notes.207: (tc): The translation follows the LXX for the first line of the verse, although the LXX has lost the second line due to homoioteleuton (similar endings of the clauses). The MT reads “The seller will not return to the sale.” This Hebrew reading has been construed as a reference to land redemption, the temporary sale of the use of property, with property rights returned to the seller in the year of Jubilee. But the context has no other indicator that land redemption is in view. If correct, the LXX evidence suggests that one of the cases of “the customer” has been replaced by “the seller” in the MT, perhaps due to hoimoioarcton (similar beginnings of the words).
notes.208: (tn): The Hebrew word refers to the din or noise made by a crowd, and by extension may refer to the crowd itself.
notes.209: (tn): Or “in their punishment.” The phrase “in/for [a person’s] iniquity” occurs fourteen times in Ezekiel: here and in v. 16; 3:18, 19; 4:17; 18:17, 18, 19, 20; 24:23; 33:6, 8, 9; 39:23. The Hebrew word for “iniquity” may also mean the “punishment for iniquity.”

rashi.heb:
*כי המוכר אל הממכר לא ישוב.* 
כשיגלה בגולה לא ישוב ויראה עוד השדה שמכר ולמה יתאבל:
rashi.eng: *For the seller will not return to that which was sold.* Once he goes into exile, he will not return and will no longer see the field that he had sold; so why should he mourn?

rashi.heb:
*ועוד בחיים חיתם.* 
כל ימי חייהם לא ישיבו אל מקומם:
rashi.eng: *as long as they are alive.* All the days of their lives they will not return to their place.

rashi.heb:
*כי חזון אל כל המונה וגו'.* 
ארי נבייא מתנבן על כל אתרגושתהון למיתב בתיובתא ולא תייבין:
rashi.eng: *for when the prophecy was [directed] to all her multitude, etc..* For the prophets prophesy concerning all their multitude to repent, but they do not repent.

rashi.heb:
*ואיש בעונו חיתו.* 
כל אחד מהם חיתו ונפשו דבוקה בעונו:
rashi.eng: *and each man’s soul is in his iniquity.* The life and soul of every one of them is attached to his iniquity.

rashi.heb:
*לא יתחזקו.* 
לא יחזקו לבם על יצרם הרע לשוב לתורתם:
rashi.eng: *they do not strengthen themselves.* They do not strengthen their heart over their evil inclination, to return to their Torah.

notes.210: (tn): The Hebrew word refers to the din or noise made by a crowd, and by extension may refer to the crowd itself.

rashi.heb:
*תקעו בתקוע.* 
כשיבוא עליהם הצר הכינו עצמם למלחמה ואין יוצא להלחם:
rashi.eng: *They sound the shofar.* When the enemy comes upon them, they prepare themselves for war, but no one will go out to fight.

rashi.heb:
*כיוני הגאיות.* 
דרך היונים להקבץ בגאיות והומות שם והיו הומים אל ההרים אשר ינוסו שם איש בעוונו כיוני הגאיות אשר כולם הומות:
rashi.eng: *like the doves of the valleys.* It is customary for doves to congregate in the valleys and moan there. They [the survivors] will moan on the mountains, where they will flee, each one for his iniquity, like the doves of the valleys, which all moan.

notes.211: (tn, Heb): “their knees will run with water.” The expression probably refers to urination caused by fright, which is how the LXX renders the phrase. More colloquial English would simply be “they will wet their pants,” but as D. I. Block (Ezekiel [NICOT], 1:261, n. 98) notes, the men likely wore skirts which were short enough to expose urine on the knees.

rashi.heb:
*תלכנה מים.* 
מזיעת אימה:
rashi.eng: *will go [like] water.* from the sweat of fright.

notes.212: (tn, Heb): “baldness will be on their heads.”

notes.213: (tn): The Hebrew term can refer to menstrual impurity. The term also occurs at the end of v. 20.
notes.215: (tn, Heb): “it.” Apparently the subject is the silver and gold mentioned earlier (see L. C. Allen, Ezekiel [WBC], 1:102).
notes.216: (tn): The “stumbling block of their iniquity” is a unique phrase of the prophet Ezekiel (Ezek 14:3, 4, 7; 18:30; 44:12).

rashi.heb:
*לנדה יהיה.* 
לשקוץ יהיה להם:
rashi.eng: *will be repugnant.* It will be disgusting for them.

notes.217: (tc): The MT reads “he set up the beauty of his ornament as pride.” The verb may be repointed as plural without changing the consonantal text. The Syriac reads “their ornaments” (plural), implying עֶדְיָם (’edyam) rather than עֶדְיוֹ (’edyo) and meaning “they were proud of their beautiful ornaments.” This understands “ornaments” in the common sense of women’s jewelry, which then were used to make idols. The singular suffix “his ornaments” would refer to using items from the temple treasury to make idols. D. I. Block points out the foreshadowing of Ezek 16:17 which, with Rashi and the Targum, supports the understanding that this is a reference to temple items. See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 1:265.

rashi.heb:
*וצבי עדיו.* 
של הקב"ה אשר לגאון שמהו להם הוא בית המקדש שנקרא גאון עוזם כמה שנאמ' (לקמן כד) הנני מחלל את מקדשי גאון עוזכם הם גלולי תועבות עשו בו ע"כ וגו':
rashi.eng: *And the beauty of His adornment.* of the Holy One, blessed be He, that He made for their pride. This is the Temple, called the pride of their might, as it is said (24:21): “Behold I profane My sanctuary, the pride of Your might.” They made in it the images of their abominations, therefore, etc.

notes.218: (sn): My treasured place probably refers to the temple (however, cf. NLT “my treasured land”).
notes.219: (sn): Since the pronouns “it” are both feminine, they do not refer to the masculine “my treasured place”; instead they probably refer to Jerusalem or the land, both of which are feminine in Hebrew.

rashi.heb:
*את צפוני.* 
את המקום שהייתי צפון שם ביניהם:
rashi.eng: *My secret place.* The place where I was hidden among them.

notes.220: (tc): The Hebrew word “the chain” occurs only here in the OT. The reading of the LXX (“and they will make carnage”) seems to imply a Hebrew text of ַהבַּתּוֹק (habbattoq, “disorder, slaughter”) instead of הָרַתּוֹק (haratoq, “the chain”). The LXX is also translating the verb as a third person plural future and taking this as the end of the preceding verse. As M. Greenberg (Ezekiel [AB], 1:154) notes, this may refer to a chain for a train of exiles but “the context does not speak of exile but of the city’s fall. The versions guess desperately and we can do little better.”
notes.221: (tn, Heb): “judgment for blood,” i.e., indictment or accountability for bloodshed. The word for “judgment” does not appear in the similar phrase in 9:9.

rashi.heb:
*עשה הרתוק.* 
שלשלת אות הוא שילכו בגולה אסורים בזיקים:
rashi.eng: *Make the chain.* Heb. הָרַתּוֹק, the chain. It is a symbolic sign that they will go into exile bound in fetters.

rashi.heb:
*משפט דמים.* 
חייבי קטול:
rashi.eng: *crimes of bloodshed.* [lit. judgment of blood. Targum renders:] Crimes deserving of death.

notes.222: (sn): Or “their holy places” (KJV, ASV, NASB, NCV, NRSV).

rashi.heb:
*רעי גוים.* 
רעים שבעכו"ם ואכזרים:
rashi.eng: *the most wicked of the nations.* Heb. רָעֵי גוֹיִם. The most wicked and cruel of the nations.

rashi.heb:
*ונחלו.* 
ויתנחלו לאחרים:
rashi.eng: *and they will deliver as an inheritance.* Heb. וְנִחֲלוּ, they will give over to others as an inheritance.

rashi.heb:
*מקדשיהם.* 
בתי היכל הבמות שהיו נועדים שם ל' בית זמונם:
rashi.eng: *their meeting places.* Heb. מְקַדְשֵׁיהֶם. The temples of the high places, where they would gather at appointed times; an expression of a house of their appointment.

notes.223: (tn): The Hebrew word occurs only here in the OT. It is interpreted based on a Syriac cognate meaning “to bristle or stiffen (in terror).”

rashi.heb:
*קפדה בא.* 
כמו (ישעיהו ל״ח:י״ב) קפדתי כאורג חיי לשון כריתה:
rashi.eng: *A cutting off comes.* Heb. קְפָדָה like (Isa. 38:12): “I severed (קִפַּדְתִּי) like a weaver, my life”; a term denoting cutting off.

rashi.heb:
*הוה על הוה.* 
מאורע על מאורע הויה אחר הויה ומנחם חברו לשון שבר:
rashi.eng: *Happening upon happening.* Heb. הוֹה עַל-הוֹה, happening upon happening, being after being. Menachem (p. 70) associated it to a term for a breach.

rashi.heb:
*ותורה תאבד מכהן.* 
הרגילים בהוראה כמו שנאמר ותורה יבקשו מפיהו (מלאכי ב׳:ז׳):
rashi.eng: *and instruction will be lost from a priest.* who usually gave instruction, as is said (Mal. 2:7): “and teaching should be sought from his mouth.”

notes.225: (tc): The LXX reads “In the sixth year, in the fifth month, on the fifth of the month.” In the sixth year, in the sixth month, on the fifth of the month would be September 17, 592 b.c., about fourteen months after the initial vision.
notes.226: (tn): Or “power.” Hand in the OT can refer metaphorically to power, authority, or influence. In Ezekiel God’s hand being on the prophet is regularly associated with communication or a vision from God (3:14, 22; 8:1; 37:1; 40:1).
notes.227: (tn, Heb): “fell upon me there,” that is, God’s influence came over him.

rashi.heb:
*בשנה הששית.* 
לגלות יכניה:
rashi.eng: *in the sixth year.* of the exile of Jeconiah.

notes.228: (tn): The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) indicates becoming aware of something and has been translated here as a verb (so also throughout the chapter).
notes.229: (tc): The MT reads “fire” rather than “man,” the reading of the LXX. The nouns are very similar in Hebrew.
notes.230: (tc): The MT reads “what appeared to be his waist and downwards was fire.” The LXX omits “what appeared to be,” reading “from his waist to below was fire.” Suggesting that “like what appeared to be” belongs before “fire,” D. I. Block (Ezekiel [NICOT], 1:277) points out the resulting poetic symmetry of form with the next line as followed in the translation here.

rashi.heb:
*ממראה מתניו וגו'.* 
אסור להתבונן בפסוק זה:
rashi.eng: *from the appearance of its loins, etc..* It is forbidden to reflect on this verse.

notes.233: (tn): The Hebrew term is normally used as an architectural term in describing the pattern of the tabernacle or temple or a representation of it (see Exod 25:8; 1 Chr 28:11).
notes.235: (map): For the location of Jerusalem see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

rashi.heb:
*בציצית ראשי.* 
בשער ראשי פלוציי"ל בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *by a lock of my hair.* Heb. צִיצִיתרֹאשִּׁי [lit. fringes of my head.] By the hair of my head, flozel in Old French, a lock of hair.

rashi.heb:
*במראות אלהים.* 
הראני כאלו נושא אותי ומביאני לירושלי':
rashi.eng: *in the visions of God.* He showed me [a vision looking] as if He were carrying me and bringing me to Jerusalem.

rashi.heb:
*שער הפנימית הפונה צפונה.* 
שער העזרה שהיא פנימית להר הבית והיו לה שערים לכל רוחותיה:
rashi.eng: *the inner gate that faces north.* The gate to the court, which is within the Temple Mount, [and] which had gates to all its sides.

rashi.heb:
*סמל הקנאה.* 
צורת הקנאה מקנא ומקניט להקב"ה שנתנוה שם להקנאות להקב"ה להרגיזו וכן ת"י צלם דקנאתא דמרגזין:
rashi.eng: *the image of jealousy.* The image of jealousy would make the Holy One, blessed be He, jealous and provoke Him, for they put it there to make the Holy One, blessed be He, jealous; to anger Him, and so did Jonathan render: the image of jealousy, which they provoked.

notes.237: (tn, Heb): “lift your eyes (to) the way of.”

rashi.heb:
*שא נא עיניך דרך צפונה.* 
להר הבית מחוץ לעזרה שהרי בפתח שער הצפוני של עזרה מבחוץ היה עומד ודרך צפונה לשער חוץ לעזרה הוא:
rashi.eng: *“Now lift your eyes northward”.* Toward the Temple Mount, outside the court. For he [already] was standing outside the northern entrance of the court, and north of the gate is [farther] outside the court.

rashi.heb:
*מצפון לשער המזבח.* 
בהר הבית מצפון לאותו שער העזרה הצפוני ואומר אני שהיה אותו שער מכוון כנגד המזבח:
rashi.eng: *from the north of the gate of the altar.* On the Temple Mount, from the north of that northern gate of the court, and I say that that gate was exactly in line with the gate of the altar.

rashi.heb:
*בבאה.* 
כשאדם בא ליכנס לעזרה מוצאו שם, בביאה אלאנטריא"ה בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *at the entrance.* Heb. בַּבִאָה. When a person comes to enter the court, he finds it there; a l’entree in French, at the entrance.

rashi.heb:
*לרחקה מעל מקדשי.* 
כדי שאתרחק מעל מקדשי:
rashi.eng: *to cause Me to distance Myself from My sanctuary.* In order that I distance Myself from My sanctuary.

rashi.heb:
*אל פתח החצר.* 
הקריבני עד פתח אותו שער עצמו:
rashi.eng: *to the entrance of the court.* He brought me up until the entrance of that very gate.

rashi.heb:
*חור אחד בקיר.* 
חומת העזרה:
rashi.eng: *a hole in the wall.* The wall of the court.

rashi.heb:
*חתר נא בקיר.* 
והרחב את החור:
rashi.eng: *dig now in the wall.* and widen the hole.

rashi.heb:
*והנה פתח אחד.* 
דרך החור ראיתי פתח לשכה אחת:
rashi.eng: *and behold an entrance.* Through the hole, I saw the entrance of one chamber.

notes.240: (tn, Heb): “detestable.” The word is often used to describe the figures of foreign gods.
notes.241: (sn): These engravings were prohibited in the Mosaic law (Deut 4:16-18).

rashi.heb:
*שקץ.* 
עשוין לשקוץ עכו"ם:
rashi.eng: *of detestation.* Made for the detestation of idolatry.

rashi.heb:
*מחוקה.* 
חקוקין על הקיר:
rashi.eng: *engraved.* Heb. מְחֻקֶה, engraved on the wall.

notes.242: (sn): Note the contrast between these seventy men who represented Israel and the seventy elders who ate the covenant meal before God, inaugurating the covenant relationship (Exod 24:1, 9).
notes.243: (tn): The Hebrew word occurs only here in the OT.

rashi.heb:
*ויאזניהו בן שפן.* 
חשוב היה ולמדין דורו הימנו לפיכך הקפיד עליו:
rashi.eng: *and Jaazaniah the son of Shaphan.* He was of high esteem, and his generation was learning from him; therefore, He took particular offense at him.

rashi.heb:
*ועתר ענן הקטרת.* 
תמור קטור ענן הקטורת ולשון עתר מרבית וכן העתרתם עלי דבריכ' (לקמן ל"ה) וכן ונעתרות נשיקות שונא (משלי כ"ד) וכן חברו מנחם במחלוקת אחת שלשתן ופירוש ענין מרובה המה אך כל אחד לשון בני אדם:
rashi.eng: *and a thick cloud of incense.* Heb. עֲתַר, thick. The ascent of the smoke of the cloud of the incense [was thick]. The word עַתַר denotes immensity, and so (35:13): “and have magnified (הַעְתַּרְתֶּם) your words against Me,” and so (Prov. 27:6): “whereas kisses of an enemy are burdensome (נַעְתָּרוֹת).” Menachem (p. 140) grouped all three under one heading and they all denote an idea of thickness, but each one is an independent expression.

notes.244: (tn, Heb): “the room of his images.” The adjective “idolatrous” has been supplied in the translation for clarity. This type of image is explicitly prohibited in the Mosaic law (Lev 26:1).

rashi.heb:
*בחדרי משכיתו.* 
משוכה ברצפת אבני שיש לשון ושכתי כפי (שמות ל"ב):
rashi.eng: *in his paved chambers.* Heb. מַשְּׂכִּיתוֹ. Covered with a floor of marble. An expression related to (Exod. 32:22): “and I will cover (וְשֲּׂכֹּתִי) you with My hand.”

notes.245: (tn): Given the context this could be understood as a shock, e.g., idiomatically “Good grief! I saw….”
notes.246: (sn): The worship of Tammuz included the observation of the annual death and descent into the netherworld of the god Dumuzi. The practice was observed by women in the ancient Near East over a period of centuries.

rashi.heb:
*אל פתח שער בית ה'.* 
תוך חלל העזרה אל פתח ההיכל אשר בצפון דאמר מר שני פשפשין היו בבית החליפות אחד בצפון ואחד בדרום:
rashi.eng: *to the entrance of the gate of the house of the Lord.* Within the inner space of the courtyard [that led] to the entrance of the heichal that is in the north, for the master [R. Jose the son] taught: Two wickets were in the Temple chamber for the knives, one in the north and one in the south (see Zev. 55b, 56a).

rashi.heb:
*מבכות את התמוז.* 
דמות א' שמחממו' אותו מבפני' והיו עיניו של עופר' והם נתוכין מחום ההיסק ונראה כאלו בוכה ואומרת תקרובת הוא שואל:
rashi.eng: *making the Tammuz weep.* There was an image that they would heat up from the inside, and its eyes, which were of lead, would melt from the heat of the fire, and it would appear as though it was weeping, and they would say, “It is asking for an offering.”

rashi.heb:
*תמוז.* 
לשון היסק כמו על די חזה למזיה (דניאל ג׳:י״ט) ואתונא אזה יתירה (שם):
rashi.eng: *Tammuz.* “Tammuz” is an expression of heating, like (Dan. 3:19): “more than it was wont to be heated (לְמֵזְיֵהּ);” (ibid. 22), “and the furnace exceedingly hot (אֵזֵהּ).”

rashi.heb:
*מבכות את התמוז.* 
פיישנ"ט פלורי"ר לא"ל קאלפי"ץ בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *Making the Tammuz cry.*  is fesant plorer la chalfez in Old French; making the heated [god] weep.

notes.247: (tn): The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) indicates becoming aware of something.
notes.248: (sn): The priests prayed to God between the porch and the altar on fast days (Joel 2:17). This is the location where Zechariah was murdered (Matt 23:35).
notes.249: (tc): The LXX reads “twenty” instead of twenty-five, perhaps because of the association of the number twenty with the Mesopotamian sun god Shamash. Or “exactly twenty-five.”
notes.251: (tn): Or “the sun god.” The worship of astral entities may have begun during the reign of Manasseh (2 Kgs 21:5).

rashi.heb:
*ויבא אותי אל חצר בית ה' הפנימי'.* 
היא העזרה כי הר הבית נקרא החצר החצונה ועד עכשיו בתוכה היה עומד אלא שהוא נכנס בשע' הצפוני והראהו בבית החליפות את צורת התמוז וחזר והוליכו למזרח לפני ההיכל והמזבח:
rashi.eng: *And He brought me to the inner court of the house of the Lord.* This is the Temple court, for the Temple Mount is called the outer court, and until now that is where he [already] had been standing, except that he had entered the northern gate when He showed him the image of the Tammuz in the chamber of the knives. Then He brought him to the east, [to stand] before the Temple and the altar.

rashi.heb:
*ופניהם קדמה וגו'.* 
ממשמע שנאמר ופניהם קדמה יודע אני שאחוריה' אל ההיכל אלא מגיד שהיה אחוריהם מגולה שהיו פוערין עצמם ומתריזין כלפי מטה:
rashi.eng: *and their faces toward the east.* From the implication of the statement, “and their faces toward the east,” I [already] know that “their backs were toward the Temple,” but [Scripture] tells us that their posteriors were exposed, for they would uncover themselves and excrete downward.

rashi.heb:
*משתחויתם.* 
בשתי תיבות הוא משמש לשון השחתה ולשון השתחויה כן הוא בירושלמי משחיתי' ההיכל ומשתחוי' לחמה וכן ת"י ואינון מתחבלין וסגדין, ומנחם חברו לשון שחוח כמו שחי ונעבור' (ישעי' נ"א):
rashi.eng: *and they were prostrating themselves.* Heb. מִשְּׁתַּחֲוִיתֶם. This serves as two words, an expression of destruction (הַשְּׁחָתָה) and an expression of prostrating oneself (הִשְּׁתַּחֲוָיָה). So it is in Yerushalmi (Suc. 5:5, see Korban Ha’edah): “They were destroying the Temple and bowing to the sun.” Jonathan, too, rendered in that manner: “and they were destroying and bowing.” Menachem (p. 171) classified it as an expression of bending down, like (Isa. 51:23): “Bend down (שְּׁחִי) and let us cross.”

notes.252: (tn): It is not clear what the practice of “holding a branch to the nose” indicates. A possible parallel is the Syrian relief of a king holding a flower to his nose as he worships the stars (ANEP 281). See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 1:145-46. The LXX glosses the expression as “Behold, they are like mockers.”

rashi.heb:
*הנקל לבית יהודה.* 
המעט להם וקל בעיניהם שאר עבירות שבידם:
rashi.eng: *Was it [too] trivial to the house of Judah.* Is it trivial and light in their eyes, the other sins that they have committed?

rashi.heb:
*מעשות את התועבות.* 
אם היו חדלים מעשות את כל התועבות אשר עשו בביתי פה:
rashi.eng: *to prevent them from performing the abominations.* that they should refrain from doing all the abominations that they have done in My house here?

rashi.heb:
*כי מלאו את הארץ חמס.* 
ונקל בעיניהם אותו עון וישובו להכעיסני בתוך ביתי בתועבות האלה:
rashi.eng: *for they have [already] filled the land with violence.* and that that iniquity is trivial in their eyes, and they repeatedly provoke Me within My house with these abominations.

rashi.heb:
*והנם שולחים את הזמורה אל אפם.* 
והנה שולחי' אל חוטמם את ריח רע של זמורה זו שהם מזמרים ברוח היוצא מפי טבעת כלומר בושתם זה אל פניהם ישוב, ומנחם פי' והנם שולחים את הזמורה אל אפם ענין דופי וקלון הוא לפירושו השוה ריח מקטרתם וכעס קרבנם וניחוחים למלאכת דופי נקבים ואחוריהם אל היכל ה' יורה על הענין:
rashi.eng: *and behold they send disgrace into their nose.* Behold they send to their nose the foul odor of this “song,” which they “sing” with the wind emerging from their anus; i.e., this disgrace of theirs will come back to their faces. Menachem (p. 79) explained: “and behold they send the disgrace into their nose” is a matter of disgrace and shame; and according to his explanation, He compares the aroma of their censers and (Ezek. 20:28) “the anger of their sacrifices” and (ibid.) “their pleasant aroma” to the work of the disgrace of the orifices.“Their backs to the Temple of the Lord” implies this idea.

notes.253: (tn): The meaning of the Hebrew term is primarily emotional: “to pity,” which in context implies an action, as in being moved by pity in order to spare them from the horror of their punishment.

notes.254: (tc, Heb): “they approached.” Reading the imperative assumes the same consonantal text but different vowels.

rashi.heb:
*קרבו פקדות העיר.* 
הקריבו את הפקודים אשר הפקדתי לשחת את העיר:
rashi.eng: *Bring near those appointed over the city.* Bring near the appointees whom I appointed to destroy the city.

notes.255: (tn): The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) indicates becoming aware of something and has been translated here as a verb.
notes.256: (sn): The six men plus the scribe would equal seven, which was believed by the Babylonians to be the number of planetary deities.
notes.257: (sn): The upper gate was built by Jotham (2 Kgs 15:35).
notes.258: (tn): Or “a scribe’s inkhorn.” The Hebrew term occurs in the OT only in Ezek 9 and is believed to be an Egyptian loanword.

rashi.heb:
*ששה אנשים.* 
רבותינו פרשום במסכת שבת קצף אף וחימה משחית משבר מכלה:
rashi.eng: *six men.* Our Rabbis explained them in Tractate Shabbath (55a) as Anger, Wrath, Fury, Destroyer, Breaker, Annihilator.

rashi.heb:
*מפצו.* 
שהוא משבר את הכל כמו ונפץ את עולליך (תהילים קל״ז:ט׳):
rashi.eng: *his sledgehammer.* Heb. כְּלִי מַפַּצוֹ, which smashes everything, as in (Ps. 137:9): “and dash (וְנִפֵּץ) your infants.”

rashi.heb:
*וקסת הסופר.* 
פנקס הם לוחות שמחופין בשעוה וחורתין בם בעט:
rashi.eng: *with a scribe’s tablet.* [Synonymous with] פִּנְקַס. These are wax-covered tablets upon which they engrave with a stylus.

rashi.heb:
*אצל מזבח הנחשת.* 
הוא מזבח אבנים שעשה שלמה תחת מזבח הנחוש' שעשה משה במדבר:
rashi.eng: *beside the copper altar.* This was the stone altar erected by Solomon instead of the copper altar that Moses had made in the desert.

rashi.heb:
*מעל הכרוב.* 
מעל הכפרת שהשכינה היתה שורה שם עד הנה והתחילה להסתלק ולצאת לחוץ מעט מעט עשר מסעו' וזה מסע הראשון (עיין עמוס ט פ' א ברש"י וצ"ע יוש"ה) מן הכרוב למפתן בית קדשי הקדשים:
rashi.eng: *from upon the cherub.* which was on the Ark cover, for the Shechinah had been resting there until then, and it began to withdraw and to go outside little by little in ten steps, and this is the first step from the cherub to the threshold of the Holy of Holies.

notes.260: (tn, Heb): “through the midst of the city, through the midst of Jerusalem.” For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
notes.261: (tn): The word translated “mark” is in Hebrew the letter ת (tav). Outside this context the only other occurrence of the word is in Job 31:35. In ancient Hebrew script this letter was written like the letter X. For a similar concept in the Bible, see Rev 7:2-4; 13:16; 14:9, 11; 20:4; 22:4.

rashi.heb:
*והתוית תו.* 
ורשמת רושם:
rashi.eng: *and you shall mark a sign.* You shall mark a sign on the foreheads of the righteous men in order to be for a sign that the destroyers should not strike them.

rashi.heb:
*על מצחות האנשים.* 
הצדיקים כדי להיות לאות שלא יפגעו בם המשחיתים:
rashi.eng: *on the foreheads.* of the righteous men in order to be for a sign that the destroyers should not strike them.

notes.262: (tn, Heb): “to these he said in my ears.”
notes.263: (tn): The meaning of the Hebrew term is primarily emotional: “to pity,” which in context implies an action, as in being moved by pity in order to spare them from the horror of their punishment.

rashi.heb:
*ולאלה אמר באזני.* 
לששת המחבלים:
rashi.eng: *And to these, He said in my ears.* To these six destroyers.

rashi.heb:
*וממקדשי תחלו.* 
מן העומדי' לפני מקדשי ורבותינו אמרו אל תקרי ממקדשי אלא ממקודשי מן המקודשים לי הם אותם חקוקי התיו שהתרה בהם מלהזיקם חזר וצוה לחבלם לפי שאמרה מדת הדין לפניו מה נשתנו אלו מאלו הרי לא מיחו בהם כדאיתא במסכת שבת:
rashi.eng: *and you shall commence from My sanctuary.* From those standing before My sanctuary. Our Rabbis said: Do not read וּמִמִּקְדָשִּׁי, and from My sanctuary, but וּמִמְּקֻדָשַּׁי, and from My sanctified ones, from those sanctified to Me. They are the ones marked with the sign, whom He had warned [them] not to hurt. [Now] He reneged and commanded [the angels] to destroy [even] them because the Divine standard of justice contended before Him, “Why are these different from those? Is it not so that they did not protest?” As is stated in Tractate Shabbath (55a).

rashi.heb:
*ואשאר אני.* 
ונשארתי אני:
rashi.eng: *that I remained.* Heb. וְנֵאשֲּׁאַר, and I remained.

notes.264: (tn): Or “lawlessness” (NAB); “perversity” (NRSV). The Hebrew word occurs only here in the OT, and its meaning is uncertain. The similar phrase in 7:23 has a common word for “violence.”
notes.265: (sn): The saying is virtually identical to that of the elders in Ezek 8:12.

rashi.heb:
*מלאה מטה.* 
דין מעוקל:
rashi.eng: *full of perversion.* Crooked judgments.

notes.266: (tn): The meaning of the Hebrew term is primarily emotional: “to pity,” which in context implies an action, as in being moved by pity in order to spare them from the horror of their punishment.
notes.267: (tn): Heb “their way on their head I have placed.” The same expression occurs in 1 Kgs 8:32; Ezek 11:21; 16:43; 22:31.

notes.268: (tn): The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) indicates becoming aware of something and has been translated here as a verb.

rashi.heb:
*על ראש הכרובים.* 
על ראש ארבעה חיות המרכבה ובפרשה זו חזר לקרותם כרובי' לפי שנהפכו פני השור לפני כרוב כמו שכתוב בפרשה זו, ואמרו רבותינו יחזקאל בקש רחמי' והפכו לכרוב אמר לפניו רבונו של עולם אין קטיגור נעשה סניגור:
rashi.eng: *over the heads of the cherubim.* Over the heads of the four living beings of the Chariot. In this chapter, he switches over to calling them [all] cherubim because the face of the ox was transformed into the face of a cherub, as it is written in this chapter. Our Rabbis said (Chag. 13b): Ezekiel begged for mercy and transformed it to a cherub. He said before Him, “Master of the world, an accuser cannot become a defender.”

notes.270: (tn, Heb): “and he”; the referent (the Lord) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.271: (tn): The Hebrew term often refers to chariot wheels (Isa 28:28; Ezek 23:24; 26:10).
notes.272: (tc): The LXX, Syriac, Vulgate, and Targum mss read plural “cherubim” while the MT is singular here, “cherub.” The plural ending was probably omitted in copying the MT due to the similar beginning of the next word.

rashi.heb:
*בינות לגלגל.* 
בין האופנים כל מקום שנאמ' ויאמר ויאמר אינו אלא לדרוש הקב"ה אמר לגבריאל והוא בקש מן הכרוב לתתם לו כדי שיצטננו הגחלים ותקל הגזירה וכן הוא מפורש בענין וישא ויתן אל חפני לבוש הבדים:
rashi.eng: *between the wheels.* Heb. (בֵּינוֹתלַגַלְגַל) [lit. between the wheel.] Wherever it says, “And he said… and he said,” it is meant only to be expounded upon. The Holy One, blessed be He, told Gabriel [to take the coals], but he [Gabriel] asked the cherub to [take them first and then] give them to him so that the coals would cool and the decree would be mitigated. And this is clearly stated in the chapter (verse 7): “and he picked up [the fire] and gave [it] into the hands of the one clothed in linen.”

rashi.heb:
*וזרוק על העיר.* 
לא זרקם מיד ואע"פ שקבלם לבוש הבדי' לא השליכם עד לאחר שש שנים לקבלתו שנתעממו הגחלים בידו כל שש שנים ותדע שהרי נבואה זו בשנה הששית נאמרה והעיר חרבה בשנת אחת עשרה:
rashi.eng: *and cast [them] upon the city.* He did not cast them immediately, and although the one clothed in linen received them, he did not cast them until six years after he had received them, for the coals were smoldering in his hand for all the six years. And you should know [that this is true] because this prophecy was said in the sixth year, and the city was destroyed in the eleventh year.

rashi.heb:
*מימין לבית.* 
בדרום:
rashi.eng: *at the right of the House.* In the south [of the Temple].

rashi.heb:
*החצר הפנימית.* 
היא העזרה:
rashi.eng: *the inner court.* This is the Temple court.

rashi.heb:
*על מפתן הבית.* 
הוא הסילוק עצמו האמור למעלה:
rashi.eng: *onto the threshold of the House.* That is the very [stage of] evacuation mentioned above (9:3).

notes.274: (tn): The name (“El Shaddai”) has often been translated “God Almighty,” primarily because Jerome translated it omnipotens (“all powerful”) in the Latin Vulgate. There has been much debate over the meaning of the name. For discussion see W. F. Albright, “The Names Shaddai and Abram,” JBL 54 (1935): 173-210; R. Gordis, “The Biblical Root sdy-sd,” JTS 41 (1940): 34-43; and especially T. N. D. Mettinger, In Search of God, 69-72.

rashi.heb:
*עד החצר החיצונה.* 
הר הבית יכול מפני שהקול נמוך ת"ל כקול אל שדי בדברו אלא משהוא מגיע לחצר החיצונה הוא נפסק:
rashi.eng: *until the outer court.* The Temple Mount. I may think that [it was heard no further] because the sound was low. Therefore, Scripture states: “like the voice of God Almighty when He speaks.” Yet, when it would reach the outer court, it would [suddenly] stop.

notes.275: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (the Lord) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.276: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (the man dressed in linen) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

notes.279: (tn): The Hebrew text adds, “from among the cherubim.”

notes.280: (tn): The Hebrew term is normally used as an architectural term in describing the plan or pattern of the tabernacle or temple or a representation of it (see Exod 25:8; 1 Chr 28:11).

notes.281: (tn): The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) indicates becoming aware of something and has been translated here as a verb.
notes.282: (tn): The MT repeats this phrase, a clear case of dittography.
notes.283: (tn, Heb): “Tarshish stone.” The meaning is uncertain. The term has also been translated “topaz” (NEB), “beryl” (KJV, NASB, NRSV), and “chrysolite” (RSV, NIV).

rashi.heb:
*והנה ארבעה אופנים.* 
לפי שנשתנית אחת מן הפנים הוזקק לחזור ולשנות כאן כל מעשה החיות כבראשונה שלא תאמר מרכבה אחרת היא:
rashi.eng: *and behold four wheels.* Since one of the faces was changed, it was necessary to repeat here the entire account of the living beings as at first, so that you should not say that it is another Chariot.

notes.284: (tn): Or “like a wheel at right angles to another wheel.” Some envision concentric wheels here, while others propose “a globe-like structure in which two wheels stand at right angles” (L. C. Allen, Ezekiel [WBC], 1:33-34). See also 1:16.

notes.286: (tn): Many interpreters assume that the human face of each cherub was the one that looked forward.

notes.287: (tc): The phrase “along with their entire bodies” is absent from the LXX and may be a gloss explaining the following words.

rashi.heb:
*וידיהם.* 
של אופנים הם החור שהמרכב' מתגלגל' בתוכן שקורין בויי"ל בלע"ז וי"ת ואשדתהון ושפוכיה':
rashi.eng: *and their hubs.* Heb. וִידֵיהֶם of the wheels. They are the hole in which the [axle of the] chariot turns, called boyol, nave, hub. Jonathan, however, renders: וְאֲשְּׁדַתְהוֹן, and their pourings.

rashi.heb:
*לארבעת'.* 
אופניה' לארבעת אופני החיות:
rashi.eng: *to their four wheels.* To the four wheels of the living beings.

rashi.heb:
*להם קורא הגלגל באזני.* 
אני שמעתי שהמלאך היה קורא את האופן גלגל:
rashi.eng: *to them was called hagalgal to my ears.* I heard that the angel would call the wheel “galgal.”

rashi.heb:
*קורא הגלגל.* 
להם נקרא שם גלגל:
rashi.eng: *was called hagalgal.* to them was called the name “galgal.”

notes.289: (tn, Heb): “each one”; the referent (the cherubim) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.290: (sn): The living creature described here is thus slightly different from the one described in Ezek 1:10, where a bull’s face appeared instead of a cherub’s. Note that some English versions harmonize the two descriptions and read the same here as in 1:10 (cf. NAB, NLT “an ox”; TEV, CEV “a bull”). This may be justified based on v. 22, which states the creatures’ appearance was the same.

rashi.heb:
*פני האחד פני הכרוב.* 
הם היו פני השור שנהפכו לכרוב:
rashi.eng: *the face of one was the face of the cherub.* That was the face of the ox, which was transformed into a cherub.

notes.293: (tn, Heb): “they”; the referent (the cherubim) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.294: (tn, Heb): “they”; the referent (the wheels) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.295: (tn, Heb): “they”; the referent (the wheels) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.298: (tn, Heb): “them”; the referent (the wheels) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*פתח שער בית ה'.* 
פתח ההיכל:
rashi.eng: *at the entrance of the… gate of the House of the Lord.* The entrance of the heichal.

rashi.heb:
*הקדמוני.* 
שבמזרח וזה היה מסע סילוק השני ממפתן בית קדשי הקדשים לעזרה:
rashi.eng: *the eastern.* Heb. הַקַדְמוֹנִי, that is in the east. This was the second stage of the evacuation, from the threshold of the Holy of Holies to the court.

rashi.heb:
*היא החיה.* 
מתוך שראיתי במרכבה זו כל מעשה המרכבה הראשונה אני אומר היא אשר ראיתי בנהר כבר:
rashi.eng: *It was the living being.* Since I saw in this Chariot the entire phenomenon of the first Chariot, I say “[It] is the one I saw by the river Chebar.”

rashi.heb:
*ואדע.* 
כי נהפך פני השור לפני כרוב והיו בה שני פני אדם פנים קטנים של ילד ופנים גדולים של אדם:
rashi.eng: *and I knew.* that the face of the ox was transformed into the face of a cherub, and there were in it two faces of man: a small face of a child and a large face of a man.

notes.303: (sn): The phrase officials of the people occurs in Neh 11:1; 1 Chr 21:2; 2 Chr 24:23.

rashi.heb:
*והנה בפתח השער וגו'.* 
הם הם שאמר למעלה אחוריהם אל היכל ה' אלא שלא פירש שם מי היו וכאן פירש את שמות שנים מהם:
rashi.eng: *and behold at the entrance of the gate [twenty-five men].* They are the very same ones that he mentioned above (ad loc.): “their backs to the Temple of the Lord” except that he did not explain there who they were, and here he delineates the names of two of them.

notes.304: (tn, Heb): “and he”; the referent (the Lord) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

notes.305: (tn): The Hebrew verb may mean “think” in this context. This content of what they say (or think) represents their point of view.
notes.306: (sn): The expression build houses may mean “establish families” (Deut 25:9; Ruth 4:11; Prov 24:27).
notes.307: (tn, Heb): “she” or “it”; the feminine pronoun refers here to Jerusalem.
notes.308: (sn): Jerusalem is also compared to a pot in Ezek 24:3-8. The siege of the city is pictured as heating up the pot.

rashi.heb:
*האומרים לא בקרוב.* 
יבאו דברי הנביאים עלינו:
rashi.eng: *Who say, ‘It is not near’.* that the words of the prophets will come upon us.

rashi.heb:
*בנות בתים.* 
אין לחוש להם אלא בנות בתים ושבת בתוכם כי לא נגלה מן העיר הזאת עד מותנו:
rashi.eng: *build houses.* We need not be concerned with them; rather build houses in which to dwell, for we shall not be exiled from this city until we die.

rashi.heb:
*היא הסיר ואנחנו הבשר.* 
כשם שאין הבשר יוצא מן הסיר עד גמר בישולו כך לא נצא ממנה עד שנמות:
rashi.eng: *it is the pot, and we are the meat.* Just as the meat is not taken out of the pot until it has been completely cooked, neither shall we leave it until we die.

notes.310: (tn): The Hebrew verb commonly means “to say,” but may also mean “to think” (see also v. 3).
notes.311: (tn, Heb): “I know the steps of your spirits.”

rashi.heb:
*כן אמרתם.* 
ידעתי כי זאת אמרתם שירושלים הסיר ואתם הבשר ואני אומר לכם כי לחללים שנתתם בה היא לסיר שהם נגמרו בה אבל לכם לא תהיה לסיר לקלוט אתכם עד יום מיתה כי אתכם אוציא מתוכה:
rashi.eng: *So have you said.* I know that you have said this, that Jerusalem is the pot and you are the meat, but I say to you that for the slain whom you have laid in it, it becomes a pot, for they are finished in it; but for you, it will not become a pot to retain you until the day of death, for you I shall take out of it.

rashi.heb:
*ומעלות רוחכם.* 
העולה על דעתכם בוטר"א טלנ"ט בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *and what enters your mind.* [lit. what goes up in your spirit.] What goes up on your thoughts, votre talant in Old French, your mind [intentions].

notes.315: (tc): Many of the versions read “I will bring you out” (active) rather than “he brought out” (the reading of MT).

rashi.heb:
*הוציא.* 
כמו להוצי' ולשוא בניתם הבתי' כי בגלות תלכו האבות והבנים ואין יורש את הבתים:
rashi.eng: *take out.* Heb. הוֹצִיא, like לְהוֹצִיא to take out. In vain have you built the houses, for you will go into exile, both the fathers and the sons, and no one will inherit the houses.

rashi.heb:
*חרב יראתם.* 
כשפניתם לעזרה למלך מצרים כמו שנאמר בצדקיהו וימרד בו לשלוח מלאכיו למצרי' (לקמן יו):
rashi.eng: *You feared the sword.* when you turned for aid to the king of Egypt, as it is said regarding Zedekiah (17:15): “And he rebelled against him (the king of Babylon) by sending his emissaries to Egypt.”

rashi.heb:
*על גבול ישראל.* 
בסוף הגבול והיא רבלה ארץ חמת היא אנטוכיא שם נשפט צדקיהו ביד נבוכדנצר כמו שנא' בספר (מלכים ב כה) שם שחט את בניו שם נקר את עיניו והיא סוף הגבול שנא' במרגלים ובכמה מקומות עד לבא חמת (במדבר יג):
rashi.eng: *by the border of Israel.* At the end of the boundary; that is Riblah, the land of Hamath, which is Antioch. There Zedekiah was judged by Nebuchadnezzar, as is stated in the Book of (II) Kings (25:6f.). There he slaughtered his sons, there he put out his eyes. And it is the end of the boundary, as is said concerning the spies and in many places (Num. 13:21): “until… coming to Hamath.”

notes.317: (tn): The Hebrew text does not have the negative particle, but it is implied. The negative particle in the previous line does double duty here.

rashi.heb:
*לא תהיה לכם לסיר.* 
המשמרת נתחיה עד גמר בישולם:
rashi.eng: *It will not become a pot for you.* [A pot,] which retains its pieces until they are completely cooked.

rashi.heb:
*ואתם תהיו בתוכה לבשר.* 
שחותכו בתוכה ותשברו בתוכה כבשר בסיר ובתוך קלחת:
rashi.eng: *but you will become in its midst as meat.* for you will be melted in its midst, and you will be broken in its midst as meat in a pot and in a cauldron.

rashi.heb:
*אל גבול ישראל אשפוט אתכם.* 
ולא בתוכה תמותו:
rashi.eng: *by the border of Israel I will judge you.* and not in its midst will you die.

notes.318: (tc): The LXX reads this statement as a question. Compare this to the question in 9:8. It is possible that the interrogative particle has been omitted by haplography. However, an exclamatory statement as in the MT also makes sense and the LXX may have simply tried to harmonize this passage with 9:8.

notes.319: (tc): The MT reads “your brothers, your brothers” either for empahsis (D. I. Block, Ezekiel [NICOT], 1:341, n. 1; 346) or as a result of dittography.
notes.320: (tc): The MT reads גְאֻלָּתֶךָ (g�’ullatekha, “your redemption-men”), referring to the relatives responsible for deliverance in times of hardship (see Lev 25:25-55). The LXX and Syriac read “your fellow exiles,” assuming an underlying Hebrew text of גָלוּתֶךָ (galutekha) or having read the א (aleph) as an internal mater lectionis for holem.
notes.321: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
notes.322: (tc): The MT has an imperative form (“go far!”), but it may be read with different vowels as a perfect verb (“they have gone far”).

rashi.heb:
*אחיך אחיך.* 
גלות שומרון וגלות יכניה:
rashi.eng: *Your brethren, your brethren.* The exile of Samaria and the exile of Jeconiah.

rashi.heb:
*וכל בית ישראל.* 
שהלכו בגולה:
rashi.eng: *and the entire house of Israel.* who have gone into exile.

rashi.heb:
*אשר אמרו להם.* 
אשר אמרו עליהם יושבי ירושלי' שלא גלו עם יכני' שהמליך עליהם נבוכדנצר את צדקיהו ועתה גם הם משחקים על אחיהם שגלו ואומרי' עליהם רחקו מעל ה':
rashi.eng: *to whom… said.* About whom they, the dwellers of Jerusalem who have not been exiled with Jeconiah, over whom Nebuchadnezzar enthroned, Zedekiah said. Now they ridicule their brethren who have been exiled, and say about them, “They have distanced themselves from the Lord.”

notes.323: (tn): Or “have been partially a sanctuary”; others take this as temporal (cf. NASB, NIV, NRSV “a little while”).

rashi.heb:
*למקדש מעט.* 
לבתי כנישתא דאינון יתבין תניין לבית מקדשא:
rashi.eng: *a minor sanctuary.* Synagogues, which are in a position second to the Temple.

notes.324: (tc): The MT reads “you”; many Hebrew mss along with the LXX and other ancient versions read “within them.”

rashi.heb:
*לב בשר.* 
לב רך ונוח להכנע:
rashi.eng: *a heart of flesh.* A heart that is soft and easily submissive.

notes.327: (sn): The expression They will be my people, and I will be their God occurs as a promise to Abraham (Gen 17:8), Moses (Exod 6:7), and the nation (Exod 29:45).

notes.328: (tn, Heb): “their way on their head I have placed.”

rashi.heb:
*ואל לב שקוציהם וגו'.* 
ואותם אשר אל לב שקוץ ותועבות לבם הולך שנשארו בירושלים שלא גלו וטועים בעכו"ם ושקוצי':
rashi.eng: *But to the heart of their detestations, etc..* And as for those whose hearts go to every detestation and abomination, who remained in Jerusalem, who were not exiled, and who go astray after idolatry and detestations.

rashi.heb:
*דרכם בראשם נתתי.* 
שאוציא עליהם חרב ושבי וילכו בגולה:
rashi.eng: *I have placed their way upon their heads.* for I will draw the sword upon them, and [place them in] captivity, and they will go into exile.

rashi.heb:
*וישאו הכרובים.* 
לאחר שגמר דבריו אלי נסתלק:
rashi.eng: *Then the cherubim lifted.* After He finished His words to me, He left.

rashi.heb:
*על ההר אשר מקדם לעיר.* 
הוא הר הזיתים שהוא במזרחו של העיר וזה מסע שלישית:
rashi.eng: *on the mountain that was on the east of the city.* That is the Mount of Olives, which is east of the city, and this is the third stage [of the Shechinah’s departure].

rashi.heb:
*במראה ברוח אלהים.* 
נדמה לי כאלו עכשיו הוא מחזירני מירושלים לבבל:
rashi.eng: *in the vision, with the spirit of God.* It seemed to me as though He now was taking me back from Jerusalem to Babylon.

notes.334: (sn): The book of Ezekiel frequently refers to the Israelites as a rebellious house (Ezek 2:5, 6, 8; 3:9, 26-27; 12:2-3, 9, 25; 17:12; 24:3).
notes.335: (sn): This verse is very similar to Isa 6:9-10.

notes.336: (tn, Heb): “see.” This plays on the uses of “see” in v. 2. They will see his actions with their eyes and perhaps they will “see” with their mind, that is, understand or grasp the point.

rashi.heb:
*כלי גולה.* 
כלי לשתות ומקידה קטנה ללוש בה חררה אות לבית ישראל שבירושלים שיעשו כן ולא יצטרכו ללוש בצק בגומא על גבי קרקע והחצצים נכנסים בתוכו והם לא שמעו לו והוצרכו לכך והוא הכתוב בספר קינות ויגרס בחצץ שני (איכה ג׳:ט״ז) במדרש קינות:
rashi.eng: *implements for exile.* A vessel from which to drink and a small earthen bowl in which to knead a cake, as a sign for the house of Israel in Jerusalem to do likewise, so that they would not have to knead dough in a hole on the ground with the gravel going into it. But they did not heed him, and they had to do just that. This is what is written in the Book of Lamentations (3:16): “Indeed, He made my teeth grind on gravel.” In Midrash Lamentations.

rashi.heb:
*וגלה יומם.* 
מיום אל יום שנים שלשה ימים נהוג בעצמך כאדם המכין צעדיו לגלות שיראו בני הגולה וישאלו מה מעשיך ואתה תגיד להם שסימן הוא לצדקיהו ועמו וישלחו להם אלו את שלוחיהם ויודיעו לאחיהם וקרוביהם אשר שם ככל אשר ישמעו מפיך וכן כל יומם שבמקרא לשון יום יום הוא דבר הנוהג ימים רבים כך שמעתי משמו של רבי מנחם ואמת דבריו:
rashi.eng: *and go into exile day by day.* Heb. יוֹמָם, from day to day, two or three days, behave like a man preparing his steps for exile, so that the people of the exile will see and ask what you are doing, and you shall tell them that it symbolizes Zedekiah and his people [in Jerusalem], and these people will send their messengers and inform their brothers and relatives who are there, according to everything they hear from your mouth. Likewise, every [occurrence of] יוֹמָם in Scripture is an expression denoting “day by day,” something that goes on [continually] for many days. This I heard in the name of Rabbi Menachem, and his words are true.

rashi.heb:
*אולי יראו.* 
שמא יבינו אפרצברונ"ט בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *perhaps they will see.* Perhaps they will understand, apercevront in French, they will realize.

rashi.heb:
*כי בית מרי המה.* 
לפיכך עדיין הוא שמא:
rashi.eng: *for a rebellious house are they.* Therefore, it is still a “perhaps.”

rashi.heb:
*כמוצאי.* 
קומ"א אישוא"ש בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *like the departures of.* Heb. כְּמוֹצָאֵי, come issues, essues in Old French, [comme les issues in modern French] like the departures.

rashi.heb:
*חתר לך בקיר.* 
סימן לצדקיהו שיצא דרך מחתרת מערה כי ירא לצאת דרך בפרהסיא מפני הכשדים:
rashi.eng: *dig for yourself in the wall.* Symbolic of Zedekiah, who [later] went out through a tunnel [leading into] a cave, for he was afraid to go out in the open because of the Chaldeans.

notes.337: (tn): Apart from this context the Hebrew term occurs only in Gen 15:17 in reference to the darkness after sunset. It may mean twilight.

rashi.heb:
*בעלטה תוציא.* 
לכשתחשך תוציא את כליך:
rashi.eng: *in the dark you shall bring [them] out.* When it becomes dark, you shall bring out your implements.

notes.340: (tn): The words “my baggage” are not in the Hebrew text, but are implied from the context.

rashi.heb:
*כלי הוצאתי ככלי גולה יומם.* 
יום יום הייתי מראה להם שאני מתקן לעצמי כלי גולה:
rashi.eng: *I brought out my implements as implements for exile, from day to day.* Every day, I would show them that I was preparing for myself implements for exile.

notes.341: (tc): The nearly incoherent Hebrew reads “The prince is this burden (prophetic oracle?) in Jerusalem.” The Targum, which may only be trying to make sense of a very difficult text, says “Concerning the prince is this oracle,” assuming the addition of a preposition. This would be the only case where Ezekiel uses this term for a prophetic oracle. The LXX reads the word for “burden” as a synonym for leader, as both words are built on the same root (נָשִׂיא, nasi’), but the verse is still incoherent because it is only a phrase with no verb. The current translation assumes that the verb יִשָּׂא (yisa’) from the root נָשִׂיא has dropped out due to homoioteleuton. If indeed the verb has dropped out (the syntax of the verbless clause being the problem), then context clearly suggests that it be a form of נָשִׂיא (see vv. 7 and 12). Placing the verb between the subject and object would result in three consecutive words based on the root נָשִׂיא and an environment conducive to an omission in copying: הַנָּשִׂיא יִשָּׁא הַמַּשָּׂא הַזֶּה (hannasi’ yisha’ hammasa’ hazzeh, “the Prince will raise this burden”). The prince in Jerusalem refers to King Zedekiah. For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
notes.342: (tc): The MT reads “within them.” Possibly a scribe copied this form from the following verse “among them,” but only “within it” makes sense in this context.

rashi.heb:
*הנשיא המשא הזה.* 
על המלך צדקיהו אני מראה המשא הזה לשון נבואה:
rashi.eng: *[Concerning] the prince is this burden.* Concerning King Zedekiah, I am showing this מַשָּׂא, burden, an expression denoting prophecy.

notes.343: (sn): The prince is a reference to Zedekiah.
notes.344: (tn): The words “his belongings” are not in the Hebrew text but are implied.
notes.345: (tc): The MT reads “they”; the LXX and Syriac read “he.”

rashi.heb:
*פניו יכסה.* 
מחמת כלימה שהוא בורח מן העיר לילה:
rashi.eng: *He will cover his face.* because of shame, that he is fleeing from the city at night.

notes.346: (tn): Or “Babylonians” (NCV, NLT). The Chaldeans were a group of people in the country south of Babylon from which Nebuchadnezzar came. The Chaldean dynasty his father established became the name by which the Babylonians are regularly referred to in the book of Jeremiah, while Jeremiah’s contemporary, Ezekiel, uses both terms.
notes.347: (sn): He will not see it. This prediction was fulfilled in 2 Kgs 25:7 and Jer 52:11, which recount how Zedekiah was blinded before being deported to Babylon.
notes.348: (sn): There he will die. This was fulfilled when King Zedekiah died in exile (Jer 52:11).

rashi.heb:
*ופרשתי את רשתי עליו.* 
מערה היתה לו מביתו עד ערבות יריחו ויצא דרך המערה מה עשה הקב"ה הביא צבי אחד לפני חיל כשדי' והולך לפניהם על גג המערה והם רודפים אותו וכשיצא צדקיהו מן המערה בערבות יריחו ראוהו יוצא ותפשוהו:
rashi.eng: *And I shall spread my net over him.* There was a cave [extending] from his house to the plains of Jericho, and he went out through the cave. What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do? He brought before the army of the Chaldeans a deer which was walking before them on the roof of the cave, and they [began] chasing it. And when Zedekiah emerged from the cave in the plains of Jericho, they saw him emerging and caught him.

rashi.heb:
*ואותה לא יראה.* 
כי ברבלה בארץ חמת דבר אתו משפטים ועיור את עיניו ואח"כ הביאו לבבל כמה שנא' בספר (מלכי' ב כה ובירמיה לט):
rashi.eng: *but he will not see it.* because in Riblah in the land of Hamath, he [Nebuchadnezzar] called him to account and blinded his eyes. Afterwards, they brought him to Babylon, as is stated in the Book of (II) Kings (25:7 and in Jer. 39:7).

rashi.heb:
*וכל אגפיו.* 
שריו ומנחם פתר בו לשון כנפים:
rashi.eng: *and all his officers.* Heb. אֲגַפָּיו, his officers, and Menachem (p. 15) interpreted it as an expression of wings (גף).

rashi.heb:
*אזרה לכל רוח.* 
אפנדר"י בלע"ז הם יוחנן בן קרח ושרי החיילי' שגלו למצרי' ושם השיגתם חרבו של נבוכדנצר כשהחריב את מצרי':
rashi.eng: *I will scatter to every direction.* Heb. אֱזָרֶה, epandre in Old French, to disperse, and they are Johanan the son of Kareah and the officers of the armies, who were exiled to Egypt, where the sword of Nebuchadnezzar overtook them when he destroyed Egypt.

rashi.heb:
*למען יספרו את כל תועבותיהם.* 
ויאמרו בעונינו לקינו כי כזאת וכזאת עשינו ואודיע כי לא על חנם כליתים:
rashi.eng: *so that they will tell of all their abominations.* and they will say, “Because of our sins, we have suffered, since such-and-such things we did,” and I shall make known that I had not annihilated you for nothing.

notes.349: (tn): The Hebrew term normally refers to an earthquake (see 1 Kgs 19:11; Amos 1:1).

rashi.heb:
*ממלואה.* 
מעושרה:
rashi.eng: *of its fullness.* Of its wealth.

rashi.heb:
*מחמס כל היושבים בה.* 
בעון חמס יושביה:
rashi.eng: *because of the violence of all who dwell therein.* Because of the iniquity of the violence of its dwellers.

rashi.heb:
*הנושבות.* 
לי"ש אשייא"ש בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *the inhabited.* Heb. הַנוֹשָבוֹת, les assiyes, inhabited.

rashi.heb:
*מה המשל הזה.* 
למה אתם מושלים כן תמיד בפיכם למשול דבר זה:
rashi.eng: *what is this proverb.* Why do you constantly use this proverb with your mouth, to make a proverb of this matter?

rashi.heb:
*יארכו הימים.* 
ולא תבוא הפורעניות ובתוך כך יאבד החזון הרע שהנביאים נבאים לנו וישתכח וישתקע:
rashi.eng: *The days will draw on.* and the retribution will not come, and meanwhile, the evil prophecy that the prophets are prophesying about us will be lost, and it will be forgotten and disappear.

notes.350: (tn, Heb): “the days draw near and the word of every vision (draws near).”

rashi.heb:
*ימשלו.* 
ל' משל:
rashi.eng: *use it as a proverb.* Heb. יִמְשְּׁלוּ, from the word מָשָּׁל, a proverb.

rashi.heb:
*כי לא יהיה עוד כל חזון שוא.* 
לא יוכלו עוד נביאי השקר להבטיח אתכם שלום על שקר כי מהרה אקדים את דברי נביאי האמת לבוא:
rashi.eng: *For there will never again be any false prophecy.* The false prophets will no longer be able to promise you peace with falsehood, for speedily I will bring near the [realization of the] words of the true prophets.

rashi.heb:
*מקסם חלק.* 
דבנייל"א בלע"ז קסם של חלקלקות:
rashi.eng: *glib divination.* Heb. מִקְסַם חָלָק, devinaylle in Old French, soothsaying, divination. Divination of smoothness.

rashi.heb:
*תמשך.* 
שר"א אלונגי"א בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *will be drawn out.* Heb. תִּמָשֵּׁך, sera allongee in French, will be deferred, delayed.

rashi.heb:
*לימים רבים.* 
הנבואה לא תתקיים אלא לזמן מרובה:
rashi.eng: *for many days.* The prophecy will not be fulfilled except after a long time.

notes.351: (tn, Heb): “from their mind.” Who prophesy from their imagination. Note the testimony of Moses in Num 16:28, which contains a similar expression.

rashi.heb:
*הנבלי'.* 
השוטים:
rashi.eng: *mad.* Heb. הַנְבָלִים, madmen.

rashi.heb:
*רוחם.* 
כמו רצונם:
rashi.eng: *their desire.* Heb. רוּחָם [lit. their spirit,] like רְצוֹנָם, their will.

rashi.heb:
*כשועלים בחרבות.* 
כשיבא אדם על פרץ החורבה בורח השועל על דרך פרץ אחרת ואינו עומד בפרץ להלחם:
rashi.eng: *Like foxes in ruins.* When a man comes upon a breach in a ruin, the fox flees through another breach, and it does not stand in the breach to fight.

rashi.heb:
*לא עליתם בפרצות.* 
לא עשיתם מעשים טובים שתוכלו לעכב את הרעה מלבא:
rashi.eng: *You have not gone up into the breaches.* You did not do good deeds so that you could prevent the evil from coming.

notes.352: (sn): The same description of a false prophet is found in Micah 2:11.
notes.353: (sn): The Lord has not sent them. A similar concept is found in Jer 14:14; 23:21.
notes.354: (tn): Or “confirmed”; NIV “to be fulfilled”; TEV “to come true.”

rashi.heb:
*חזו.* 
לשון נבואה:
rashi.eng: *They prophesied.* Heb. חָזוּ, a term for prophecy.

rashi.heb:
*ויחלו לקיים דבר.* 
ואיך סבורים לקיים דבריהם, לשון תוחלת וי"א איקוויירירא"ט בלע"ז, ל' אחר ל' המתנה:
rashi.eng: *and expect their words to be fulfilled.* Heb. וְיִחֲלוּ.“Now how do they expect that their words will be fulfilled?” [The word is] an expression of hope (תּוֹחֶלֶת). Some say that it is ecuydiyant in Old French, and they hoped. [Other editions read: et croiront, and they believed.] Another explanation: An expression of waiting.

notes.355: (tn): The word h!nn@h indicates becoming aware of something and has been translated here as a verb.
notes.356: (tn): Or “I challenge you.” The phrase “I am against you” may be a formula for challenging someone to combat or a duel. See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 1:201-2, and P. Humbert, “Die Herausforderungsformel ‘h!nn#n' ?l?K>,’” ZAW 45 (1933): 101-8.

notes.357: (tn): The Hebrew term may refer to the secret council of the Lord (Jer 23:18; Job 15:8), but here it more likely refers to a human council comprised of civic leaders (Gen 49:6; Jer 6:11; 15:17 Ps 64:3; 111:1).
notes.358: (tn): The reference here is probably to a civil list (as in Ezra 2:16; Neh 7:64) rather than to a “book of life” (Exod 32:32; Isa 4:3; Ps 69:29; Dan 12:1). This registry may have been established at the making of David’s census (2 Sam 24:2, 9).

notes.360: (tn): The Hebrew word only occurs here in the Bible. According to L. C. Allen (Ezekiel [WBC], 1:202-3) it is also used in the Mishnah of a wall of rough stones without mortar. This fits the context here comparing the false prophetic messages to a nice coat of whitewash on a structurally unstable wall.

rashi.heb:
*והוא בונה חיץ.* 
והנה עמי כבונים בנין מחיצה והנביאים טחים אותו תפל קרקע הדומה לסיד ואינו מתקיים לפני הגשמים:
rashi.eng: *and it is building a flimsy wall.* And behold My people are like builders of a partition, and the prophets are plastering with daub-earth similar to lime cement, but which does not resist the rains.

rashi.heb:
*תפל.* 
אוטומנ"ץ בלע"ז וי"א בלאשטניי"א בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *daub.* Heb. תָּפֵל, ajo[s] tamanz in Old French, coating, layer, and others say: plastre, plaster.

notes.362: (sn): A violent wind will break out. God’s judgments are frequently described in storm imagery (Pss 18:7-15; 77:17-18; 83:15; Isa 28:17; 30:30; Jer 23:19; 30:23).

rashi.heb:
*ואתנה.* 
כמו ואתן:
rashi.eng: *then you.* Heb. וְאַתֵּנָה, like וְאֶתֵּן [the second person pronoun in the feminine plural].

rashi.heb:
*אבני אלגביש.* 
אבני ברד גדולות ואומר אני לפי שהם מזהירות ככל אבני גביש (ברד) הוא מדמה אותם אל גביש שהיא אבן טובה כענין שנאמר ראמות וגביש (איוב כ״ח:י״ח) ורבותינו אמרו אל גביש שעמדו באויר על גב איש וזהו משה רבינו שנאמר ומטר לא נתך ארצה (שמות ט׳:ל״ג) אותם שהתחילו לירד לא הגיעו לארץ:
rashi.eng: *gigantic hailstones.* Heb. אַבְנֵי אֶלְגָּבִישּׁ, huge hailstones, and I say that because they shine as do all [crystal] hailstones, he likens them to crystal (גָבִישּׁ), which is a precious stone, as in the way that it is stated (Job 28:18): “Coral and crystal (וְגָבִישּׁ).” Our Sages (Ber. 54b) said: [They are called] אֶלְגָבִישּׁ because they [once] stood in the air over a man עַל גַב אִישּׁ, and this is Moses, our teacher, as it is said (Exod. 9:33): “and rain did not reach the earth” those that started to fall did not reach the earth.

rashi.heb:
*תפולנה.* 
על הקיר:
rashi.eng: *will fall.* on the wall.

rashi.heb:
*איה הטיח.* 
כך כשתבא הרעה יאמר לכם איה השלום שהבטחתם:
rashi.eng: *Where is the plaster.* When the calamity comes, such will be said to you: “Where is the peace that you promised?”

notes.363: (tn): Or “within it,” referring to the city of Jerusalem.

rashi.heb:
*הקיר.* 
היא ירושלים:
rashi.eng: *the wall.* That is Jerusalem.

notes.364: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

notes.367: (sn): The wristbands mentioned here probably represented magic bands or charms. See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 1:413.
notes.368: (tn, Heb): “joints of the hands.” This may include the elbow and shoulder joints.
notes.369: (tn): The Hebrew term occurs in the Bible only here and in v. 21. It has also been understood as a veil or type of head covering. D. I. Block (Ezekiel [NICOT], 1:414) suggests that given the context of magical devices, the expected parallel to the magical arm bands, and the meaning of this Hebrew root (סָפַח [safakh, “to attach” or “join”]), it may refer to headbands or necklaces on which magical amulets were worn.
notes.370: (tn, Heb): “human lives” or “souls” (three times in v. 18 and twice in v. 19).

rashi.heb:
*הוי למתפרות כסתות.* 
קוטרא"ש בלע"ז כמין כסתות קטנות היו תופרות ותולות לנשאלים אליהם על אצילי ידיהם וקוסמות להם באותן כסתות קסם שקרי' ולמי שהם חפצות אומרות קסם טוב ולמי שרוצות אומרות קסם רע:
rashi.eng: *Woe to those who sew cushions.* Heb. לִמְתַפְּרוֹת, coseres(es) in Old French, needle-women; coudre, to sew. They would sew something like small cushions and hang them on the armpits of those consulting them, and they would divine with those cushions with a false divination; and to those whom they wished, they would tell a favorable divination, and to whom they wished, they would tell an unfavorable divination.

rashi.heb:
*אצילי.* 
איישיל"ש בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *armpits.* Heb. אַצִילֵי, aisselles in French.

rashi.heb:
*אצילי ידי.* 
כמו אצילי ידים וכמו תלמי שדי (הושע יא):
rashi.eng: *armpits.* Heb. אַצִילֵי יָדַי, like אַצִילֵי יָדַיִם, as in (Hosea 12:12): “the furrows of the fields (שָׂדָי).”

rashi.heb:
*ועושות המספחות.* 
על ראשי האנשים אף הם לקסום בהם ולא ידעתי מה הם מתוך שנאמר וקרעתי אותם אומר אני שהן של בגד ויונתן תרגמו פת כומרים וכן תרגם במות טלואות מחפיין פת כומרים:
rashi.eng: *and who make the veils.* on the heads of people. They, too, are made to divine with, but I do not know what they are. Since it says (verse 21), “And I shall tear them,” I say that they are of cloth, and Jonathan renders: פַּתכּוּמָרִין, embroidered cloths over the heads of idolatrous statues, and so he renders (16:16): “mounds of striped clothing” בָּמוֹתטְלֻאוֹת covered with פַּתכּוּמָרִין “cloths of idolatrous statues.”

rashi.heb:
*המספחות.* 
כמו ספחני נא (שמואל א ב׳:ל״ו) לישאגמנ"ץ בלע"ז ויש לועזים פלטראיי"ש בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *the veils.* Heb. הָמִּסְפָּחוֹת, like (I Sam. 2:36): “Allow me to join (סָפְחֵנִי).” Faltres in Old French, veils, wraps, coverings.

rashi.heb:
*לצודד נפשות.* 
בהן הן צדות הנפשות לגיהנם שמחזיקות ידי הרשעים לקסום להם שלום ומרפות ידי צדיקים לקסום להם רעה:
rashi.eng: *to ensnare souls.* With them they ensnare souls for Gehinnom, for they encourage the wicked by divining favorably for them, and they discourage the righteous by divining unfavorably for them.

rashi.heb:
*הנפשות תצודדנה וגו'.* 
תמיה היא:
rashi.eng: *Will you ensnare the souls, etc..* This is a rhetorical question.

rashi.heb:
*ונפשות לכנה תחיינה.* 
לכנה כמו לכם שאתנה נוטלות שכר על כך ומתפרנסות בכך:
rashi.eng: *and sustain your own souls.* Heb. לָכֶנָה, like לָכֶן, for you take reward for this and thereby earn a livelihood.

rashi.heb:
*בשעלי שעורים.* 
כמו מי מדד בשעלו מים (ישעיהו מ׳:י״ב) אונגיאלוניא"ש בלע"ז, לשון אחר לשון מדה:
rashi.eng: *for fistfuls of barley.* Heb. בְּשֳּׁעֲלֵי, like (Isa. 40:12): “Who measured water with his fist (בְּשָּׁעֳלוֹ)?” Jaloynes in Old French, double-handfuls. Another explanation: an expression of a measure.

rashi.heb:
*ובפתותי לחם.* 
איאנפיצא"ש בלע"ז שאתן נוטלות בשכרכן:
rashi.eng: *and for morsels of bread.* E an piyezes in Old French, and with morsels, that you take as your fee.

rashi.heb:
*להמית נפשות אשר לא תמותנה.* 
כלומר לאמר על נפשות אשר לא תמותנה אלו ימותו ולאמ' על אשר לא תחיינ' יחיו כי קסמיכם שקר ועמי מקבלים את קסמי כזב שלכם:
