notes.505: (tn): The verbs and persons in this verse are plural whereas the individual has been the subject of the chapter.

rashi.heb:
*שובו והשיבו.* 
שובו אתם והשיבו את אחרים רטורני"ר בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *repent and cause others to repent.* Heb. שּׁוּבוּ וְהָשִּׁיבוּ, you repent and you cause others to repent (tourner, retourner in French), turn [others], return.

notes.507: (sn): In Ezek 11:19, 36:26 the new heart and new spirit are promised as future blessings.

notes.508: (tn, Heb): “the death of the one dying.”

notes.510: (sn): Lions probably refer to Judahite royalty and/or nobility. The lioness appears to symbolize the Davidic dynasty, though some see the referent as Hamutal, the wife of Josiah and mother of Jehoahaz and Zedekiah. Gen 49:9 seems to be the background for Judah being compared to lions.

rashi.heb:
*מה אמך לביא.* 
כמה היתה חשובה אמך אתה צדקיהו שנמשלה ללביאה:
rashi.eng: *How was your mother a lioness!.* How esteemed was your mother, you, Zedekiah that she was compared to a lioness!

rashi.heb:
*בין אריות.* 
שרי יהודה:
rashi.eng: *Among the lions.* The princes of Judah.

rashi.heb:
*ותעל אחד מגוריה.* 
על בני יאשיהו נאמרה קינה זו שראשון הוא יהואחז:
rashi.eng: *And she raised up one of her cubs.* This lamentation was said regarding the sons of Josiah. The first is Jehoahaz.

rashi.heb:
*אדם אכל.* 
גוזל את ישראל כי ישראל נקראו אדם כמו שנאמר (לקמן ל"ד) ואתנה צאני צאן מרעיתי אדם אתם ולפי המשל כל חיה שטעמה טעם בשר אדם מתגרה באנשים לעולם:
rashi.eng: *he devoured men.* Heb. אָדָם. He robbed Israel, for Israel is called אָדָם, man, as is stated (below 34:31): “And you are My flock, the flock of My pasture; you are men,” and according to the allegory, any beast that tasted human flesh will always provoke humans.

notes.512: (sn): The description applies to king Jehoahaz (2 Kgs 23:31-34; Jer 22:10-12).

rashi.heb:
*וישמעו אליו גוים.* 
פרעה מלך מצרים:
rashi.eng: *Nations gathered around him.* Pharaoh the king of Egypt.

rashi.heb:
*בשחתם נתפש.* 
גומין חופרין ומכסין פיהם בקש והחיה נופלת בתוכה:
rashi.eng: *in their pit he was caught.* Heb. בְּשַּׁחְתָם. They dig pits and cover their openings with straw, and the beast falls into them.

rashi.heb:
*חחים.* 
כמין טבעות ברזל נוקבין חוטמו ומושכין אותן בהן:
rashi.eng: *and they brought him with hooks.* A sort of iron ring. They puncture his nose and pull him with them.

notes.513: (sn): The identity of this second lion is unclear; the referent is probably Jehoiakim or Zedekiah. If the lioness is Hamutal, then Zedekiah is the lion described here.

rashi.heb:
*ותרא.* 
אמו כנסת ישראל:
rashi.eng: *Now she saw.* His mother, the congregation of Israel.

rashi.heb:
*כי נוחלה.* 
לשון חולי:
rashi.eng: *that she had taken ill.* Heb. נוֹחַלָה, an expression of illness (חֹלִי).

rashi.heb:
*ותקח אחד מגוריה.* 
יהויקים:
rashi.eng: *and she took one of her cubs.* Jehoiakim.

rashi.heb:
*כפיר שמתהו.* 
מלך כל כפיר שבמקרא ארי בחור וגבור:
rashi.eng: *and made him a young lion.* [i.e.,] a king. Every כְּפִיר in Scripture is a young and mighty lion.

notes.514: (tc): The Hebrew text reads “knew,” but is apparently the result of a ר-ד (dalet-resh) confusion. For a defense of the emendation, see L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 1:284. However, Allen retains the reading “widows” as the object of the verb, which he understands in the sense of “do harm to,” and translates the line: “He did harm to women by making them widows” (p. 282). The line also appears to be lacking a beat for the meter of the poem.
notes.515: (tc): The Hebrew text reads “widows” instead of “strongholds,” apparently due to a confusion of ר (resh) and ל (lamed). L. C. Allen (Ezekiel [WBC], 1:284) favors the traditional text, understanding “widows” in the sense of “women made widows.” D. I. Block, (Ezekiel [NICOT], 1:602) also defends the Hebrew text, arguing that the image is that of a dominant male lion who takes over the pride and by copulating with the females lays claim to his predecessor’s “widows.”

rashi.heb:
*וידע אלמנותיו.* 
מענה את הנשים והורג את בעליהן, ויש פותרין אלמנותיו כמו ארמנותיו וידע לשון פגור והרס כמו וגבוה ממרחק יידע (תהילים קל״ח:ו׳):
rashi.eng: *And he was intimate with their widows.* He would rape the women and kill their husbands. Some interpret אַלְמְנוֹתָיו like אַרְמְנוֹתָיו [their palaces] and וַיֵדַע as an expression of destruction and ruin, as in (Ps. 138:6): “and He chastises (יְיֵדָע) the haughty from afar.”

rashi.heb:
*ועריהם החריב.* 
שנתן מס על הארץ לתת לפרעה בכל שנה כמו שנאמר (מ"ב ג):
rashi.eng: *and their cities he laid waste.* For he levied a tax on the land to give Pharaoh annually, as it is said in II Kings (23:35).

rashi.heb:
*ויתנו עליו גוים סביב ממדינות.* 
וישלח ה' בו את גדודי ארם ואת גדודי כשדים ואת גדודי מואב ואת גדודי בני עמון (שם כ):
rashi.eng: *And nations gathered around against him from provinces.* וַיִתְּנוּ [is rendered by Jonathan as:] and they gathered.

rashi.heb:
*ויתנו עליו גוים.* 
ואיתכנשו:
rashi.eng: *And nations gathered.* וַיִתְּנוּ [is rendered by Jonathan as:] and they gathered.

notes.516: (tn): Or “They put him in a neck stock with hooks.” The noun סּוּגַר (sugar), translated “collar,” occurs only here in the Bible. L. C. Allen and D. I. Block point out a Babylonian cognate that refers to a device for transporting prisoners of war that held them by their necks (D. I. Block, Ezekiel [NICOT], 1:597, n. 35; L. C. Allen, Ezekiel [WBC], 1:284). Based on the Hebrew root, the traditional rendering had been “cage” (cf. ASV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV).
notes.517: (tc): The term in the MT occurs only here and in Eccl 9:12 where it refers to a net for catching fish. The LXX translates this as “prison,” which assumes a confusion of dalet and resh took place in the MT.

rashi.heb:
*בסוגר.* 
ת"י בקולרין:
rashi.eng: *into a collar.* Heb. בַּסוּגַר. Jonathan rendered: into a collar.

rashi.heb:
*במצדות.* 
להיות כלוא שם:
rashi.eng: *into strongholds.* to be imprisoned there.

notes.518: (tc): The Hebrew text reads “in your blood,” but most emend to “in your vineyard,” assuming a ב-כ (beth-kaph) confusion. See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 1:284. Another attractive emendation assumes a faulty word division and yields the reading “like a vine full of tendrils, which/because…”; see D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 1:607, n. 68.

rashi.heb:
*אמך כגפן.* 
עוד זה מן הקינה:
rashi.eng: *Your mother is like a vine.* This is still part of the lamentation.

rashi.heb:
*בדמך.* 
לשון דמיון ומשל כלומר דומה אתה למי שהיתה אמו כגפן שתולה על מים:
rashi.eng: *in your likeness.* Heb. בְּדָמְךָ, a term denoting a likeness and an analogy; i.e., you are like one whose mother was like a vine planted by water.

rashi.heb:
*פוריה.* 
כמו פורה ראש לשון עושה פרי:
rashi.eng: *fruitful.* Heb. פֹּרִיָה, like (Deut. 29:17): “that bears (פּוֹרָה) gall,” [a word meaning:] produces fruit.

rashi.heb:
*ממים רבים.* 
על ידי מים רבים:
rashi.eng: *from many waters.* Through many waters.

notes.519: (tn): The word “fit” does not occur in the Hebrew text.
notes.520: (tn, Heb): “and it was seen by its height and by the abundance of its branches.”

rashi.heb:
*מטות עוז אל שבטי מושלים.* 
שלטונין תקיפין ומלכין גברין:
rashi.eng: *sturdy rods for the scepters of the rulers.* Powerful rulers and mighty kings.

rashi.heb:
*עבותים.* 
אילנות שענפיהן מרובין:
rashi.eng: *over between the interwoven branches.* The trees whose branches were many.

notes.521: (sn): The east wind symbolizes the Babylonians.

rashi.heb:
*ותתש.* 
כל נתישה ונטיעה היא דבר המוטל בפיזור על פני כל הארץ:
rashi.eng: *And it was scattered.* Heb. וַתֻּתֳּשּׁ. Every [expression of] נְתִישָּׁה or נְטִישָּׁה means something that lies scattered upon the face of the whole earth.

rashi.heb:
*ורוח הקדים.* 
נ"נ:
rashi.eng: *and the east wind.* Nebuchadnezzar.

rashi.heb:
*הוביש פריה.* 
שחט את בני צדקיהו:
rashi.eng: *dried up its fruit.* He slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah.

notes.522: (sn): This metaphor depicts the Babylonian exile of the Davidic dynasty.

notes.523: (tn): The verse describes the similar situation recorded in Judg 9:20.

rashi.heb:
*ותצא אש ממטה בדיה.* 
מעון מלכיה ושריה באת לה הרעה:
rashi.eng: *And fire came out of the staff of its sturdy branches.* From the iniquity of its kings and princes, the evil came to it.

rashi.heb:
*קינה היא ותהי לקינה.* 
איליא היא נבואתא ותהא לאיליא:
rashi.eng: *It is a lamentation, and it will be a lamentation.* The prophecy is a lamentation, and it will be a lamentation.

notes.524: (sn): The date would be August 14th, 591 b.c. The seventh year is the seventh year of Jehoiachin’s exile.

rashi.heb:
*לדרוש את ה'.* 
על צרכיהם ואם אינו שומע לנו גם אנו לא נענש על עבירות שבידנו שהרי כבר מכרנו ואין לו עלינו כלום עבד שמכרו רבו ואשה שגרשה בעלה כלום יש לזה על זה כלום ומסוף הענין אתה למד מתשובה שהשיבם והעולה על רוחכם וגו' (לקמן ל"ב):
rashi.eng: *to inquire of the Lord.* concerning their needs, and if He does not listen to us, neither will we be punished for the sins in our hands, for He has already sold us, and He has nothing on us. If a master has sold his slave, or a husband has divorced his wife, does one have anything on the other? And from the conclusion of the matter you learn [this], from the reply that he gave them (verse 32): “What enters your thoughts, etc.”

notes.527: (tn): Or “I will not reveal myself to you.”

rashi.heb:
*אם אדרש לכם.* 
בבקשתכם ובסוף הספר הזה הוא אמר אדרש לבית ישראל זו אחת מן המקומות המלמדים אותנו שהקב"ה חוזר בו על הרעה ועל כיוצא בזה ההוא אמר ולא יעשה (במדבר כ״ג:י״ט) מדרש תנחומא:
rashi.eng: *I will not be inquired of by you!.* in your request. Yet at the end of this Book (36:37): He says: “I will… be inquired of by the house of Israel.” This is one of the places that teach us that the Holy One, blessed be He, recants on evil. And regarding matters similar to this, it is said (Num. 23:19): “He says but He does not do.” Midrash of Rabbi Tanchuma (Vayera 13).

notes.528: (tn, Heb): “will you judge.” Here the imperfect form of the verb is probably used with a desiderative nuance. Addressed to the prophet, “judge” means to warn of or pronounce God’s impending judgment.

rashi.heb:
*התשפוט אותם.* 
לשון ויכוח:
rashi.eng: *Will you contend with them.* Heb. הֲתִישְׁפֹּט, an expression of contending.

rashi.heb:
*ביום בחרי בישראל.* 
הרי שהיתה שנאה זו כבושה לפני המקום קרוב לתשע מאות שנה משהיו במצרי' עד יחזקאל והיתה אהבתו מחפ' עליהם ועל ידי שהיו עתה מרבים לפשוע נתעוררה ועל זה נאמר שנאה תעורר מדנים וגו' (משלי י׳:י״ב):
rashi.eng: *On the day I chose Israel.* This hatred was pent up before the Omnipresent close to nine hundred years from [the days] that they were in Egypt until [those of] Ezekiel, but His love had shielded them. Now that they had increased their transgressions, though, it was awakened, and concerning this it is stated (Prov. 10:12): “Hatred arouses quarrels [but love covers up all transgressions].”

notes.532: (tn, Heb): “I lifted up my hand to them.”
notes.533: (tn): Or “searched out.” The Hebrew word is used to describe the activity of the spies in “spying out” the land of Canaan (Num 13-14); cf. KJV “I had espied for them.”
notes.534: (sn): The phrase “a land flowing with milk and honey,” a figure of speech describing the land’s abundant fertility, occurs in v. 15 as well as Exod 3:8, 17; 13:5; 33:3; Lev 20:24; Num 13:27; Deut 6:3; 11:9; 26:9; 27:3; Josh 5:6; Jer 11:5; 32:23 (see also Deut 1:25; 8:7-9).

notes.535: (tn, Heb): “each one, the detestable things of his eyes, throw away.” The Pentateuch does not refer to the Israelites worshiping idols in Egypt, but Josh 24:14 appears to suggest that they did so.

rashi.heb:
*ואומר אליהם.* 
אהרן ניבא להם נבואה זו קודם שנגלה הקב"ה על משה בסנה וזהו שנאמר (שמואל א ב׳:כ״ז) לעלי הנגלה נגלתי אל בית אביך בהיותם במצרים וגו':
rashi.eng: *And I said to them.* Aaron proclaimed this prophecy to them before the Holy One, blessed be He, revealed Himself to Moses in the thorn bush. This is what was said to Eli (I Sam. 2:27): “Did I appear to the house of your father when they were in Egypt, etc.?”

notes.536: (tn, Heb): “each one, the detestable things of their eyes did not throw away.”
notes.537: (tn, Heb): “and I said/thought to pour out.”

rashi.heb:
*וימרו בי.* 
הם הרשעים רובם של ישראל שמתו בשלשת ימי אפלה כמו שנאמר וחמושים עלו בני ישראל וגו' (שמות יד) אחד מחמשים ויש אומרים אחד מחמש מאות:
rashi.eng: *But they rebelled against Me.* They are the wicked, the majority of Israel, who died in the three days of darkness, as it is said (Exod. 13:18): “and the children of Israel went out of Egypt, (חֲמֻשִּׁים)” one out of fifty, and some say, one out of five hundred.

notes.538: (tn, Heb): “for the sake of my name.”
notes.539: (tn, Heb): “before the eyes of the nations in whose midst they were.”
notes.540: (tn, Heb): “to whom I made myself known before their eyes to bring them out from the land of Egypt.” The translation understands the infinitive construct (“to bring them out”) as indicating manner. God’s deliverance of his people from Egypt was an act of self-revelation in that it displayed his power and his commitment to his promises.

rashi.heb:
*לבלתי החל.* 
שלא יתחלל שמי מאחר שנודעתי להם והבטחתים להוציאם והכירו מצרים שהם עמי אילו הייתי משחיתם היו אומרים אויביהם מבלתי יכולת בידו להוציאם:
rashi.eng: *that it should not be desecrated.* That My Name should not be desecrated; since I became known to them and I promised to take them out, and the Egyptians recognized that they are My people, if I were to destroy them their enemies would say, “Because He has not the ability to take them out.”

notes.541: (sn): The laws were given at Mount Sinai.
notes.544: (tn): The wording and the concept is contained in Lev 18:5 and Deut 30:15-19.

notes.545: (sn): Ezekiel’s contemporary, Jeremiah, also stressed the importance of obedience to the Sabbath law (Jer 17).
notes.546: (tn, Heb): “to become a sign between me and them.”
notes.547: (tn): Or “set them apart.” The last phrase of verse 12 appears to be a citation of Exod 31:13.

rashi.heb:
*להיות לאות.* 
אות גדול הוא להם שנתתי את יום מנוחתי להם למנוחה הרי היכר גדול שקדשתים לי:
rashi.eng: *to be for a sign.* It is a great sign for them, that I gave the day of My resting to them for a resting. Behold this is a phenomenal manifestation that I hallowed them to Myself.

notes.548: (tn, Heb): “and I said/thought to pour out.”
notes.549: (tn, Heb): “to bring them to an end.”

rashi.heb:
*בחוקותי לא הלכו.* 
נסו אותי בעגל וברפידים מלקבל את התורה והותירו מן המן:
rashi.eng: *they walked not in My statutes.* They tested Me with the calf, and in Rephidim [i.e., showing unwillingness] to receive the Torah, and they left over some of the manna.

rashi.heb:
*ואת שבתותי חללו.* 
יצאו מן העם ללקוט מן:
rashi.eng: *and My Sabbaths they desecrated.* Some of the people went out to gather manna.

notes.551: (tn): The words “I did this” are not in the Hebrew text, but are supplied for stylistic reasons. Verses 15-16 are one long sentence in the Hebrew text. The translation divides this sentence into two for stylistic reasons.
notes.552: (tn, Heb): “for after their idols their heart was going.” The use of the active participle (“was going”) in the Hebrew text draws attention to the ongoing nature of their idolatrous behavior.

notes.554: (tn, Heb): “sons,” reflecting the patriarchal idiom of the culture.

notes.557: (tn, Heb): “and they will become a sign between me and you.”

notes.560: (tn, Heb): “and I said/thought to pour out.”

rashi.heb:
*וימרו בי הבנים.* 
שבטו של דן וכן הנצמדים לבעל פעור (מדבר כה) לאחר שמתו דור המדבר:
rashi.eng: *But the children rebelled against Me.* The tribe of Dan, and likewise those who became attached to Baal Peor after the generation of the wilderness had died out.

notes.561: (tn, Heb): “drew my hand back.” This idiom also occurs in Lam 2:8 and Ps 74:11.

notes.563: (sn): Though the Pentateuch does not seem to know of this episode, Ps 106:26-27 may speak of God’s oath to exile the people before they had entered Canaan.

rashi.heb:
*להפיץ אותם.* 
מאז הבטחתים להפיצם כי תוליד בנים ובני בנים וגו' (דברים ד׳:כ״ה):
rashi.eng: *to scatter them.* Back then, I promised them to scatter them (Deut. 4:25ff.): “When you will beget children and children’s children, etc. [the Lord will scatter you among the nations, etc.].”

notes.564: (tn): The words “I did this” are not in the Hebrew text, but are supplied for stylistic reasons. Verses 23-24 are one long sentence in the Hebrew text. The translation divides this sentence into two for stylistic reasons.
notes.565: (tn, Heb): Or “they worshiped” (NCV, TEV, CEV); “their eyes were on” or “were after” (cf. v. 16).

notes.566: (tn): Or “permitted.” The content of the verse is shocking: that God would “give” bad decrees. This probably does not refer to the Mosaic law but to the practices of the Canaanites who were left in the land in order to test Israel. See Judg 2:20-23, the note on “decrees” in v. 25, and the note on “pass through the fire” in v. 26.
notes.567: (tn): The Hebrew term חֻקּוֹת (khuqot; translated “statutes” elsewhere in this chapter) is normally feminine. Here Ezekiel changes the form to masculine: חֻקִּים (khuqim). Further, they are not called “my decrees” as vv. 11 and 13 refer to “my statutes.” The change is a signal that Ezekiel is not talking about the same statutes in vv. 11 and 13, which lead to life.

rashi.heb:
*נתתי להם חוקים לא טובים.* 
מסרתם ביד יצרם להכשל בעוונם וכן ת"י ומסרתינון ביד יצרהון טפשא ואזלו ועבדו גזירן דלא תקנן ונמוסין דלא יתקיימו בהון:
rashi.eng: *statutes that were not good.* I delivered them into the hands of their temptation to stumble over their iniquity, and so did Jonathan render: And I delivered them into the hands of their foolish temptation, and they went and made decrees that were not good, and practices by which they cannot live.

notes.569: (sn): This act is prohibited in Deut 12:29-31 and Jer 7:31; 19:5; 32:35. See also 2 Kgs 21:6; 23:10. This custom indicates that the laws the Israelites were following were the disastrous laws of pagan nations (see Ezek 16:20-21).
notes.570: (sn): God sometimes punishes sin by inciting the sinner to sin even more, as the biblical examples of divine hardening and deceit make clear. See Robert B. Chisholm, Jr., “Divine Hardening in the Old Testament,” BSac 153 (1996): 410-34; idem, “Does God Deceive?” BSac 155 (1998): 11-28. For other instances where the Lord causes individuals to act unwisely or even sinfully as punishment for sin, see 1 Sam 2:25; 2 Sam 17:14; 1 Kgs 12:15; 2 Chr 25:20.

rashi.heb:
*ואטמא אותם במתנותם.* 
אותם מתנות שחקקתי להם לקדש לי כל בכור מסרתים ביד יצרם להעבירם לאותם בכורות למולך הרי חוקים לא טובים:
rashi.eng: *And I defiled them with their gifts.* Those gifts that I legislated for them to hallow for Me every firstborn, I delivered them into the hands of their temptation: to pass those firstborn to the Molech. Hence the statutes that are not good.

rashi.heb:
*למען אשמם.* 
אשימם ואחריב אותם, אשמם לשון שממה והמפרשו לשון אשמה טועה הוא שהאל"ף אינה משרשי התיבה:
rashi.eng: *in order that I lay them desolate.* Heb. אֲשְּׁמֵם. I shall lay them desolate and destroy them. אֲשְּׁמֵם, is an expression of שְּׁמָמָה, desolation. Whoever explains it as an expression of אַשְּׁמָה, guilt, errs, because the ‘aleph’ is not part of the radical.

rashi.heb:
*אשר ידעו.* 
כשאביא עליהם הרעה:
rashi.eng: *that they know.* when I will bring upon them the evil.

rashi.heb:
*עוד זאת.* 
הוסיפו לעשות כשהביאותים אל הארץ:
rashi.eng: *this too.* they continued to do when I brought them into the land.

notes.571: (tn, Heb): “which I lifted up my hand.”

rashi.heb:
*ויקרא שמה במה.* 
לשון גנאי כלומר במה היא נחשבת:
rashi.eng: *So its name was called Bamah.* A pejorative: i.e., of what (בַּמֶה) importance is it?

notes.573: (tn, Heb): “in the way of your fathers.”

rashi.heb:
*הבדרך אבותיכם וגו'.* 
לשון תימה וכי כך הגון שבדרך אבותיכם אתם נטמאים ואני אדרש לכם להשיב על שאלתכם:
rashi.eng: *in the way of your forefathers, etc..* [This is] a rhetorical question. Is this proper, that you should have defiled yourselves in the way of your forefathers, and I should be inquired of by you to reply to your question?

notes.575: (tn): Or “Will I reveal myself to you?”
notes.576: (tn): Or “I will not reveal myself to you.”

rashi.heb:
*ובשאת מתנותיכם.* 
ובלקיחת מתנותיכם שהיה לכם לתת לי ואתם לוקחים אותם ממני להעביר בכורותיכם לעבודת כוכבים:
rashi.eng: *And when you take your gifts.* And with the taking of your gifts that you should have given Me, and you take them from Me to cause your firstborn to pass to idols.

notes.578: (tn): The Hebrew could also read: “Let us be.”
notes.579: (tn, Heb): “serving wood and stone.” This verse echoes the content of 1 Sam 8:20.

rashi.heb:
*והעולה על רוחכם.* 
שעולה על דעתכם:
rashi.eng: *But what enters your mind.* Heb. רוחכם והעלה על- [lit. what ascends upon your spirit], what ascends upon your mind.

rashi.heb:
*נהיה כגוים.* 
נפרוק עולו מעל צוארנו מאחר ששלח מעליו:
rashi.eng: *‘Let us be like the nations’.* Let us break off His yoke from our necks since He sent us away from Him.

rashi.heb:
*היו לא תהיה.* 
כי כבר קבלתם עליכם מדעתכם בימי יהושע כמו שנאמר (יהושע כ״ד:א׳) ויאסוף יהושע את כל שבטי ישראל וכל הענין:
rashi.eng: *shall not come about.* For you already accepted upon yourselves of your own free will in the days of Joshua, as it is written (Josh. 24:1): “And Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel,” and the entire episode.

notes.580: (sn): This phrase occurs frequently in Deuteronomy (Deut 4:34; 5:15; 7:19; 11:2; 26:8).

rashi.heb:
*מדבר העמים.* 
הוא המדבר שהלכו בו ארבעים שנה וכן ניבא (הושע ב) והולכתיה המדבר:
rashi.eng: *the wilderness of the peoples.* That is the wilderness through which they [the children of Israel] traveled for forty years, and so did Hosea prophesy (2:16): “and I will… lead her into the desert.” That is the desert of Sihon and Og. Ezekiel called it the wilderness of the peoples because many nations bordered upon it.

notes.581: (tn): This is the same Hebrew verb used to describe the passing of the children through the fire.
notes.582: (sn): The metaphor may be based in Lev 27:32 (see also Jer 33:13; Matt 25:32-33). A shepherd would count his sheep as they passed beneath his staff.

rashi.heb:
*תחת השבט.* 
שתהיו כפופי' לי ולמוסרי:
rashi.eng: *under the rod.* That you shall be subordinate to Me and to My chastisement.

rashi.heb:
*במסורת הברית.* 
בברי' שמסרתי לכם:
rashi.eng: *into the transmission of the covenant.* The covenant that I transmitted to you.

rashi.heb:
*וברותי.* 
לשון ברירה:
rashi.eng: *And I shall separate.* Heb. וּבָרוֹתִי, an expression of ברד [selecting, separating].

rashi.heb:
*מארץ מגוריהם.* 
מארץ גלותם אוציא אותם ואמיתם במדבר:
rashi.eng: *from the land of their sojournings.* From the land of their exile I shall take them and slay them in the wilderness.

notes.584: (sn): Compare the irony here to Amos 4:4 and Jer 44:25.
notes.585: (tn, Heb): “and after, if you will not listen to me.” The translation leaves out “and after” for smoothness. The text is difficult. M. Greenberg (Ezekiel [AB], 1:374) suggests that it may mean “but afterwards, if you will not listen to me…” with an unspoken threat.
notes.586: (sn): A similar concept may be found in Lev 18:21; 20:3.

rashi.heb:
*לכו עבודו.* 
ואל תראו לאומות שאתם נקראים על שמי בבואכם אל הנביא לשאול לו תורה ומאחר שהוא אומר לכם דברי אינכם שומעים אלי כענין שנאמר (לקמן לג) והנך להם כשיר עגבים וגו' שומעים את דבריך ואינם עושים אותם:
rashi.eng: *go worship.* and do not show the nations that you are called by My Name by coming to the prophet to inquire of him [about the] Torah, and, after he tells you My words, not hearkening to Me, as the matter that is stated (33:32): “And behold you are to them like the song of the flutes, etc.” They hear your words, but they do not carry them out.

rashi.heb:
*במתנותיכם ובגלוליכם.* 
שאתם מפרישים הבכורות בשם בכורה כאשר צויתי אתכם ומשנקרא שמי על הדבר אתם מקריבים אותם לעבודת כוכבים:
rashi.eng: *with your gifts and with your idols.* For you separate the first born to be designated as a firstborn as I commanded you, but once My Name is called upon the thing, you sacrifice them to idols.

rashi.heb:
*משאותיכם.* 
כמו משארותיכם לשון מזון כמו שארה כסותה ועונתה לא יגרע (שמות כא) וכן חברו מנחם:
rashi.eng: *and the first of your food.* Heb. מַשְׂאוֹתֵיכֶם, like מִשְׁאַרוֹתֵיכֶם your kneading troughs, an expression of food, like (Exod. 21:10): “her food (שְּׁאֵרָה), her clothing, or her conjugal rights shall not be diminished.” Menachem also (p. 168) associated it in this manner.

rashi.heb:
*ונקוטותם.* 
לשון קטטה לשון אחר כתרגומו ותידנקון וכן תרגם יונתן הנאנחים דמוני"ר בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *and you will quarrel.* Heb. וּנְקֹטֹתֶם, an expression of quarreling (קְטָטָה). Another explanation, following the Targum: וְתִּידַנְקוּן, and so does Jonathan render (9:4) הַנֶאֱנָחִים: “and those who groan,” demonir in Old French, to melt away.

notes.592: (sn): Beginning with , the verse numbers through in the English Bible differ by five from the verse numbers in the Hebrew text (BHS), with ET = HT, ET = HT, ET = HT etc., through ET = HT. Beginning with the verse numbers in the English Bible and the Hebrew Bible are again the same.

notes.593: (tn, Heb): “set your face toward.” This expression occurs as well in Ezek 6:2; 13:17.
notes.594: (tn): Or “the way toward the south,” or “the way toward Teman.” Teman is in the south and may be a location or the direction.
notes.595: (tn): Or “toward Darom.” Darom may mean the south or a region just north of southern city of Beer Sheba. See M. Greenberg, Ezekiel (AB), 2:417-18.
notes.596: (tn): The Hebrew term can also mean “forest,” but a meaning of uncultivated wasteland fits the Negev region far better. See M. Greenberg, Ezekiel (AB), 2:418.

notes.597: (tn): The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) indicates becoming aware of something and has been translated here as a verb.
notes.598: (tn): Fire also appears as a form of judgment in Ezek 15:4-7; 19:12, 14.

notes.600: (sn): Ezek in the English Bible is in the Hebrew text (BHS). See the note at 20:45.

notes.602: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

rashi.heb:
*דרך תימנה.* 
ארץ ישראל בדרומה של בבל:
rashi.eng: *southward.* The land of Israel is south of Babylon.

rashi.heb:
*אל יער השדה.* 
אל בית מקדשי שעתיד להיות כיער וכשדה להחרש להלך בו שועלים:
rashi.eng: *to the forest of the field in the south.* To My Temple, which is destined to be like a forest and like a field, to be plowed in order to be overrun by foxes.

notes.604: (tn): The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) draws attention to something and has been translated here as a verb.
notes.605: (tn): Or “I challenge you.” The phrase “I am against you” may be a formula for challenging someone to combat or a duel. See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 1:201-2, and P. Humbert, “Die Herausforderungsformel ‘h!nn#n' ?l?K>,’” ZAW 45 (1933): 101-8.
notes.606: (sn): This is the sword of judgment, see Isa 31:8; 34:6; 66:16.
notes.607: (sn): Ezekiel elsewhere pictures the Lord’s judgment as discriminating between the righteous and the wicked (9:4-6; 18:1-20; see as well Pss 1 and 11) and speaks of the preservation of a remnant (3:21; 6:8; 12:16). Perhaps here he exaggerates for rhetorical effect in an effort to subdue any false optimism. See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:25-26; D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 1:669-70; and W. Zimmerli, Ezekiel (Hermeneia), 1:424-25.

rashi.heb:
*ונצרבו.* 
לשון צרבת השחין (ויקרא יג) על שפתיו כאש צרבת (משלי טז) לשון כויה:
rashi.eng: *shall be scorched.* Heb. וְנִצְרְבוּ, an expression related to (Lev. 13:23): “a scar (צָרֶבֶת) from the boil;” (Prov. 16:27), “and on his lips is a kind of searing (צָרֶבֶת) fire,” an expression of a burn.

rashi.heb:
*כל פנים מנגב צפונה.* 
כל האנשים שבדרומה של בבל שהוא בצפון ל' צרב רטרי"יר בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *all faces from the south to the north.* All the people south of Babylon, which is to the north. וְנִצְרְבוּ, shall be scorched, comes from צרב (as Lev. 13:2), retrere in Old French, to shrivel up.

notes.608: (tn, Heb): “all flesh” (also in the following verse).
notes.609: (tn, Heb): “Negev.” The Negev is the south country.

rashi.heb:
*ממשל משלים הוא.* 
כשאני מתנבא להם בלשון משל וחידה כגון יער ואש אוכלת לח ויבש:
rashi.eng: *‘Is he not an inventor of parables’.* when I prophesy to them in language of parable and riddle, such as a forest and a fire consuming [trees] moist and dry.

rashi.heb:
*ויהי דבר ה' אלי לאמר.* 
הנבא להם נבואה מפורשת שאמרתי לך שים פניך דרך תימנה אני מפרש לך שים פניך אל ירושלים:
rashi.eng: *Then the word of the Lord came to me, saying.* Prophesy to them a clear prophecy. What I said to you, “Set your face southward,” I explain to you: “Set your face toward Jerusalem.”

notes.612: (sn): This expression depicts in a very vivid way how they will be overcome with fear. See the note on the same phrase in 7:17.

rashi.heb:
*והטף.* 
והנבא וכן אל תטיפו (מיכה ב) ואל תטיף על בית ישחק (עמוס ז):
rashi.eng: *and prophesy.* Heb. וְהַטֵף, and prophesy. Similarly (Micah 2:6): “Preach (תַטִיפוּ) not;” (Amos 7:16), “and do not prophesy (תַטִיף) concerning the house of Isaac.”

rashi.heb:
*אל מקדשים.* 
הוא יער השדה:
rashi.eng: *about the sanctuaries.* That is the forest of the field.

rashi.heb:
*מקדשים.* 
שני חורבנים:
rashi.eng: *sanctuaries.* “Sanctuaries” denotes the two destructions.

rashi.heb:
*צדיק ורשע.* 
הוא הלח והיבש:
rashi.eng: *righteous and wicked.* That is “the moist and the dry.”

rashi.heb:
*יען אשר הכרתי ממך.* 
וידעתי כי ישמחו העובדי כוכבים לאידכם אקצוף עליהם ואגרה את נבוכדנצר בכולם והוא שכתבתי ונצרבו בה כל פנים הדרומיים:
rashi.eng: *Since I cut off from you.* and I knew that the nations would rejoice at your misfortune, I shall be wroth with them and incite Nebuchadnezzar against all of them, and that is what I wrote, “and all faces from the south will be scorched.”

notes.613: (tn, Heb): “Or shall we rejoice, scepter of my son, it despises every tree.” The translation understands the subject of the verb “despises,” which is a feminine form in the Hebrew text, to be the sword (which is a feminine noun) mentioned just before this. Alternatively, the line may be understood as “let us not rejoice, O tribe of my son; it despises every tree.” The same word in Hebrew may be either “rod,” “scepter,” or “tribe.” The word sometimes translated as “or” or taken as an interrogative particle may be a negative particle. See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 1:672, n. 79. The people of Judah should not place false hope in their king, symbolized by his royal scepter, for God’s judgment (symbolized by fire and then a sword) would destroy every tree (see 20:47), symbolizing the righteous and wicked (see 21:3-4).

notes.614: (sn): This physical action was part of an expression of grief. Cp. Jer. 31:19.

notes.615: (tn, Heb): “For testing (will come) and what if also a scepter, it despises, will not be?” The translation understands the subject of the verb “despises,” which is a feminine form in the Hebrew text, to be the sword (which is a feminine noun) mentioned in the previous verses. The text is very difficult and any rendering is uncertain.

rashi.heb:
*חרב חרב.* 
שתי חרבות חרב מלך בבל ראשונה ואח"כ חרב בני עמון ביד ישמעאל בן נתניה שיהרוג את גדליה ואת הנאספים אליו משארית החרב כמו שמפורש (בירמיהו מ״א:י״א-י״ב):
rashi.eng: *A sword, a sword.* Two swords: the sword of the king of Babylon first, and afterwards the sword of the children of Ammon in the hand of Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, who will slay Gedaliah and those gathered to him of the survivors of the sword, as is delineated in Jeremiah (41:1-10).

rashi.heb:
*מרוטה.* 
פורביא"ה בלע"ז מנחם חברו לשון שליפה וכן ויתן אותה למורטה וכן כולם:
rashi.eng: *furbished.* Heb. מְרוּטָה, forbide in Old French, furbished, polished. Menachem (p. 120), however, associated it as an expression of drawing. Likewise (verse 16): “and He gave it to draw (לְמָרְטָה),” and so all of them.

rashi.heb:
*היה לה ברק.* 
להיות לה ברק זהרורית פלנדור"ש בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *that it may glitter.* Heb. בָּרָק, to have a glitter, a shine, flandours, a flash, flashing (as in Deut 32:41).

rashi.heb:
*או נשיש.* 
לשון תמיה הוא שמא יש לנו לשמוח עוד:
rashi.eng: *Shall we rejoice?.* This is a rhetorical question. Do we have anything more to be happy about?

rashi.heb:
*שבט בני מואסת כל עץ.* 
שבט שאני מכה בה את בני ליסרו קשה מכל השבטים ומואסת היא מכת כל מטה וכל עץ כי אינם אצלה לכלום:
rashi.eng: *The rod for My son disdains every stick.* The rod with which I strike My son to chastise him is the hardest of all rods, and it disdains the blow of every staff and every stick, for they are like nothing to it.

rashi.heb:
*ויתן אותה.* 
את השבט:
rashi.eng: *Then he had it.* the rod.

rashi.heb:
*למרטה לתפש בכף.* 
לצחצחה שתהא נוחה והגונה לתופשה בכף:
rashi.eng: *furbished to grasp in the hand.* To furbish it so that it be easy and fit to grasp with the hand.

rashi.heb:
*היא הוחדה חרב.* 
היא השבט חרב חדה ומרוטה היא לתת אותה ביד נבוכדנצר להרוג בה:
rashi.eng: *that is the sword that was sharpened.* That is the rod; it is a sharp and furbished sword, to give it into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar to slay with it.

rashi.heb:
*והילל.* 
לשון יללה:
rashi.eng: *and wail.* Heb. וְהֵילֵל, a term for wailing (יְלָלָה).

rashi.heb:
*כי היא.* 
החרב תהיה בעמי ובכל נשיאיהם ושריהם:
rashi.eng: *for it.* The sword will be upon My people and upon their princes and officers.

rashi.heb:
*מגורי אל חרב.* 
קבוצות עמים באים לחרב היו סביבות עמי כן ת"י מגורי לשון אוגר בקיץ בן משכיל (משלי י׳:ה׳) אגרה בקציר (משלי ו׳:ח׳) נהרסו ממגורות (יואל א׳:י״ז) העוד הזרע במגורה (חגי ב׳:י״ט) ומנחם חברו לשון יראה כמו ויגר מואב (במדבר כב):
rashi.eng: *those gathered to the sword.* Heb. מְגוּרֵי, a gathering of nations coming to the sword were around My people. So did Jonathan render מְגוּרֵי, related to the word in (Prov. 10:5): “An intelligent son gathers (אוֹגֵר) in the summer;” (ibid. 6:8), “She gathers (אָגְרָה) her food in the harvest;” (Joel 1:17), “garners (מַמְּגֻרוֹת) are demolished;” (Haggai 2:19), “The seed is still in the granary (בַּמְגוּרָה).” Menachem, however, connected it to the word for fear, like (Num. 22:3): “And Moab became terrified (וַיָגָר).”

rashi.heb:
*לכן ספוק אל ירך.* 
לנהי ולקינה:
rashi.eng: *therefore, clap upon your thigh.* as a wailing and a lament.

rashi.heb:
*כי בוחן.* 
כי בוחן רב בצרות שאר פורעניות הרבה נבחנו בהן שפוט ודבר ורעב וחיה:
rashi.eng: *For a test.* For a great test, with torments in many other forms of retribution, they were tested: the rod, pestilence, famine, and wild beasts.

rashi.heb:
*ומה אם גם שבט מואסת לא יהיה.* 
ומה תהי עוד על בני אם גם שבט מואסת זו תבא עליו עם שאר הבחן:
rashi.eng: *and what of it, if there be also a rod that disdains-He will not be.* And what more will be on My son if also this disdainful rod comes upon him with the rest of the test?

rashi.heb:
*לא יהיה.* 
עוד בני בעולם וכן ת"י לא יתקיימון אבל שאר המקרא לא תרגם כך וכן נראה בעיני ושמעתי בו לשונות רבים וראיתי בספרי פתרונות ולא נתיישבו לי והפייט שיסד בחנוכה (בשבת ראשונה ביוצר) המואסת כל עץ הדקיר המזנה מסייעני שקרא את החרב מואסת כל עץ ויונתן כן תרגם או נשיש וגו' על דחדיאו שבטיא דבית יהודה ובנימין לשבטי דישראל כד גלו על דפלחו לטעוותא ותבו אינון למטעי בתר צלמי אעיא אף הוא מפרש או נשיש לשון תמיהא:
rashi.eng: *He will not be.* My son will no longer be in the world. Jonathan also rendered it “they will not exist,” but the rest of the verse he did not render in this [i. e., Rashi’s] way, but so it appears to me. I heard many explanations for it, and I saw [others] in books of interpretations, but they did not appear correct to me, and the ‘payat’ who composed for Chanukah [for the morning of the first Sabbath]: “That which disdained all wood stabbed the adulterer,” supports me, for he called the sword “that which disdained all wood.” Jonathan rendered in this manner: (verse 15) אוֹ נָשִׂישׂ. because the tribe of the house of Judah and Benjamin rejoiced at the tribes of Israel when they were exiled for worshipping idols, and they returned to stray after wooden images. He, too, explains אוֹ נָשִׂישׂ as a rhetorical question.

rashi.heb:
*כי בוחן ומה אם גם שבט מואסת לא יהיה.* 
ארי איתנביאו עליהון נבייא ולא תבו כלומר כבר הדבר בחוץ שלא ישובו ומה יהא בסופיהון:
rashi.eng: *For a test.* and what if also a rod that disdains He will not be [Jonathan renders:] “For the prophets prophesied about them but they did not repent.” That is to say, the matter is already determined that they will not repent. And what will be their end?

rashi.heb:
*אם גם שבט מואסת לא יהיה.* 
אמר ואף שבטיא דבית יהודה ובנימין מגלא יגלון ובעובדיהון בישיא לא יתקיימון מלכות שבט שהיתה מואסת בחבירתה ומלעגת עליהם ועל הרעה הבאה עליהם אף היא לא תהיה ולא תקום, עוד אפרשנו לשון אחר
rashi.eng: *if also a disdainful rod? He will not be.* He [Jonathan] says: “And also the tribes of the house of Judah and Benjamin will be exiled, and with their evil deeds, they not [continue to] exist.” The kingdom of the tribe that disdained its fellow and scorned them and the evil that befell them, she too will not be and will not endure. I shall further interpret it in another manner:

rashi.heb:
*או נשיש וגומר.* 
או שמא נשיש כי תאמר אלי שבט בני מואסת כל עץ מלכי יהודה מואסי עבודת כוכבים הם כמו שמצינו באביה שאמר (דברי הימים ב י״ג:ח׳) ועמכם עגלי הזהב ואסא ויהושפט וחזקיה ויאשיהו שבערו כל עבודת כוכבים שבעולם שתחת ידם ואף אלו ישובו בתשובה.
rashi.eng: *Or shall we rejoice, etc..* Or perhaps we should rejoice, for you say to Me that the tribe of My son disdains all wood: The kings of Judah disdain idolatry, as we find with Abijah, who said (II Chron. 13:8): “and with you are the golden calves,” and Asa, Jehoshaphat, Hezekiah, and Josiah, who abolished all the idolatry in the world that was under their control, and these [the remaining tribes] too will repent.

rashi.heb:
*זעק והילל.* 
ואל תשיש על זאת כי היא תהיה בעמי ולמה:
rashi.eng: *Cry and wail.* and do not rejoice over this, for it will be upon My people. And why?

rashi.heb:
*כי בוחן.* 
כבר בוחן הדבר לפני שלא ישובו תשובה הוגנת:
rashi.eng: *Because it is tested.* The matter is already tested and determined before Me that they will not repent properly.

rashi.heb:
*ומה אם גם שבט מואסת לא יהיה.* 
ומה אמתין עוד אפילו אם באו לשוב ולמאוס בעבודת כוכבים לא יתקיים הדבר בידם כי ימהרו לשוב לרשעתם והוא שאמר לירמיה אם ישוב לא ישוב:
rashi.eng: *And what if even they disdain wood, it will not be.* And what if I wait longer? Even if they came to repent and to disdain idolatry, the matter would not last with them because they would hasten to revert to their wickedness. That is what is said in Jeremiah (8:4): “if he repents, will he not return?”

rashi.heb:
*הנבא והך כף אל כף.* 
כדרך הסופדים ומה היא הנבואה:
rashi.eng: *prophesy and clap your hands one upon the other.* in the manner of those who lament, and what is the prophecy?

rashi.heb:
*ותכפל חרב שלישתה.* 
אני אמרתי חרב חרב חרבו של נבוכדנצר להחריב ירושלים וחרב בני עמון בגדליה עוד יש חרב של שלישית כפולה כי שתיהן הללו חרב חללים תהיה והיא חרב החלל הגדול המפלת חללי' רבים:
rashi.eng: *and a third sword shall be doubled.* I said, “A sword, a sword;” Nebuchadnezzar’s sword to destroy Jerusalem and the sword of the children of Ammon upon Gedaliah. There is yet a third sword, doubled as much as these two, and it shall be a sword of the slain; that is the sword of the great slaughter, which causes many slain to fall.

rashi.heb:
*החודרת להם.* 
בכל אשר תצאו תרדוף אתכם בחדרי חדרים הרי יוחנן בן קרח ושרי החיילים ילכו למצרים שם תשיגם חרב וכן בכל המקומות אשר ימלטו מהם אל ערים בצורות כמו שאמור בענין על כל שעריהם נתתי אבחת חרב:
rashi.eng: *which penetrates to them.* Wherever you go out, it will pursue you into the innermost chambers. Behold, Johanan the son of Kareah and the generals of the armies will go to Egypt; there the sword will overtake them, and so in all the place from which they will flee, to the fortified cities, as it is stated in this piece: “by all your cities I gave the scream of the sword.”

notes.618: (tc): The MT reads “Judah in fortified Jerusalem,” a geographic impossibility. The translation follows the LXX, which assumes בְּתוֹכָהּ (b�tokhah, “in it”) for בְּצוּרָה (b�tsurah, “fortified”).� As the Babylonians approached from the north, one road would branch off to the left and lead down the east side of the Jordan River to Ammon. The other road would veer to the right and lead down west of the Jordan to Jerusalem.

rashi.heb:
*למוג.* 
לשון הנעה לשון אחר לשון דבר נמס:
rashi.eng: *In order to melt.* Heb. לָמוּג, an expression of moving. Another explanation: an expression of something melting.

rashi.heb:
*והרבה המכשולים.* 
והרבות המכשולים וכן כל הרבה שבמקרא לשון הרבות הוא לשון פעול:
rashi.eng: *and to increase the stumbling blocks.* Heb. וְהַרְבֵּה, and to increase the stumbling blocks, and so every הַרְבֵּה in Scripture is an expression of increasing, an infinitive.

rashi.heb:
*אבחת חרב.* 
יש פותרין טבחת טי"ת תחת אל"ף בא"ט ב"ח ויש פותרין כמו אבעת לשון בעתה ולא יתכן כי התיו באבחת אינה יסוד ולא באה אלא לסמיכה והתי"ו בבעתה מן היסוד ואני אומר אבחת חרב השמעת קול הרוגי חרב לשון נביחה גלאפ"י שמינ"ט בלע"ז כי נו"ן בנביחה יסוד נופל הוא כמו נו"ן בנשיכה ותבא אל"ף במקומה כמו (איוב י״ג:י״ז) ואחותי באזניכם אסוך שמן (מלכים ב יד) ומנחם פירש כמו אימת חרב ואין לו דמיון אלא פתרונו לפי עניינו:
rashi.eng: *the scream of the sword.* Heb. אִבְחֳת. Some interpret [this as] טִבְחַת, the slaughter of, the ‘teth’ in place of the ‘aleph,’ by the code of א -ט ב ח [whereby ‘aleph’ is interchangeable with ‘teth,’ ‘beth’ with ‘cheth,’ etc.] [This appears to be Jonathan’s interpretation.] Others interpret it as אִבְעַת an expression of בְּעָתָה [fright], but this cannot be because the ‘tav’ in אִבְחֳת is not part of the radical, and it comes only for the construct state, whereas the ‘tav’ in בְּעָתָה is a radical. Therefore, I say that אִבְחֳתחֶרֶב means the sounding of the voice of those slain by the sword, an expression of barking (נְבִיחָה) glapissement in French, yelping, for the ‘nun’ in נְבִיחָה is a defective radical, like the ‘nun’ in נְשִּׁיכָה biting, and the ‘aleph’ comes in its place, like (Job 13:17): “and… my speech (אַחְוָתִי) in your ears;” (II Kings 4:2), “except a jug (אָסוּךְ) of oil.” Menachem (p. 12) explained it as fear of the sword. It has no counterpart, but is interpreted according to the context.

rashi.heb:
*אח עשויה לברק.* 
אוי ואח כי עשויה היא ללהט מרוטה ומוברקת:
rashi.eng: *Woe, it is made to glitter.* Alas and alack! For it is made into a furbished and polished blade.

rashi.heb:
*מעטה לטבח.* 
ועטויה בשמלה עד תתפש בכף לטבח ביום המלחמ' ויש פותרין מעטה על ל' מיעוט שמתמעטת כשמשננין אותה וטעות הוא בידם כי חסרון הוי"ו ודגשות הטי"ת יורה עליה כי אין המ"ם שורש בתיבה כמ"ם של מעונה ומשונה ומעוט' ומעולפת ספירי' (שיר ה) ומנחם חבר מעטה לשון מחשבה כמו (דניאל ב׳:י״ד) התיב עיטה וטעם אבל דונש פתר אותו כמו עוטה אור כשלמ' (תהילים ק״ד:ב׳):
rashi.eng: *enwrapped for the slaughter.* And enwrapped in a cloth until it would be grasped in the hand for slaughter on the day of war. Some interpret מְעֻטָה as a form of the word for diminishing (מִעוּט), for it diminishes when they sharpen it, but it is an error that they have made, for the absence of the ‘vav’ and the ‘dagesh’ in the ‘teth’ indicate about it that the ‘mem’ is not a radical, [but,] like the ‘mem’ of מְעֻנָה, afflicted, מְעֻטָה, enwrapped, and (Songs 5:14) מְעֻלֶפֶת, “overlaid with sapphires.” Menachem (p. 132) associated it as an expression of thought, like (Dan. 2:14): “answered with counsel (עֵטָא) and discretion.” Dunash, however, interprets it (p. 78) like (Ps. 104:2): “[You] enwrap (עֹטֶה) Yourself with light like a garment.”

notes.620: (sn): Mesopotamian kings believed that the gods revealed the future through omens. They employed various divination techniques, some of which are included in the list that follows. A particularly popular technique was the examination and interpretation of the livers of animals. See R. R. Wilson, Prophecy and Society in Ancient Israel, 90-110.
notes.621: (tn): This word refers to personal idols that were apparently used for divination purposes (Gen 31:19; 1 Sam 19:13, 16).

rashi.heb:
*התאחדי.* 
אל מקום אחד או לימין או לשמאל:
rashi.eng: *Get yourself to one side.* To one place, either to the right or to the left.

rashi.heb:
*מועדות.* 
מזומנות:
rashi.eng: *directed.* Heb. מֻעָדוֹת, prepared.

notes.624: (tn): Or “on the right side,” i.e., the omen mark on the right side of the liver.
notes.625: (tn, Heb): “to open the mouth” for slaughter.
notes.626: (tn, Heb): “to raise up a voice in a battle cry.”

rashi.heb:
*וגם אני אכה כפי אל כפי.* 
אני אומר לך הכה כף אל כף וגם אני כמוך מקונן עליהם ואכה כפי אל כפי אך חמתי בוערת בי והניחותי אותה:
rashi.eng: *I, too, shall clap My hands.* I say to you, “Clap your hands one upon the other,” and “I, too,” like you, lament over them, and I “shall clap My hands” one upon the other, but My fury burns within Me, “and I shall give it rest.”

notes.627: (tn, Heb): “they”; the referent (the people in Jerusalem) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.628: (sn): When the people of Judah realized the Babylonians’ intentions, they would object on grounds that they had made a treaty with the Babylonian king (see 17:13).
notes.629: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (the king of Babylon) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.631: (tn, Heb): “and he will remind of guilt for the purpose of being captured.” The king would counter their objections by pointing out that they had violated their treaty with him (see 17:18).

notes.633: (tn, Heb): “Because you have brought to remembrance your guilt when your transgressions are uncovered so that your sins are revealed in all your deeds – because you are remembered, by the hand you will be seized.”

rashi.heb:
*שים לך שנים דרכים.* 
כמו שהוא מסיים המקרא:
rashi.eng: *make for yourself two roads.* as He concludes the [next] verse.

rashi.heb:
*ויד ברא בראש דרך עיר.* 
פנה לך מקום בראש דרך שאתה בה עשה לך כמין דרך מפוצלת לפרשת דרכים אחד פונה לימין ואחד פונה לשמאל:
rashi.eng: *and clear a place; at the head of the road to the city.* Clear for yourself a place at the head of the road you are on, and make for yourself a sort of road opening into the crossroads, one facing right and one facing left.

rashi.heb:
*יצאו שניהם.* 
שני הדרכים:
rashi.eng: *both of them will emanate.* The two roads.

rashi.heb:
*ויד ברא.* 
מקום פנוי מן הקוצים והברקני' אישרטי"ר בלע"ז ודוגמתו בספר יהושע (יז) עלה לך היערה ובראת לך שמה ועוד כי הר יהיה לך כי יער הוא ובראת (שם) ומנחם חברם כולם לשון ברירה כמו ברו לכם איש (שמואל א י״ז:ח׳) ברא לישנ"ט בלעז:
rashi.eng: *and clear a place.* A place cleared of the thorns and the thistles; [בָּרִא is like] essarter in French, to clear. A word similar to it appears in the Book of Joshua (17:15): “then go up to the forest, and clear it (וּבֵרֵאתָ) for yourself there.” Again (ibid. verse 18): “But the mountain shall be yours, for it is a forest, and you shall cut it down (וּבֵרֵאתוֹ).” Menachem connected them all (p. 48) as an expression of choosing, like (I Sam. 17:8): “Choose (בְּרוּ) for yourselves a man”; בָּרֵא meaning lisant in Old French, choosing, appointing.

notes.634: (tn): This probably refers to King Zedekiah.

rashi.heb:
*דרך תשים לבוא וגו'.* 
סי' שתי דרכים הללו למלך בבל היוצא מארצו על מנת לילך או לירושלים או לרבת בני עמון לאיזה משתיהן שיפול לו גורל בקסמיו עליה כמו שמפורש כי עמד מלך בבל וגו':
rashi.eng: *You shall make a road for the coming, etc..* These two roads symbolize the king of Babylon, who is leaving his country with the intention of going either to Jerusalem or to Rabbah of the children of Ammon. To whichever of the two of them the lot will fall for him by his divinations, he will march, as is delineated (verse 26): “For the king of Babylon stood, etc.”

notes.635: (tn): Elsewhere in the Bible the turban is worn by priests (Exod 28:4, 37, 39; 29:6; 39:28, 31; Lev 8:9; 16:4), but here a royal crown is in view.

rashi.heb:
*אם הדרך.* 
קארפו"ר בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *the crossroads.* Heb. אֵם הַדֶרֶךְ, carrefour in French, crossroads.

rashi.heb:
*קלקל בחצים.* 
ליהט בלהט חצים זרק חץ כלפי מעלה והיא פונה מאיליה לימין או לשמאל ולמקום שהיא פונה הוא הגורל:
rashi.eng: *he furbished the arrows.* Heb. קִלְקַל, he furbished the arrows with a glitter. He shot an arrow upward, and it turns by itself right or left, and to the place it turns, that is the lot.

rashi.heb:
*קלקל בחצים.* 
חברו מנחם עם נחשת קלל (לעיל א) והוא לא פנים קלקל (קהלת י) ויש משמע קלקל לשון קלקול כמו (ירמיה ד) וכל הגבעות התקלקלו ויש לועזים קלקל טראאי"ט בלע"ז וכן ת"י קלקל קשת בחצים בגירריא:
rashi.eng: *he flashed with the arrows.* Menachem (p. 155), connected it with (above 1:7): “burnished (קָלָל) copper;” (Ecc. 10:10): “and he did not sharpen (קִלְקֵל) the edge.” It may also be explained as an expression of deterioration, as in (Jer. 4:24): “and all the hills deteriorated (הִתְקַלְקָלוּ).” Some translate קִלְקַל into French, as trait, he shot, and Jonathan as well renders קִלְקַל בֲּחִצִים as קְשֲּׁתבְּגִרְרֲיָא.

rashi.heb:
*שאל בתרפים.* 
דמות שמדבר במכשפות ויש שעה שמכוונת שאם עושהו באותה שעה יש בו דבור לעולם:
rashi.eng: *he inquired of the teraphim.* An image that talks through magic, and there is a set time, that if one makes it at that time, it possesses speech forever.

rashi.heb:
*ראה בכבד.* 
יש בקיאים קוסמים בכבד:
rashi.eng: *looked into the liver.* There are some experts who divine with liver.

notes.638: (tn, Heb): “A ruin, a ruin, a ruin I will make it.” The threefold repetition of the noun “ruin” is for emphasis and draws attention to the degree of ruin that would take place. See IBHS 233 �12.5a and GKC 431-32 �133.k. The pronominal suffix (translated “it”) on the verb “make” is feminine in Hebrew. The probable antecedent is the “turban/crown” (both nouns are feminine in form) mentioned in verse 26. The point is that the king’s royal splendor would be completely devastated as judgment overtook his realm and brought his reign to a violent end.
notes.639: (tn, Heb): “Also this, he was not, until the coming of the one to whom the judgment belongs and I have given it.” The Hebrew text, as it stands, is grammatically difficult. The pronoun “this” is feminine, while the following negated verb (“was not”) is masculine. Some emend the verb to a feminine form (see BHS). In this case the statement refers to the destiny of the king’s turban/crown (symbolizing his reign). See the previous note. The preposition translated “when” normally means “until,” but here it seems to refer to the period during which the preceding situation is realized, rather than its termination point. See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:19, 21. The second part of the statement, though awkward, probably refers to the arrival of the Babylonian king, to whom the Lord had assigned the task of judgment (see 23:24). Or the verse may read “A total ruin I will make, even this. It will not be until the one comes to whom is (the task of) judgment and I have assigned it.”

rashi.heb:
*בימינו היה הקסם ירושלים.* 
כל גורלותיו קסמו לו לבא ירושלים:
rashi.eng: *At his right was the divination to Jerusalem.* All his lots gave divinistic indication to come to Jerusalem.

rashi.heb:
*לשום כרים.* 
שלטונים ממונים ראשי גייסות:
rashi.eng: *to appoint officers.* Heb. כָּרִים, appointed officers, heads of troops.

rashi.heb:
*לשום כרים על שערים.* 
אתה וגייס שלך שב על שער פלוני:
rashi.eng: *to station officers over the gates.* You and your troop, take position by such-and-such a gate.

rashi.heb:
*לשפוך סוללה.* 
שופכין עפר וסוללין וצוברין תל גבוה וכובשין אותה כעין שכובשים תלי המגדלים לעמוד עליו ולהלחם בבני העיר:
rashi.eng: *to pour a siege mound.* They pour earth and tread it down and pile up a high mound and press it down, in a fashion similar to the way they press down the mound of the towers, to stand on it and to wage war against the people of the city.

notes.641: (tn, Heb): “to contain, endure.” Since the Hebrew text as it stands makes little, if any, sense, most emend the text to read either “to consume” or “for destruction.” For discussion of options see D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 1:693.

rashi.heb:
*והיה להם.* 
לישראל מה שעשה נבוכדנצר:
rashi.eng: *And it was to them.* To Israel, what Nebuchadnezzar did.

rashi.heb:
*כקסם שוא.* 
ולא יאמינו שיצליח אך באמת שבועי שבועות להם ארבעים ותשע פעמים קסם להם נבוכדנצר וכל הקסמים כוונו זה כזה:
rashi.eng: *like a false divination.* and they will not believe that he would succeed, but indeed, they had seven sevens. Nebuchadnezzar divined forty-nine times, and all the divinations coincided exactly.

rashi.heb:
*והוא מזכיר עון להתפש.* 
נבוכדנצר בקסמו את קסמיו היה מזכיר עוונות שביד ישראל שהיו מודיעים לו עמון ומואב שכניהם שהיו שומעין את תוכחות הנביאים:
rashi.eng: *and he brings iniquity to be remembered in order that they be seized.* And Nebuchadnezzar, in his divinations, would cause the iniquities that Israel committed to be remembered, for Ammon and Moab, their neighbors, would make them known to him because they would hear the reproofs of the prophets.

rashi.heb:
*להתפש.* 
שיהיו ישראל נתפשים בידו:
rashi.eng: *in order that they be seized.* [lit. to be seized.] That Israel be seized in his hand.

notes.642: (tn, Heb): “in the seeing concerning you falsehood, in divining concerning you a lie.” This probably refers to the attempts of the Ammonites to ward off judgment through prophetic visions and divination.
notes.643: (tn, Heb): “you”; the referent (the sword mentioned in v. 28) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.644: (sn): The second half of the verse appears to state that the sword of judgment would fall upon the wicked, despite their efforts to prevent it.

rashi.heb:
*יען הזכרכם עונכם.* 
שאתם מחדשין עבירות מיום אל יום ועונותיכם הראשונים נזכרים על ידיהם:
rashi.eng: *Because you have made your iniquity to be remembered.* For you commit new transgressions daily, and your earlier iniquities are remembered through them.

rashi.heb:
*בהגלות פשעיכם.* 
החדשים:
rashi.eng: *in that your transgressions are revealed.* [i.e.,] the new ones.

rashi.heb:
*להראות חטאתיכם.* 
הישנים:
rashi.eng: *so that your sins appear.* [i.e.,] the old ones.

rashi.heb:
*יען הזכרכם.* 
לפני לרעה לפיכך:
rashi.eng: *because of your being remembered.* before Me for evil, therefore…

rashi.heb:
*בכף תתפשו.* 
ביד מלכא דבבל תתמסרון:
rashi.eng: *you shall be seized in the hand.* You shall be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon.

notes.645: (sn): Once the Babylonian king’s sword (vv. 19-20) has carried out its assigned task, the Lord commands it to halt and announces that Babylon itself will also experience his judgment. See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:28.
notes.646: (tn): In the Hebrew text of vv. 30-32 the second person verbal and pronominal forms are feminine singular. This may indicate that the personified Babylonian sword is being addressed. The Hebrew word for “sword” (see v. 28) is feminine. However, it may refer to the Ammonites.

rashi.heb:
*חלל רשע.* 
חייב להיות חלל ברשעך:
rashi.eng: *wicked man, sentenced to be slain.* Liable to be slain for your wickedness.

rashi.heb:
*נשיא ישראל.* 
צדקיהו:
rashi.eng: *prince of Israel.* Zedekiah.

rashi.heb:
*בעת עון קץ.* 
בעת נתמלאת הסאה והגיע העון האחרון הממלא את הסאה:
rashi.eng: *at the time of the final iniquity.* At the time the measure has become filled and the final iniquity, which fills the measure, has arrived.

rashi.heb:
*הסיר המצנפת וגו'.* 
כתרגומו אעדי מצנפתא משריה כהנא רבא ואבטל כתרא מצדקיה מלכא אמר דין ודין באתריה לא יתקיים:
rashi.eng: *I shall remove the turban and lift off the crown, etc..* This is to be explained as the Targum renders: I shall remove the turban from Seraiah the High Priest, and I shall abolish the crown from King Zedekiah. He said: Neither this nor that will remain in its place.

rashi.heb:
*הגבה וגו'.* 
גדליה בר אחיקם דלאו הוה דיליה יסבונה וצדקיהו דדיליה היא תעדי מיניה:
rashi.eng: *the humble will be uplifted.* Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, to whom it did not belong, will take it, and Zedekiah, to whom it did belong, it will be taken from him.

notes.647: (tn, Heb): “your blood will be in the middle of the land.”

rashi.heb:
*עוה עוה.* 
לשון עי השדה לשון חורבה אחר חורבה פעמים ושלש אשימנה כבר ניטלה מיכניה ונתנה לצדקיה ומצדקיה תנתן לגדליה הרי שתי' ומנחם חבר עוה עם עותה ושתי המלכה (אסתר א׳:ט״ז) העוינו והרשענו (תהלים קו):
rashi.eng: *A ruin, a ruin.* Heb. עַוָה, an expression of (Micah 1:6): “a heap (עִי) in the field,” an expression of ruin after ruin, two and three times, I shall make it: It was already taken from Jeconiah and given to Zedekiah, and from Zedekiah it will be given to Gedaliah; this makes twice. Menachem (p. 131) connected עַוָה with (Esther 1:16): “has Vashti the queen done wrong (עָוְתָה)?;” (Ps. 106:5), “we have committed iniquity (הֶעֱוִינוּ) and wickedness.”

rashi.heb:
*גם זאת לא היה.* 
גם לגדליה לא תתקיים עד בא ישמעאל בן נתניה:
rashi.eng: *this too will not be.* Also, to Gedaliah it will not remain, [only] until Ishmael the son of Nethaniah [the assassin] comes.

rashi.heb:
*אשר לו המשפט.* 
אשר עליו שמתי להפרע נקמתי ומשפטי:
rashi.eng: *until he who has the judgment.* Upon whom I placed [the mission] to exact My vengeance and My judgment.

rashi.heb:
*ונתתיו.* 
בידו:
rashi.eng: *and I will deliver him.* into his hands.

rashi.heb:
*אל בני עמון ואל חרפתם.* 
אשר שמחו בנפול גורלו של נבוכדנצר בקסמיו לבא על ירושלים וחרפו אותי ואת עמי לאמר יד עכו"ם שלהם רמה:
rashi.eng: *concerning the children of Ammon and concerning their blasphemy,.* [in] that they rejoiced when Nebuchadnezzar’s lot in his divinations fell out to come upon Jerusalem, and they blasphemed Me and My people, saying that their deity was triumphant.

rashi.heb:
*להכיל.* 
חללים רבים :
rashi.eng: *to consume.* Heb. לְהָכִיל, to cause many slain to fall.

rashi.heb:
*למען ברק.* 
למען לא יחשך מראה להט שלה בחללי':
rashi.eng: *in order to glitter.* In order that its shiny appearance should not be darkened by its slain ones.

rashi.heb:
*בחזות לך שוא.* 
קוסמי עמון חזו להם שוא לאמר לא יבא עוד עלינו:
rashi.eng: *When you prophesy vanity for yourself.* The diviners of Ammon prophesied vanity for themselves, saying, “Nothing more will come upon us.”

rashi.heb:
*לתת אותך אל צוארי חללי רשעים.* 
להטעותך ולתת את צואריך כצוארי חללי רשעי' של ישראל:
rashi.eng: *to place you with the necks of the slain of the wicked.* To mislead you and to place your neck like the necks of the slain of the wicked of Israel.

rashi.heb:
*אשר בא יומם וגו'.* 
יום שלהם:
rashi.eng: *whose day has come, etc..* Heb. יוֹמָם, their day.

rashi.heb:
*השב.* 
כמו השב שהרי השי"ן רפה המתיני עד שוב חרב שעל ישראל אל תערה ואחר כך כשיגמור נקמתו בישראל ישוב עליך ובמקום אשר נבראת וגומר:
rashi.eng: *It has been returned.* Heb. הָשֵּׁב, like שָּׁבָה, it has returned, because the ‘shin’ has no ‘dagesh.’ [The missing ‘dagesh’ indicates that no letter is missing; hence, the root is שוּב, return, rather than ישב, sit or dwell.] Wait until the sword that is upon Israel returns into its sheath, and afterward, when he has finished His revenge upon Israel, He will return upon you, and in the place you were created, etc.

rashi.heb:
*אפיח עליך.* 
לשון נפיחת אש במפוח:
rashi.eng: *I shall blow upon you.* Heb. אָפִּיחָ, an expression for blowing fire with a bellows.

rashi.heb:
*אנשים בוערים.* 
מנהיגין עצמן בשגעון לחבל ולהשחית:
rashi.eng: *brutish men.* Who behave madly to ruin and to destroy.

rashi.heb:
*חרשי משחית.* 
אומנין לקטלא, (זה ימים רבים שפירשתי פרשה זו כאשר כתוב למעלה עכשיו אני רואה בשינוי לשונות שבה שאין הנביא מדבר אלא על החרב), לתת אותך אל צוארי חללי רשעים וגו', השב אל תערה וגו', אפיח עליך וגו' אינו נופל ל' זה אלא על מתכת וכן חרשי משחית ונראה בעיני שעל נבוכדנאצר נאמרה נבואה זו וכן משמע הנבא ואמרת כה אמר ה' אלהים על בני עמון ועל חרפתם כלומר (שחרפתי שמחרפים היו) על נבוכדנצר (בשביל נבוכדנצר) שבני עמון מחרפים את ישראל על שהחריבם נבוכדנצר:
rashi.eng: *craftsmen of destruction.* Artisans of murder. (Already many days [have passed] since I explained this chapter as it is written above. Now I see from the peculiarities of its wording that the prophet is talking only about the sword.) “To place you upon the necks of the slain of the wicked”, “It has been returned to its sheath, etc.” “I shall blow upon you.” This wording is appropriate only for metal, and so “craftsmen of destruction.” It seems to me that this prophecy was stated about Nebuchadnezzar, and so it appears [from]: “prophesy and say: So said the Lord God concerning the children of Ammon and concerning their taunts.” That is to say, [their taunts] over Nebuchadnezzar [because of Nebuchadnezzar], for the children of Ammon were taunting Israel because Nebuchadnezzar destroyed them. [33]

rashi.heb:
*שחרב חרב פתוחה.* 
חרב נבוכדנצר הכפולה לצאת בשני הדרכים על ירושלם ועל בני עמון כמו בפרשה העליונה הרי פורענות לבני עמון:
rashi.eng: *Sword, drawn sword.* The sword of Nebuchadnezzar, which is double, to go out on the two ways, against Jerusalem and against the children of Ammon, as is delineated in the above chapter, thus the retribution on the children of Ammon. [34]

rashi.heb:
*בחזות לך שוא בקסם לך כזב.* 
אתה סבור כי על ידי קסמיך של הבל ושוא וכזב אתה מצליח שחרבך נתונה אל צוארי חללים הרשעים שבא יומם בגזרה מלפני בעת תשלום את קיצם:
rashi.eng: *When you prophesy for yourself, when you divine lies for yourself.* You think that through your divinations of vanity, futility, and lies, you will prosper, for your sword is placed upon the necks of the slain of the wicked, whose day has come by decree from before Me at the time of the payment at the time of their end. [35]

rashi.heb:
*השב אל תערה.* 
כלומר העת יבא שתשוב אל תערה ותקבל החרב פורענותה מיד מלכי מדי ואז אפיח עליך באש עברתי ותהיה נתונה ביד נפחים שוטים שהם חרשי משחית שיבואו לחדדך ולמורטך כאשר מאז וישחיתוך:
rashi.eng: *It has been returned to its sheath.* That is to say, the time will come that the sword will return to its sheath, and the sword will receive its own retribution, at the hands of the kings of Media, and then I shall blow upon you with the fire of My wrath, and you shall be delivered into the hands of mad blacksmiths, who are craftsmen of destruction, who will come to sharpen and to furbish it as of yore, and they will destroy you.

notes.648: (tn, Heb): “will you judge.” Here the imperfect form of the verb is probably used with a desiderative nuance. Addressed to the prophet, “judge” means to warn of or pronounce God’s impending judgment upon the city. See 20:4.
notes.649: (tn): The phrase “bloody city” is used of Nineveh in Nah 3:1.

rashi.heb:
*ויהי דבר ה' אלי לאמר. התשפוט את עיר הדמים.* 
ירושלים:
rashi.eng: *will you judge the city of bloodshed.* Jerusalem.

rashi.heb:
*והודעתה.* 
מפיק ה"א והודעתה אותה:
rashi.eng: *and let her know.* The “ heh” in והודעתה is pointed, so that the meaning is, “and let her know.”

notes.650: (tn, Heb): “her time”; this refers to the time of impending judgment (see the note on “doom” in v. 4).

rashi.heb:
*עיר שופכת דם בתוכה לבוא עתה.* 
הרי זה מקרא מסורס וזהו פיר' עיר שופכת דם בתוכה אמר ה' אלהים לבוא עתה:
rashi.eng: *O city that sheds blood in her midst, her time is approaching.* This is a transposed verse, and this is its meaning: A city that sheds blood in her midst the Lord God said that its time is coming.

rashi.heb:
*ועשתה גילולים.* 
כמו ואשר עשתה גלולים וגו':
rashi.eng: *and makes idols.* Like “and which makes idols, etc.”

notes.651: (tn, Heb): “you have brought near your days.” The expression “bring near your days” appears to be an adaptation of the idiom “days draw near,” which is used to indicate that an event, such as death, is imminent (see Gen 27:41; 47:29; Deut 31:14; 1 Kgs 2:1; Ezek 12:23). Here “your days” probably refers to the days of the personified city’s life, which was about to come to an end through God’s judgment.
notes.652: (tn, Heb): “and you have come to your years.” This appears to mean that she has arrived at the time when her years (i.e., life) would end, though it may mean that her years of punishment will begin. Because “day” and “time” are so closely associated in the immediate context (see 21:25, 29) some prefer to emend the text and read “you have brought near your time.” See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:31, as well as the translator’s note on verse 3.
notes.653: (tn): The Hebrew verb is a prophetic perfect, emphasizing that the action is as good as done from the speaker’s perspective.

rashi.heb:
*עד שנותיך.* 
גזירת ונושנתם (דברים ד) בגי' שאמר משה:
rashi.eng: *up to your years.* The decree of (Deut. 4:25): “and you will have grown old,” with its numerical value, which Moses said.

rashi.heb:
*וקלסה.* 
דבה שהכל נדברים ביך פרלרי"ץ בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *and [a subject of] gossip.* Heb. וְקַלָסָה, gossip, that everyone will speak about you, parlediz in Old French, [subject of] gossip.

rashi.heb:
*יתקלסו בך.* 
ומה היא הקלסות
rashi.eng: *will gossip about you.* And what is the gossip?…

rashi.heb:
*טמאת השם.* 
זו היא שטמאת את שמה שהיו נקראים עם קדוש בנים ליוצרם וגרמו עצמם להקראו' עם טמא שפתים (ישעיהו ו׳:ה׳):
rashi.eng: *whose name is so befouled.* This is she who befouled her name, for they were called a holy people, sons of their Creator, and they caused themselves to be called (Isa. 6:5) “a people of unclean lips.”

notes.655: (tn, Heb): “Look! The princes of Israel, each according to his arm, were in you in order to shed blood.”

rashi.heb:
*איש לזרועו.* 
כל דאלים גבר:
rashi.eng: *each one by his own arm.* Whoever was stronger overpowered [the other].

notes.657: (tn): Widows and orphans are often coupled together in the OT (Deut 14:29; 16:11, 14; 24:19-21; 26:12-13; Jer 7:6; 22:3). They represented all who were poor and vulnerable to economic exploitation.

rashi.heb:
*אב ואם הקלו בך.* 
כל התועבות שבפ' קדושים תהיו שהוזהרו עליהם נמנו כאן:
rashi.eng: *Father and mother are held light in you.* All the abominations in the section of (Lev. 19, 20) “You shall be holy,” about which they were warned, are enumerated here.

rashi.heb:
*קדשי בזית.* 
ולא כמו שאמרתי לרצונכם תזבחו (ויקרא י"ט):
rashi.eng: *My holy things have you despised.* And not as I said (Lev. 22:29): “you shall slaughter it as an expression of your good will.”

notes.658: (tn, Heb): “men of slander are in you in order to shed blood.”
notes.659: (tn, Heb): “and on the mountains they eat within you.” The mountains mentioned here were the site of pagan sacrifices. See 18:6.
notes.660: (sn): This statement introduces vv. 10-11 and refers in general terms to the sexual sins described there. For the legal background of vv. 10-11, see Lev 18:7-20; 20:10-21; Deut 22:22-23, 30; 27:22.

rashi.heb:
*ואל ההרים אכלו בך.* 
ובטוריא פלחו ביך לטעותא:
rashi.eng: *and in you they have eaten upon the mountains.* and on the mountains they have worshipped in you to pagan deities.

rashi.heb:
*זמה עשו.* 
עצות של רשעה:
rashi.eng: *they have held wicked plans.* Heb. זִמָה, plans of wickedness.

notes.661: (tn, Heb): “the nakedness of a father one uncovers within you.” The ancient versions read the verb as plural (“they uncover”). If the singular is retained, it must be taken as indefinite and representative of the entire group. The idiomatic expression “uncover the nakedness” refers here to sexual intercourse (cf. Lev 18:6). To uncover a father’s nakedness could include sexual relations with one’s own mother (Lev 18:7), but more likely it refers to having intercourse with another wife of one’s father, such as a stepmother (Lev 18:8; cf. Gen 35:22; 49:4).
notes.662: (tn, Heb): “(one who is) unclean due to the impurity they humble within you.” The use of the verb “to humble” suggests that these men forced themselves upon women during menstruation. Having sexual relations with a woman during her period was forbidden by the Law (Lev 18:19; 20:18).

notes.664: (tn): The verb is the same one used in verse 10b and suggests forcible sexual violation of the woman.
notes.665: (sn): Sexual relations with one’s half-sister may be primarily in view here. See Lev 18:9; 20:17.

notes.666: (tn, Heb): “usury and interest you take.” See 18:13, 17. This kind of economic exploitation violated the law given in Lev 25:36.
notes.667: (sn): Forgetting the Lord is also addressed in Deut 6:12; 8:11, 14; Jer 3:21; 13:25; Ezek 23:35; Hos 2:15; 8:14; 13:6.
notes.668: (tn): The second person verb forms are feminine singular in Hebrew, indicating that the personified city is addressed here as representing its citizens.

rashi.heb:
*ותבצעי רעיך בעושק.* 
העשרת את אוהביך בעושק שעשקת מן העניים לשון אחר ותבצעי לשון גזל כמו ובוצע ברך נאץ ה' (תהלים ו') וכה פתרונו ותגזלי לרעיך בעושק:
rashi.eng: *and enriched your neighbors with dishonest gain.* You made your friends rich with the dishonest gain that you gained dishonestly from the poor. Another explanation: וַתְּבַצְעִי is a form of a word for robbery, like (Ps. 10:3): “and the robber (וּבֹצֵעַ) blesses himself for having blasphemed the Lord.” Accordingly, its interpretation is: and you robbed your friends with affliction.

notes.669: (sn): This gesture apparently expresses mourning and/or anger (see 6:11; 21:14, 17).
notes.670: (tn, Heb): “the blood which was in you.”

rashi.heb:
*הכיתי כפי.* 
צעקתי ווי וקינה:
rashi.eng: *I clapped My hands together.* I cried out, “Woe!” and lamentation.

rashi.heb:
*אל בצעיך.* 
כאן למדנו שהגזל קשה מן הכל שעליו נתחתם גזר דין:
rashi.eng: *over your dishonest gain.* Here we learn that robbery is more severe than all of them, for their verdict was sealed because of it.

notes.671: (tn, Heb): “stand.” The heart here stands for the emotions; Jerusalem would panic in the face of God’s judgment.
notes.672: (tn, Heb): “in the days when I act against you.”

rashi.heb:
*אשר אני עושה אותך.* 
פועל לך כפעלך:
rashi.eng: *that I will deal with you.* That I will deal with you according to your deeds.

notes.673: (sn): The ultimate purpose of divine judgment is to purify the covenant community of its sins.

rashi.heb:
*והתימותי.* 
וכליתי:
rashi.eng: *and I will make… completely disappear.* And I will end.

notes.674: (tc): Several ancient versions read the verb as first person, in which case the Lord refers to how his people’s sin brings disgrace upon him. For a defense of the Hebrew text, see D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 1:712, n. 68, and M. Greenberg, Ezekiel (AB), 2:457-58. The phrase “within yourself” is the same as the several previous occurrences of “within you” but adjusted to fit this clause which is the culmination of the series of indictments.

rashi.heb:
*ונחלת בך.* 
תתחלחלי בעצמך על מה שעשית:
rashi.eng: *And you shall be profaned within yourself.* Heb. וְנִחַלְתְּ בָּךְ, you shall be profaned within yourself for what you have done.

notes.675: (tn): For similar imagery, see Isa 1:21-26; Jer 6:27-30.

rashi.heb:
*לסיג.* 
תערובת פסולת המעורב בכסף וזהב וצריך להתיכו באש לצורפו:
rashi.eng: *dross.* A mixture of dross mixed in silver and gold, and it is necessary to smelt it in fire to refine it.

rashi.heb:
*כור.* 
שצורפין בו זהב:
rashi.eng: *a furnace.* in which gold is refined.

notes.676: (tn): The Hebrew second person pronoun is masculine plural here and in vv. 19b-21, indicating that the people are being addressed.
notes.677: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

notes.678: (tn, Heb): “I will put.” No object is supplied in the Hebrew, prompting many to emend the text to “I will blow.” See BHS and verse 21.

rashi.heb:
*קבוצת כסף.* 
כאשר יקבוץ הצורף את כל הסיגים אל תוך כור:
rashi.eng: *As they gather silver.* As the silversmith gathers all the dross into the furnace.

rashi.heb:
*לפחת.* 
לנפח:
rashi.eng: *to blow.* Heb. לָפַחַת, to blow (לְנַפֵּחַ).

rashi.heb:
*להנתיך.* 
ויצקת מתרגם ותתיך:
rashi.eng: *to melt.* Heb. לְהַנְתִּיךְ. (Exod. 25:12) “and cast (וְיָצַקְתָּ)” is translated into Aramaic as וְתַתִּיךְ.

notes.679: (tc): The MT reads “that is not cleansed”; the LXX reads “that is not drenched,” which assumes a different vowel pointing as well as the loss of a מ (mem) due to haplography. In light of the following reference to showers, the reading of the LXX certainly fits the context well. For a defense of the emendation, see L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:32. Yet the MT is not an unreasonable reading since uncleanness in the land also fits the context, and a poetic connection between rain and the land being uncleansed may be feasible since washing with water is elsewhere associated with cleansing (Num 8:7; 31:23; Ps 51:7).

rashi.heb:
*לא גושמה ביום זעם.* 
לא נתן גשם הראוי לה לטהר ביום זעם ופירוש הדבר כתרגומו לא איתעבידו בה עובדין טבין דיגנון עלה ביום לווט:
rashi.eng: *it was not rained upon on the day of fury.* The rain fit to cleanse it on the day of fury was not given it, and the explanation of the matter is as the Targum paraphrases: Good deeds were not performed in her which would protect her on the day of curse.

notes.681: (tn, Heb): “a conspiracy of her prophets is in her midst.” The LXX reads “whose princes” rather than “a conspiracy of prophets.” The prophets are mentioned later in the paragraph (v. 28). If one follows the LXX in verse 25, then five distinct groups are mentioned in vv. 25-29: princes, priests, officials, prophets, and the people of the land. For a defense of the Septuagintal reading, see L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:32, and D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 1:720, n. 4.
notes.682: (tn, Heb): “her widows they have multiplied.” The statement alludes to their murderous acts.

rashi.heb:
*קשר נביאיה.* 
נקשרים יחד בעצה רעה:
rashi.eng: *There is a conspiracy of her prophets.* Heb. קֶשֶׁר [lit. a knot]. They are joined together in an evil counsel.

rashi.heb:
*נפש אכלו.* 
שהיו נוטלין שוחד ומחזיקין ידי מרעים להרוג ולשלול ולבוז ונבאין להם שלום:
rashi.eng: *they devoured souls.* For they would take bribes and strengthen the hands of evildoers to kill and plunder and rob, and then they would prophesy peace for them.

rashi.heb:
*חוסן.* 
ממון:
rashi.eng: *riches.* Heb. חֹסֶן, money.

notes.683: (tn): Or “between the consecrated and the common.”
notes.684: (tn, Heb): “hide their eyes from.” The idiom means to disregard or ignore something or someone (see Lev 20:4; 1 Sam 12:3; Prov 28:27; Isa 1:15).

rashi.heb:
*חמסו תורתי.* 
עליהם היה להוכיח ולהורות ולהודיע חק ומשפט ולא עשו הרי זה חמס שחמסוה מן הצריכין ללמוד:
rashi.eng: *robbed My Torah.* It was incumbent upon them to reprove, to instruct, and to make known statutes and ordinances, but they did not do so. This is robbery, for they robbed it from those who needed to learn.

rashi.heb:
*ואחל.* 
ונתחללתי:
rashi.eng: *and I was profaned in their midst.* Heb. וָאֵחַל, and I was profaned.

rashi.heb:
*למען בצוע בצע.* 
לחטוף ממון:
rashi.eng: *for the sake of dishonest gain.* To seize money.

notes.685: (tn, Heb): “her prophets coat for themselves with whitewash.” The expression may be based on Ezek 13:10-15.

rashi.heb:
*טחו להם תפל.* 
דומין לטחי בנין בטיט שאינו מעובד כל צרכו שאין בו תבן והוא נפשר מאליו בבא עליו גשמים ולשון תפל כל דבר המחוסר תקון:
rashi.eng: *plastered for them with daub.* They are like those who plaster a building with plaster that is not completely processed, which has no straw; it dissolves by itself when rain falls on it. The expression תָּפֵל means anything that is lacking preparation.

notes.686: (tn, Heb): “and the foreigner they have oppressed without justice.”

notes.688: (tn, Heb): “their way on their head I have placed.”

rashi.heb:
*שתים נשים.* 
תרתי מדינן דאינון כתרתין נשין:
rashi.eng: *two women.* Two states, which are like two women.

rashi.heb:
*בנות אם אחת.* 
שתיהן מכנסיה אחת נחלקו לשתים בימי רחבעם:
rashi.eng: *the daughters of one mother.* The two of them were from one nation, separated into two in the days of Rehoboam.

notes.689: (tn): In the Hebrew text the subject is left unstated and must be supplied from the context.

rashi.heb:
*שמה מועכו.* 
בני מצרים את שדיהם ל' ומעוך (ויקרא כב):
rashi.eng: *There… were pressed.* [Heb. מֹעְכוּ]. The Egyptians [pressed] their bosoms, an expression of (Lev. 22:24): “and anything that has been crushed (וּמַעוּךְ).”

rashi.heb:
*ושם עשו.* 
המצריים את דדי בתוליהן כלומר למדום את דרכי תועבותם, עשו איטיינירי"ש בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *and there they squeezed.* The Egyptians [squeezed] their virgin breasts; i.e., they taught them the ways of their abominations. [Heb. עִשׂוּ,] eteyn[d] irent in Old French, they squeezed

notes.690: (tn): The names Oholah and Oholibah are both derived from the word meaning “tent.” The meaning of Oholah is “her tent,” while Oholibah means “my tent is in her.”
notes.691: (sn): In this allegory the Lord is depicted as being the husband of two wives. The OT law prohibited a man from marrying sisters (Lev 18:18), but the practice is attested in the OT (cf. Jacob). The metaphor is utilized here for illustrative purposes and does not mean that the Lord condoned such a practice or bigamy in general.

rashi.heb:
*ושמותן.* 
בכינוי אהלה ואהליב':
rashi.eng: *And their names.* i.e., their nicknames were Oholah and Oholibah.

rashi.heb:
*ושמותן.* 
הראשונים שומרון היא שאני מכנה אהלה שנעשית אהל מתחילה לעגלי ירבעם ובית הבעל לאחאב ואע"פ ששומרון לא נבנתה אלא בימי עמרי קורא את מלכי ישראל על שמה שמשנבנית נעשית ראש:
rashi.eng: *and their names.* The original ones. Samaria is the one I nickname Oholah, for from the beginning she became a tent (אֹהֶל) for the calves of Jeroboam and for Ahab’s temple of Baal. Although Samaria was not built until the days of Omri, He calls the kings of Israel by its name, because as soon as it was built, it became the capital.

rashi.heb:
*אהליבה.* 
על שם שאהלי היה בה ומקדשי:
rashi.eng: *Oholibah.* Because My tent (אֹהֹלִי) was in her (בָה), and My sanctuary.

notes.692: (tn, Heb): “while she was under me.” The expression indicates that Oholah is viewed as the Lord’s wife. See Num 5:19-20, 29. Played the harlot refers to alliances with pagan nations in this context. In Ezek 16 harlotry described the sin of idolatry.
notes.694: (tn): The term apparently refers to Assyrian military officers; it is better construed with the description that follows. See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 1:738.

rashi.heb:
*ותעגב.* 
ותתאוה אישויי"ר בלע"ז ל"א דיששירי"ר:
rashi.eng: *and she lusted.* [Heb. וַתַּעְגַּב,] and she lusted, esvayer or eswaier in Old French, to covet, to lust after. Some editions read: desirer, to desire.

rashi.heb:
*אל אשור קרובים.* 
שהיו שכנים לה ושלחו להם להיות להם לעזר זה היה מנחם בן גדי (מלכים ב ט״ו:י״ט) שנתן מס לפול מלך אשור להיות ידו אתו להחזיק הממלכה בידו והנביא מדמה הדבר לאשה מנאפת שאם היו עובדים להקב"ה לא נצטרכו למלכי אשור:
rashi.eng: *for the Assyrians, who were nearby.* Who were her neighbors, and they sent to them [requesting that they] aid them. This is Menachem the son of Gadi (II Kings 15:19f.), who gave tribute to Pul king of Assyria in order “that his hands might be with him to strengthen the kingdom in his hand.” The prophet likens the matter to an adulterous woman, for, had they worshipped the Holy One, blessed be He, they would not have needed the kings of Assyria.

rashi.heb:
*ותתן תזנותיה עליהם.* 
לב ניאופים ורוח זנונים נתנה עליה' שהית' מתאוה להם:
rashi.eng: *And she bestowed her harlotries upon them.* Her adulterous heart and her promiscuous spirit she bestowed upon them, for she desired them.

rashi.heb:
*ובכל אשר עגבה וגו'.* 
בכל העכו"ם אשר נשתתפה עמהם למדה דרכיהם ונטמא בגילוליהם:
rashi.eng: *and in all that she lusted.* In all the nations with whom she collaborated, she learned their ways and became defiled with their idols.

notes.696: (tn, Heb): “and poured out their harlotry on her.”

rashi.heb:
*ואת תזנותיה ממצרים לא עזבה.* 
גם על מלכי מצרים סמכו שמצינו (שם יו) בהושע בן אלה אשר שלח מלאכים אל סוא מלך מצרים:
rashi.eng: *And her harlotries from Egypt she did not abandon.* They relied also upon the kings of Egypt, for we find (II Kings 17:4), concerning Hoshea the son of Elah, that he sent messengers to So the king of Egypt.

rashi.heb:
*כי אותה שכבו וגו'.* 
ומאז וישפכו תזנותם עליה תאות זנונים נכנס בה מימי נעוריה:
