rashi.eng: *for they had lain with her, etc..* And since then, “they poured out their harlotry upon her” - her promiscuous spirit entered her from the days of her youth.

notes.697: (tn, Heb): “I gave her into the hand of her lovers, into the hand of the sons of Assyria.”

rashi.heb:
*לכן נתתיה וגו'.* 
שבא סנחרב והגלה אותם:
rashi.eng: *Therefore, I delivered her, etc..* For Sennacherib came and exiled them.

rashi.heb:
*ותהי שם לנשים.* 
לוקח מהן קללה לכל הנואפו' להווסר ממנה ראו מה עלתה לפלונית על זימתה:
rashi.eng: *and she became a name for the women.* to take from them a curse for any adulteress to learn a lesson from her: See what happened to so and so because of her lewdness.

rashi.heb:
*ושפוטים.* 
כמו שפטים יושטישא"ט בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *and… judgments.* [Heb. וּשְּׁפוּטִים,] like שְּׁפָטִים, judgments, justises, jostises in Old French, judgments, punishments.

notes.699: (tn): The word “this” is not in the original text.

rashi.heb:
*ותרא אחותה אהליבה.* 
את כל הרעה אשר בא לאחותה על זנוניה ולא יראה:
rashi.eng: *And her sister Oholibah saw.* all the evil that befell her sister because of her harlotries, but she was unafraid.

rashi.heb:
*ותשחת עגבתה.* 
תאותה זויט"ר בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *she became… corrupt in her lust.* [Heb. עַגְבָתָה,] her lust, wai(y)ter in Old French, unbridled passion.

rashi.heb:
*אל בני אשור עגבה.* 
זה אחז ששלח אל מלך אשור לעזרה (שם):
rashi.eng: *For the sons of Assyria she lusted.* This is Ahaz, who sent to the king of Assyria for aid (II Kings 16:7).

notes.700: (tn): The only other occurrence of the Hebrew term is in Jer 22:14.

rashi.heb:
*ותוסף אל תזנותיה.* 
להתאוות לצלמים שלא ראתה אותם אלא דמותם:
rashi.eng: *And she increased her harlotries.* to lust for images that she had not seen [in actuality], only their likeness.

rashi.heb:
*מחוקה על הקיר וגו'.* 
בששר כזאת לא עשתה אחותה:
rashi.eng: *engraved on the wall.*  with types of drawings, whereas her sister did not do anything like this.

rashi.heb:
*צלמי כשדים.* 
דמות אנשי כשדים שמשונין בלבושיהון:
rashi.eng: *images of Chaldeans.* The likeness of Chaldean men, who were unusual in their attire.

rashi.heb:
*בששר.* 
מיני ציור:
rashi.eng: *with types of drawings.* [Heb. בַּשָׁשַׁר,] types of drawings.

rashi.heb:
*חגורי אזור.* 
כן דרך לבושי כשדים:
rashi.eng: *Girded with girdles.* This was the way of the Chaldeans’ attire.

rashi.heb:
*סרוחי טבולים.* 
יתירי כובעים גדולים ומנחם פירש כמו ויטבלו הכתונת בדם (בראשית ל״ז:ל״א) ופתרון סרוחי טבולי' כן הוא סרח העודף (שמו' כו) מן המצנפת צבועה, טבולים אין לו דמיון ופתרונו לפי הענין וכן ת"י מחתין קולסין:
rashi.eng: *hanging turbans.* [Heb. סְרוּחֵי טְבוּלִים.] [סְרוּחֵי means] oversized, large hats. Menachem (p. 97) explains [טְבוּלִים] like (Gen. 37:31) “and dipped (וַיִטְבְּלוּ) the shirt in the blood.” Thus the interpretation of סְרוּחֵי טְבוּלִים is as follows (Exod. 26:12): “The overhanging (וְסֵרַח) length” of the dyed turban. There is no [other occurrence of a word] similar to טְבוּלִים, and its meaning is derived from the context, and so did Jonathan render: helmets placed on their heads].

rashi.heb:
*שלישים.* 
גבורים:
rashi.eng: *mighty men.* [Heb. שָׁלִישִׁים,] mighty men.

notes.702: (tn, Heb): “at the appearance of her eyes.”
notes.703: (sn): The Chaldeans were prominent tribal groups of Babylonia. The imagery is reminiscent of events in the reigns of Hezekiah (2 Kgs 20:12-15) and Jehoiakim (2 Kgs 23:34-24:1).

rashi.heb:
*למראה עיניה.* 
בשביל שראתה דמות צורתן:
rashi.eng: *at the sight [that reached] her eyes.* Because she saw the likeness of their form.

notes.704: (tn, Heb): “The sons of Babel came to her on a bed of love.”

rashi.heb:
*ויבאו אליה בני בבל למשכב דודים.* 
כרתו יחד ברית ואומר אני שזה נאמר על חזקיה ששמח על מלאכי מרודך בלאדן (ישעיהו ל״ט:א׳) והאכילן על שלחנו והראם את כל בית נכותה ודוגמא שאמר הנביא אנשי מחוקה על הקיר לפי שמארץ רחוקה באו ולא היו בני כשדים רגילים אצלם כמו שנאמר שם מארץ רחוקה באו אלי ובשביל ראות פניהם פעם אחת נתחבבו עליו והקפיד הקב"ה על הדבר כמה שנאמר הנה ימים באים ונשא את כל אשר בביתך וגו' (שם) (ובדברי הימים ב ל״ב:כ״ה) ולא כגמול עלי השיב חזקיהו כי גבה לבו ויהי עליו קצף גדול וגומר:
rashi.eng: *And the children of Babylon came to her for a bed of love.* They made a covenant together, and I say that this is said concerning Hezekiah, who rejoiced about the emissaries of Merodach-baladan (Isa. 39, II Kings 20), and he fed them at his table and showed them his entire treasure house. This resembles the prophet’s statement (verse 14), “men engraved on the wall,” because they came from a distant land, and the Chaldeans were not frequent visitors to them, as it is said (Isa. 39:3): “They have come to me from a distant country,” and from seeing their faces once, they became endeared to him. And the Holy One, blessed be He, became wroth with him because of this matter, as it is written (Isa. 36:6, II Kings 20:17): “Behold a time will come when everything in your palace… will be carried off, etc.,” and in (II) Chronicles (32:25): “But Hezekiah did not pay back according to the benefit they had done for him, but his heart became haughty; therefore, wrath came upon him and upon Judah, etc.”

rashi.heb:
*ותקע נפשה מהם.* 
שמרד בהם יהויקים וצדקיהו, ותקע אשלוקי"ר בלע"ז, ותקע כמו (בראשית ל״ב:כ״ו) ותקע כף ירך יעקב הוקעה. לשון חבור ותקיעת עץ בארץ הוא וכן בהשתלפו מן הארץ יפול בו ל' קעייה כאשר תאמר ותשרש שרשיה (תהילים פ׳:י׳) לשון קליטה ובכל תבואתי תשרש לשון עקור וכן בסעיפיה פוריה (ישעיהו י״ז:ו׳) ל' ענפים ומסעף פארה (שם י) לשון קוצץ ענפי העץ ופארותיו:
rashi.eng: *her soul was disgusted with them.* [Heb. וַתֵּקַע.] That Jehoiakim and Zedekiah rebelled against them. וַתֵּקַע is esloched in Old French, dislocated. וַתֵּקַע is like (Gen. 32: 26): “and the upper joint of Jacob’s thigh was dislocated (וַתֵּקַע).” הוֹקָעָה is an expression of joining and inserting a pole into the earth, and also when it is withdrawn from the earth, is the expression קְעִיָה appropriate for it, just as you say (Ps. 80:10): “it took root (וַתַשְׁרֵשׁ),” as an expression of taking root, and (Job 31:12), “and it uproots (תְּשָׁרֵשׁ) all my grain,” as an expression of uprooting. Similarly (Isa. 17:6): “on its branches (בִּסְעִפֶיהָ) when it produces fruit,” is an expression of branches, and (ibid. 10:33), “lops off (מְסָעֵף) the branches,” is an expression of cutting off the branches of the tree and its boughs.

notes.706: (tn, Heb): “She exposed her harlotry and she exposed her nakedness.”

rashi.heb:
*לזכור את ימי נעוריה.* 
עלתה על לבה תאות בני מצרים ששלח צדקיהו אליה שנאמר (לעיל יז) וימרד בו לשלוח מלאכיו מצרים:
rashi.eng: *to remember the days of her youth.* The desire for the Egyptians rose in her heart, for Zedekiah sent to them, as it is said (above 17:15): “But he rebelled against him by sending to Egypt.”

notes.709: (tn, Heb): “She lusted after their concubines (?) whose flesh was the flesh of donkeys.” The phrase “their concubines” is extremely problematic here. The pronoun is masculine plural, suggesting that the Egyptian men are in view, but how concubines would fit into the picture envisioned here is not clear. Some suggest that Ezekiel uses the term in an idiomatic sense of “paramour,” but this still fails to explain how the pronoun relates to the noun. It is more likely that the term refers here to the Egyptians’ genitals. The relative pronoun that follows introduces a more specific description of their genitals.

rashi.heb:
*ותעגבה על פלגשיהם.* 
על פלגשות' להיות להם לפלגש:
rashi.eng: *And she lusted for their concubinage.* [Heb. פִּלַּגְשֵׁיהֶם,] for their concubinage, to be a concubine to them.

rashi.heb:
*אשר בשר חמורים בשרם.* 
אבר תשמיש:
rashi.eng: *those whose flesh is the flesh of donkeys.* [i.e.,] the phallus.

rashi.heb:
*וזרמת סוסים.* 
לשון רבוי תשמיש שמרבים תשמיש יותר משאר כל הזכרים שבבהמה:
rashi.eng: *and… is the issue of horses.* An expression of a profusion of sexual intercourse, for they engage in sexual intercourse more than any other male animals.

rashi.heb:
*זרמת.* 
קלוח הזרע כמו זרם מים עבר (חבקוק ג׳:י׳):
rashi.eng: *whose issue.* זִרְמַת refers to the stream of semen, like (Habakkuk 3:10): “A stream (זֶרֶם) of water passed.”

notes.710: (tn): Or “you took note of.” The Hebrew verb פָּקַד (paqad) in the Qal implies evaluating something and then acting in light of that judgment; here the prophet depicts Judah as approving of her youthful unfaithfulness and then magnifying it at the present time. Some translations assume the verb should be repointed as a Niphal, rendering “you missed” or by extension “you longed for,” but such an extension of the Niphal “to be missing” is otherwise unattested.
notes.711: (tn, Heb): “when (they) did,” but the verb makes no sense here and is better emended to “when (they) fondled,” a verb used in vv. 3 and 8. See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:43.
notes.712: (tn, Heb): “for the sake of,” but the expression is awkward and is better emended to read “to squeeze.” See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:43.

rashi.heb:
*ותפקדי.* 
ותזכרי:
rashi.eng: *And you remembered.* [Heb. וַתִּפְקְדִי,] and you remembered.

rashi.heb:
*בעשות.* 
לשון כבישה:
rashi.eng: *were squeezed.* [Heb. בַּעֲשׂוֹת,] an expression of pressing.

notes.713: (tn): The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) indicates becoming aware of something and has been translated here as a verb.

rashi.heb:
*את מאהביך.* 
את כשדים אשר ערבו על חזקיהו:
rashi.eng: *your lovers.* The Chaldeans, who pleased Hezekiah.

rashi.heb:
*את אשר נקעה נפשך מהם.* 
אשר חזר צדקיהו ושנאם ומרד בהם:
rashi.eng: *those with whom your soul has become disgusted.* Whom Zedekiah [in a change of heart] subsequently hated and against whom he rebelled.

notes.714: (sn): Pekod was the name of an Aramean tribe (known as Puqudu in Mesopotamian texts) that lived in the region of the Tigris River.
notes.715: (sn): Shoa was the name of a nomadic people (the Sutu) that lived in Mesopotamia.
notes.716: (sn): Koa was the name of another Mesopotamian people group (the Qutu).

rashi.heb:
*פקוד ושוע וקוע.* 
ת"י שם מדינות ומקרא מסייעו (בספר ירמיהו נ׳:כ״א) על הארץ מרתים עלה עליה ועל יושבי פקוד, והפותרים אומרים ל' פקודים ושרים ושלטונים:
rashi.eng: *Pekod, Shoa, and Koa.* Jonathan rendered [these as] the names of states, and Scripture supports him in the Book of Jeremiah (50:21): “Upon the rebellious land, march upon her, and upon the inhabitants of Pekod.” [But] the Commentators say that they are an expression of appointees, princes, and rulers.

rashi.heb:
*וקרואים.* 
שמונ"ץ בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *and summoned ones.* Somonz, semonz in Old French, summoned (top people).

notes.718: (tn): This is the only occurrence of this term in the OT. The precise meaning is uncertain.
notes.720: (tn, Heb): “I will place before them judgment.”

rashi.heb:
*הצן.* 
פירש דונש אחד מכלי המלחמה הוא ואני אומר לשון הקפות מחנות כמו ולצנינים בצדיכם (במדבר ל״ג:נ״ה) ולמשירין מקפנכון הצן (מנחם פירשו כמו צנה וסוחרה אמתו (תהילים צ״א:ד׳) ואין דונש מודה לו והתרגום שמתרגם וייתון עלך במאני זיינא מסייע לדונש): הצן כמו בהוצן ויש משמע הוצן כמו חוצן מן והביאו בניך בחוצן (ישעיהו מ״ט:כ״ב) שפירושו זרוע וכן ובאו עליך הוצן (כאן) ועניינו חיל כמו וזרועות הנגב (דניאל י״א:ט״ו) שפירושו וחיילות הנגב:
rashi.eng: *weapons.* [Heb. הֹצֶן]. Dunash (p. 59) explained it as one type of weapon, but I say that it is an expression of the surroundings of camps like (Num. 33:55): “and camps (וְלִצְנִינִים) in your sides,” [which Onkelos renders:] and camps surrounding you. Menachem (p. 150) explains הֹצֶן like (Ps. 91:4): “His truth is an encompassing shield (צִנָה וְסֹחֵרָה), but Dunash does not agree with him, and the Targum supports Dunash, rendering: they will come upon you with weapons. הֹצֶן is like בְּהֹצֶן, with weapons, and הֹצֶן could mean the same as חֹצֶן, from (Isa. 49:22): ” and they shall bring your sons בְּחֹצֶן, “ which means with the arm, and so too: ” And they will come upon you הֹצֶן, “ meaning [as with] an army, as (Dan. 11:15),” and the arms (וּזְרוֹעוֹת) of the south," meaning the armies of the south.

rashi.heb:
*ונתתי לפניהם משפט.* 
מה שעלי לשפוט אעשה אותם שלוחי לעשות המשפט:
rashi.eng: *and I shall place judgment before them.* What is incumbent upon Me to judge. I will make them My agents to execute the judgment.

rashi.heb:
*במשפטיהם.* 
משפט שלא כתבתי בתורתי והוא ממשפטי נימוסיהם ואיזה זה זה סימוי עינים שעוורו את עיני צדקיהו:
rashi.eng: *with their judgments.* A judgment that I did not write in My Torah, but which is one of the judgments of their customs, and what is it? Blinding the eyes, that they blinded Zedekiah’s eyes.

notes.722: (tn, Heb): “they will remove.”� This method of punishment is attested among ancient Egyptian and Hittite civilizations. See W. Zimmerli, Ezekiel (Hermeneia), 1:489.

rashi.heb:
*אפך ואזניך.* 
הם תפארת הפרצוף ולהם המשיל הכהונה והמלכות:
rashi.eng: *your nose and your ears.* They are the beauty of the countenance, and to them he compared the priesthood and the kingship.

rashi.heb:
*ואחריתך.* 
שאר העם:
rashi.eng: *and your survivors.* The rest of the people.

rashi.heb:
*ואחריתך תאכל באש.* 
ושפר ארעיך שהן אחריות לישען עליהם לפרנסה:
rashi.eng: *and your residue will be consumed by fire.* And the best of your land, which is the security upon which to rely for a livelihood.

rashi.heb:
*את בגדיך.* 
בגדי כהונה:
rashi.eng: *of your garments.* The priestly raiment.

notes.724: (tn, Heb): “I will cause your obscene conduct to cease from you and your harlotry from the land of Egypt.”

notes.726: (tn): The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) indicates becoming aware of something and has been translated here as a verb.
notes.727: (tn, Heb): “I am giving you into the hand of.”

rashi.heb:
*אשר שנאת.* 
כשדים שמרדת בהם:
rashi.eng: *those you hate.* The Chaldeans, against whom you rebelled.

notes.728: (tn): The Hebrew term means “labor,” but by extension it can also refer to that for which one works.
notes.729: (tn, Heb): “The nakedness of your prostitution will be exposed, and your obscene conduct and your harlotry.”

notes.730: (tn): The infinitive absolute continues the sequence begun in v. 28: “Look here, I am about to deliver you.” See Jo�on 2:430 �123.w.

rashi.heb:
*עשה אלה.* 
לשון פעול פיישנ"ט בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *These will be done.* [Heb. עָשׂה,] an expression of continuous action, faisant in French, doing (gerundive).

notes.731: (tn, Heb): “her cup.” A cup of intoxicating strong drink is used, here and elsewhere, as a metaphor for judgment because both leave one confused and reeling. (See Jer 25:15, 17, 28; Hab 2:16.) The cup of wrath is a theme also found in the NT (Mark 14:36).

notes.732: (sn): The image of a deep and wide cup suggests the degree of punishment; it will be extensive and leave the victim helpless.

rashi.heb:
*מרבה להכיל.* 
יתירה מלהכיל כמו מלסבול:
rashi.eng: *too much to bear.* Too much to contain, like to bear.

rashi.heb:
*ושממה.* 
תמהון:
rashi.eng: *and bewilderment.* [Heb. וּשְׁמָמָה] bewilderment.

notes.734: (tn, Heb): “You will drink it and drain (it).”
notes.735: (tn): D. I. Block compares this to the idiom of “licking the plate” (Ezekiel [NICOT], 1:754, n. 137). The text is difficult as the word translated “gnaw” is rare. The noun is used of the shattered pieces of pottery and so could envision a broken cup. But the Piel verb form is used in only one other place (Num 24:8), where it is a denominative from the noun “bone” and seems to mean to “break (bones).” Why it would be collocated with “sherds” is not clear. For this reason some emend the phrase to read “consume its dregs” (see L. C. Allen, Ezekiel [WBC], 2:44) or emend the verb to read “swallow,” as if the intoxicated Oholibah breaks the cup and then eats the very sherds in an effort to get every last drop of the beverage that dampens them.
notes.736: (sn): The severe action is more extreme than beating the breasts in anguish (Isa 32:12; Nah 2:7). It is also ironic for these are the very breasts she so blatantly offered to her lovers (vv. 3, 21).

rashi.heb:
*ומצית.* 
לשון מוצץ עד התמצית אישוצרא"ש בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *and drain.* [Heb. וּמָצְת,] an expression of sucking to the last drop, et tu suceras in French, and you will suck.

rashi.heb:
*ואת חרשיה.* 
דימה כוס המשקה פורענות לישראל לכלי חרש שמשנשתבר אין לו תקנה כך משתבא תשועתם וישבר הכוס לא ישוב להשקותם עוד וכשהוא מדבר בהשקאת העכו"ם קורא אותו זהב שנאמר כוס זהב בבל ביד ה' המשכרת כל הארץ (ירמיהו נ״א:ז׳):
rashi.eng: *and its shards.* He compares the cup that gives Israel the drink of retribution to an earthenware vessel, which, once broken, can no longer be repaired. So will it be that once their salvation comes and the cup breaks, He will not return to give them any more to drink. When He speaks of giving drink to the nations, however, He calls it gold, as it is said (Jer. 51:7): “Babylon is a golden cup in the Lord’s hand, it intoxicates all the earth.”

rashi.heb:
*ואת חרשיה תגרמי.* 
כמו ועצמותיהם יגרם (במדבר כ״ד:ח׳) לא גרמו לבקר (צפניה ג׳:ג׳) רונגייר בלע"ז גורר בשיניו את סביבות העצם או החרש לרדות מעליו בשר הדבוק בו ומנחם חברו לשון שבירה וגם כן פתר ועצמותיהם יגרם וכן לא גרמו לבקר:
rashi.eng: *you shall scrape.* [Heb. תְּגָרֵמִי,] like (Num. 24:8): “and he scrapes (יְגָרֵם) their bones;” (Zeph. 3:3), “they did not leave over the bones (גָרְמוּ) for morning,” ronger in French, to gnaw. He scrapes with his teeth around the bone or the shard to detach from it the meat adhering to it. Menachem (p. 59) connects it to an expression of breaking, and he interprets: “and he breaks their bones,” and “they did not break the bones for morning,” in like manner.

notes.737: (tn, Heb): “and you cast me behind your back.” The expression pictures her rejection of the Lord (see 1 Kgs 14:9).
notes.738: (tn): The word “punishment” is not in the Hebrew text but is demanded by the context.

rashi.heb:
*שאי זמתך.* 
קבילי חובי עצת חטאיך:
rashi.eng: *bear your lewdness.* Accept the liabilities of the counsel of your sins.

notes.739: (tn, Heb): “will you judge.” Here the imperfect form of the verb is probably used with a desiderative nuance. Addressed to the prophet, “judge” means to warn of or pronounce God’s impending judgment. See 20:4; 22:2.

rashi.heb:
*התשפוט.* 
לשון ויכוח:
rashi.eng: *will you judge.* [Heb. הֲתִשׁפֹט,] an expression of debate.

notes.740: (sn): The Lord speaks here in the role of the husband of the sisters.
notes.741: (tn): Heb “they have passed to them for food.” The verb is commonly taken to refer to passing children through fire, especially as an offering to the pagan god Molech. See Jer 32:35.

rashi.heb:
*ודם בידיהן.* 
בנאופיהם שפכו דם:
rashi.eng: *and blood is on their hands.* Through their adulteries, they shed blood.

rashi.heb:
*ואת גילוליהן נאפו.* 
נאוף שלהם עם גלוליהם היה:
rashi.eng: *and with their idols they have committed adultery.* Their adultery was with their idols.

rashi.heb:
*וגם את בניהן וגו'.* 
וזהו שפיכות הדם שבידיהם (כלומר שהוציאו זרע לבטלה בידיהם ולא עשו תשובה):
rashi.eng: *and also their children, etc..* And this is the bloodshed that is on their hands (i.e., they masturbated with their hands and they did not repent).

rashi.heb:
*טמאו את מקדשי ביום ההוא.* 
ביום ששחטו את בניהם לעכו"ם באות לפני במקדשי לעשות בו תועבה להכעיסני:
rashi.eng: *they defiled My sanctuary on that day.* On the day they slaughter their children for idolatry, they come before Me in My sanctuary to commit abominations therein, to provoke Me.

rashi.heb:
*ואת שבתותי חללו.* 
שהיו שוחטין את בניהם בשבת:
rashi.eng: *and they profaned My Sabbaths.* For they would slaughter their children on the Sabbath.

notes.743: (tn, Heb): “to whom a messenger was sent, and look, they came.” Foreign alliances are in view here.
notes.744: (tn): The Hebrew verb form is feminine singular, indicating that Oholibah (Judah) is specifically addressed here. This address continues through verse 42a (note “her”), but then both sisters are described in verse 42b, where the feminine pronouns are again plural.

rashi.heb:
*ואף כי תשלחנה.* 
וכל שכן קשה מן הכל כי תשלחנה להביא אליהן משרי העכו"ם אויביהן ורואין החלול שמחללות מקדשי:
rashi.eng: *And furthermore, that they would send.* [Heb. וְאַף כִּי.] And surely, worst of all is that they would send to bring to them [invite] some of the princes of the nations, their lovers, and these see the profanation with which they profane My sanctuary.

rashi.heb:
*שלוח אליהם וגו'.* 
מאת אהלה ואהליבה לבא אליהם:
rashi.eng: *to whom an emissary is sent, etc..* from Oholah and Oholibah to come to them.

rashi.heb:
*והנה באו לאשר רחצת כחלת וגו'.* 
לאשר תרגם יונתן לאתר אללו"א בלע"ז אל מקום אשר יעדת להם לאמר במקום פלוני נצא לקראתכם מקושטות במרחץ וכחול:
rashi.eng: *and behold they came to the place where you bathed, daubed, etc..* [Heb. לַאֲשֶׁר,] to which. Jonathan renders: לַאֲתַר, to the place, au lieu in Modern French. To the place that you designated for them, saying, “In such and such a place, we will come out to meet you, beautified by the bathing and the daubing.”

rashi.heb:
*כחלת.* 
מין צבע ושמו כחול וצובעות בו עיניהם אוקליר"א בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *daubed.* [Heb. כָּחַלְתָּ,] a kind of dye named כָּחוֹל, with which they color their eyes, ecler in Old French, to brighten.

rashi.heb:
*מטה כבודה.* 
מכוללת במצעות נאות פריד"י בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *a stately bed.* Adorned with all kinds of beautiful bedclothes, parede in Old French, adorned lavishly.

notes.746: (tn, Heb): “and men from the multitude of mankind.”
notes.747: (tn): An alternate reading is “drunkards.” Sheba is located in the area of modern day Yemen.
notes.748: (tn, Heb): “they”; the referents (the sisters) have been specified in the translation for the sake of clarity.

rashi.heb:
*וקול המון.* 
של עכו"ם רבות היו בה ולא המון של מלחמה אלא קול המון שליו:
rashi.eng: *And the sound of a multitude.* of many nanons were in her; not a multitude that came for war, but the voice of a tranquil multitude.

rashi.heb:
*ואל אנשים.* 
בשביל אנשים ושל אנשים היו אותו המון ולא של בהמה:
rashi.eng: *for the sake of men.* [Heb. אֶנָשִׁים וְאֶל,] for the sake of men. That multitude was of men, not of animals.

rashi.heb:
*מרוב אדם.* 
שהיו בתוכה המובאים לנאוף מן המדבר:
rashi.eng: *of the many people.* who were in her midst, who were brought to commit adultery, from the desert.

rashi.heb:
*סבאים.* 
שהיו דרין סביב לה משכיניה עמון ומואב וכן תרגום סבאים מסחור סחור:
rashi.eng: *those dwelling all around.* [Heb. סָבָאִים,] people who lived around her. Of her neighbors, Ammon and Moab, and so did [Jonathan] render סָבָאִים“from all around.”

rashi.heb:
*ויתנו.* 
אהלה ואהליבה צמידים אל ידיהן. להתקשט לנאוף כלומר עמון ומואב מתוך שהן רבים היא מתקשטת ומתפארת להם ומתוך שהם שכיניה מתפארת לעיניהם בקישוטיה לפיכך ויתנו אהלה ואהליבה צמידים על ידיהם כדי שיהו נאות בעיני הנואפים וי"ו של ויתנו יתירה כמו אותה של עזי וזמרת יה ויהי לי לישועה (שמות יד) וכמו אותך של ואשר לא שם לבו אל דבר ה' ויעזב (שם ט):
rashi.eng: *they placed.* Oholah and Oholibah [placed] bracelets on their hands to adorn themselves in order to commit adultery; i.e., Ammon and Moab, since they are many, she adorns and beautifies herself for them, and because they are her neighbors, she beautifies herself before their eyes with her ornaments; therefore, Oholah and Oholibah put bracelets on their hands in order to be beautiful in the eyes of the adulterers. The “vav” of וַיִתְּנוּ is superfluous, like that of (Exod. 15:2): “The strength and the cutting of God was (וַיְהִי) my salvation,” and like that of (ibid. 9:21): “But whoever did not take the word of the Lord to heart left (וַיַעֲזֹב).”

rashi.heb:
*ואומר לבלה נאופים.* 
עתה יזנו וגו' אמר לי לבי על זו שבלתה והזקינה בנאופים מעתה שהזקינה יזנו תזנותיה ממנה ותצא תאות זנותה מלבה ותחזור בה והרי היא עודנה בזנוניה כאשר בתחלה:
rashi.eng: *And I said of the one who had aged [in] adulteries, “Now her harlotries will end,” etc..* I said to Myself about this one who had become worn out and aged in her adulteries, “From now on, since she has aged, her harlotries will leave her, and the desires for her harlotry will leave her heart, and she will repent,” but she is still in her harlotries as in the beginning.

rashi.heb:
*יזנו.* 
יצאו כל זונה תרגום נפקת ברא כך שמעתי וכן ת"י:
rashi.eng: *will end.* [Heb. יִזְנוּ] will leave. Every “harlot” (זוֹנָה) is translated into Aramaic as נֳפְקֲתבְּרָא, one who goes out. So did I hear, and so did Jonathan render.

rashi.heb:
*לבלה נאופים.* 
כמו לבלה בנאופים כאשר תאמר ותשב בית אביה (בראשית לה) כמו בבית אביה ירחצו מים (שמות ל) כמו ירחצו במים ויצאה חנם (שם כא) ואם בית אישה נדרה (במדבר ל׳:י״א) וכן פירש דונש ומנחם חברו עם תבל עשו (ויקרא כ) ולא יתכנו דבריו:
rashi.eng: *of the one who had aged [in] adulteries.* like: [lit. to the one who had aged adulteries,] the one who had aged in adulteries, as you say (Gen. 38:11): “and she remained her father’s house,” is like “in her father’s house;” (Exod. 30:20), “they shall wash water,” is like “they shall wash with water.” [Likewise,] (ibid.): “And he shall go out freedom;” [and] (Num. 30:11): “But if she made a vow [in] her father’s house.” So did Dunash (p. 17) explain [this]. However, Menachem connected it (p. 45) to (Lev 20: 12): “they committed a disgraceful act (תֶּבֶל),” but his words are impossible.

rashi.heb:
*ויבוא אליה.* 
כל אשר מלאו לבו:
rashi.eng: *And he came to her.* whoever so desired

rashi.heb:
*אשות הזמה.* 
נשי הזמה:
rashi.eng: *the lewd women.* [Heb. אִשֹׁתהַזִמָּה,] [like] נְשֵׁי הַזִמָּה, women of lewdness.

notes.750: (tn, Heb): “and upright men will judge them (with) the judgment of adulteresses and the judgment of those who shed blood.”

rashi.heb:
*ואנשים צדיקים.* 
אנשים דיינים שרי מלך בבל ומלך אשור וי"ת זכאין בקיבליהון לפי מעשיהן של אלו הזונות צדיקים העכו"ם מהנה:
rashi.eng: *And righteous men.* Judges, the princes of the king of Babylon and the king of Assyria. But Jonathan renders: righteous, as compared to them. According to the deeds of these harlots, the nations are more righteous than they.

rashi.heb:
*משפט נאפות ומשפט שופכות דם.* 
כמו שמפורש אחריו:
rashi.eng: *the judgment of adulteresses, etc..* as is delineated further.

rashi.heb:
*העלה.* 
ונתון, וברא, כולן לשון עשה ופעול הם:
rashi.eng: *Let… be brought up… and let them be submitted.* All these are expressions of doing and of a continuous action.

rashi.heb:
*ורגמו עליהן אבן.* 
הריגת בניהן ובנותיהן ושריפת בתיהן הוא משפט נואפות:
rashi.eng: *shall pelt them with stone.* The slaying of their sons and daughters and the burning of their houses is the judgment of adulteresses.

rashi.heb:
*וברא אתהן בחרבותם.* 
הוא משפט שופכות דם וברא לשון קציצה וכן ובראתו דיער יהיה לך בספר (יהושע י״ז:י״ז):
rashi.eng: *and slash them with their swords.* That is the judgment of murderesses. [The word] וּבָרֵא is an expression of cutting, and so: “and you shall cut it down (וּבֵרֵאתוֹ),” of “the forest shall be yours” in the Book of Joshua (17:18).

notes.754: (tn, Heb): “and the sins of your idols you will bear.” By extension it can mean the punishment for the sins.

rashi.heb:
*ונתנו זמתכנה עליכן.* 
שופטיכן יתנו את משפט זמתכן בראשיכן:
rashi.eng: *And they shall put their lewdness upon you.* Your judges shall put the judgment of your lewdness on your heads.

notes.755: (tn): The date of this oracle was January 15, 588 b.c.

rashi.heb:
*התשיעית.* 
לצדקיהו:
rashi.eng: *in the ninth year.* of Zedekiah.

notes.757: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

rashi.heb:
*סמך מלך בבל.* 
היום צר עליה:
rashi.eng: *the king of Babylon has besieged.* Today he besieged it.

notes.758: (sn): The book of Ezekiel frequently refers to the Israelites as a rebellious house (Ezek 2:5, 6, 8; 3:9, 26-27; 12:2-3, 9, 25; 17:12; 24:3).

rashi.heb:
*שפות הסיר.* 
ע"פ הכירה במקום מושבה היא קרויה שפיתה בלשון המשנה שאמרו רבותינו מקום שפיתת שתי קדירות ועוד שנינו אחד שופת את הקדירה ואחד נותן לתוכה מים ואחד נותן לתוכה תבלין למדנו שהשפיתה היא הושבתה על פי הכירה עד שלא יתנו לתוכה כלום והדוגמא זו על ירושלים שאמרתם (לעיל) עליה היא הסיר עתה בא העת שתהיה לסיר ואתם בתוכה לבשר יבא נבוכדנצר ויתננה על האור, ומנחם פירש לשון שימה:
rashi.eng: *Set the pot.* [Heb. שְׂפֹת, set.] On the mouth of the stove on the place where it is set. That is called שְׂפִיתָה in Mishnaic Hebrew, for our Rabbis said (Shab. 38b): “[A stove has] a place for the setting of שְׂפִיתַת two pots.” We learned also (Beizah 34a): “If one sets the pot, one puts in water, and one puts in the condiments…” We learn that is the placing it on the mouth of the stove before they put anything into it. This figure represents Jerusalem, about which you said, “It is the pot.” Now the time has come for it to become a pot, and you will become the meat inside it, and Nebuchadnezzar is coming and will put in on the fire. Menachem (p. 179) explained it as an expression of placing.

rashi.heb:
*וגם יצוק בו מים.* 
הם צרכי המצור, יצוק כמו שפוך:
rashi.eng: *and also pour water into it.* These [represent] the accessories for the siege. יִצֹק is like שְׁפֹךְ, pour.

rashi.heb:
*אסוף נתחיה אליה.* 
מיראת המצור אספו לתוכה כל ראשיה ושריה:
rashi.eng: *Gather its pieces to it.* Out of fear of the siege, gather into it all its leaders and its princes.

rashi.heb:
*כל נתח טוב.* 
כל גבר גיבר אימתן וגבר עביד קרב כן ת"י:
rashi.eng: *every good piece.* Every mighty, awesome hero and every warrior.

rashi.heb:
*מבחר הצאן לקוח.* 
קח אתה נבוכדנצר את מבחר חייליך סביבותיה כן ת"י ואינו מיושב על ענין הסיר וכן צריך לפותרו מבחר ישראל יבאו ויכנסו בתוכה:
rashi.eng: *Take the choice of the flocks.* You, Nebuchadnezzar, take the choicest of your armies around it. So did Jonathan render, but this does not fit with the idea of the pot. This must therefore be interpreted to mean that the choicest of Israel will come and enter into its midst.

rashi.heb:
*וגם דור העצמים תחתיה.* 
סדר וערך העצמים תחת שאר האיברים כלומר ילחמו הגבורים בשביל החלשים ויסמכו אלו עליהן, דור לשון עריכה וכן יצנפך צנפה כדור (ישעיהו כ״ב:י״ח) שורות היקף גייסות וכן שורה תרגום דרא מנחם פירש כמו אני אגדיל המדורה:
rashi.eng: *and also arrange the limbs under it.* [Heb. דוּר,] an expression of arranging, and so (Isa. 22:18): “He shall wind you around like a turban, like a surrounding wall (כַּדוּר),” a row of surrounding troops. A row (דוּרָה) is translated into Aramaic as דַּרָא. However, Menachem explains it (p. 67) as (verse 9): “Even I shall enlarge the fire (הַמְדוּרָה).”

rashi.heb:
*רתח רתחיה.* 
ואחר שיהו כולם לתוכה יקרבו כלי המצור והמלחמה אל העיר:
rashi.eng: *make it boil well.* After they all are inside it, the siegeworks and the armaments will come near the city.

notes.762: (tn): Here “lot” may refer to the decision made by casting lots; it is not chosen at all.

rashi.heb:
*חלאתה.* 
זוהמתה שמוציאין מעל פיה על ידי הרתחתה שקורין אשקומ"א בלע"ז כלומר לא יצאו ממנה רשעים שבה:
rashi.eng: *and its filth.* Its filth, which they remove from its surface by boiling it, is called escume in Old French, foam, ecume in Modern French. This means: the wicked within her have not come out.

rashi.heb:
*לנתחיה לנתחיה.* 
גלות אחר גלות היוצא ונפל אל הכשדים איש איש לבדו:
rashi.eng: *limb by limb.* Exile after exile, who went out and defected to the Chaldeans, every man by himself.

rashi.heb:
*לא נפל עליה גורל.* 
לא כשאר קדירות שמוציאין נתחיהן יחד לתתה לפני כל אחד ואחד חלקו וגורלו ויונתן תרגם מדלא יתעביד בה תיובא לא נפל עליה גורלו של מקום:
rashi.eng: *no lot has fallen on it.* Not like other pots, whose pieces they take out all at once in order to place before each one his portion and his lot. Jonathan renders: because they did not repent within it. [Therefore,] the lot of the Omnipresent did not fall on it.

rashi.heb:
*צחיח.* 
שעיעות:
rashi.eng: *smooth.* [Heb. צְחִיחַ,] smoothness.

rashi.heb:
*לא שפכתהו על הארץ וגו'.* 
ת"י בזידו ובדרע מרומם שפכתיה לא שפכתיה בשלו למיעבד עלוהי תיובא, ורבותינו פירשוהו בדמו של זכריה בן יהוידע לא נהגו בו לא כדם הצבי ולא כדם האיל:
rashi.eng: *she did not pour it out on the ground, etc..* Jonathan paraphrased: with willful wickedness and with an arm raised on high did she shed it; she did not shed it unintentionally to repent of it. Our Rabbis (Git. 57b, Pesikta d’Rav Kahana 122a) explained it as referring to the blood of Zechariah the son of Jehoiada. They did not treat it as the blood of the deer or the blood of the gazelle.

rashi.heb:
*להעלות חמה.* 
לפני צויתי לאותו דם שלא יבלע בקרקע כדי שיזכר לנקום נקמתו:
rashi.eng: *So that it might bring up fury.* before Me. I [therefore (Etz Chaim ms.)] commanded that blood not to be absorbed into the ground, in order that it might be remembered, so that My vengeance might be taken.

rashi.heb:
*המדורה.* 
הסק גדולה פואיא"ה בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *the fire.* [Heb. הַמְדוּרָה,] a great kindling, foaie in Old French, a pyre.

rashi.heb:
*הרבה העצים הדלק האש.* 
להרבות העצים ולהדליק האש:
rashi.eng: *pile on the wood, kindle the fire.* And to pile on the wood, to kindle the fire, and to consume the meat.

rashi.heb:
*התם הבשר והרקח המרקחה.* 
כשהבשר חם מעל העצמות והוא מצטמק ומעורב ברוטב ומגיס בכף דומה למרקחת פטום סממנין שמערבין אותה יפה יפה ומתוך צימוק הבשר עשנה נהפך לתוכה שקורין אאורש"יר בלע"ז וזהו שאמר :
rashi.eng: *and prepare the mixture.* When the meat is consumed off the bones and it shrivels and becomes mingled with the liquid, and one stirs it with a spoon, it resembles a mixture of a compounding of spices, which they mix very thoroughly; and through the shriveling of the meat, its smoke is turned back into it, which is called aorser in Old French, to burn. And this is what [the following verse] says:

rashi.heb:
*העצמות יחרו.* 
יבשו ויעשנו לשון חרה מני חורב (איוב כ"ט) וכן למען תחם וחרה נחשתה כדרך קדירה שתמו מימיה ברתיחתה מתחממת ונשרפין חרסיה והתבשיל מתקלקל:
rashi.eng: *and the bones will be scorched.* [Heb. יִחָרוּ.] They will be cooked and smoked, an expression of (Job 30:30): “dried out (חָרָה) from the heat.” Similarly (verse 11), “in order that it be heated, that its base be scorched (וְחַרָה),” as happens with a pot whose water has evaporated through its boiling: it heats up, its shards burn, and the cooked food spoils.

notes.763: (tn, Heb): “set it upon its coals, empty.”

rashi.heb:
*תתום חלאתה.* 
תכלה זוהמתה ותבלע בנחשתה סיר של נחשת היא:
rashi.eng: *its filth shall be consumed.* [Heb. תִּתֻּם.] Its filth will end and be absorbed into its base. סִיר is [a pot] made of copper.

notes.765: (tn, Heb): “(with) toil she has wearied.” The meaning of the statement is unclear in the Hebrew text; some follow the LXX and delete it. The first word in the statement (rendered “toil” in the literal translation above) occurs only here in the OT, and the verb “she has wearied” lacks a stated object. Elsewhere the Hiphil of the verb refers to wearying someone or trying someone’s patience. The feminine subject is apparently the symbolic pot.
notes.767: (tn, Heb): “in fire its rust.” The meaning of the expression is unclear. The translation understands the statement as a command to burn the rust away. See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 1:768.

rashi.heb:
*תאונים הלאת.* 
בתואנה ותרמית הלאת את העניים לכן לא יצאו ממנה רשעי' שבתוכה אלא באש פורענותה יכלו:
rashi.eng: *With guile she wearied.* [Heb. תְּאֻנִים הֶלְאָת.] With pretext and guile, she wearied the poor. Therefore, the wicked in her midst will not leave her, but they will perish in the fire of her retribution.

notes.769: (tn, Heb): “because I cleansed you.” In this context (see especially the very next statement), the statement must refer to divine intention and purpose. Despite God’s efforts to cleanse his people, they resisted him and remained morally impure.
notes.770: (tn): The Hebrew text adds the word “again.”

rashi.heb:
*בטומאתך.* 
בטומאה של זמה תכלה:
rashi.eng: *With your defilement.* With defilement of lewdness you will perish.

rashi.heb:
*יען טיהרתיך.* 
להוכיח ע"פ הנביאים ולא טהרת וגו':
rashi.eng: *Since I purified you.* by reproving you through the prophets, and you did not become purified, etc.

notes.771: (tn, Heb): “it”; the referent has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.773: (tc): Some medieval Hebrew mss and the major ancient versions read a first person verb here. Most Hebrew mss read have an indefinite subject, “they will judge you,” which could be translated, “you will be judged.”

rashi.heb:
*לא אפרע.* 
לא אבטל גזירתי:
rashi.eng: *I shall not nullify.* [Heb. לֹא אֶפְרַע.] I shall not nullify My decree.

rashi.heb:
*ולא אנחם.* 
לשוב ממחשבתי הרעה אשר דברתי לעשות לך:
rashi.eng: *nor shall I renege.* [Heb. וְלֹא אֶנָחֵם,] to turn back from My plans of evil, which I said I would execute upon you.

rashi.heb:
*מחמד עיניך.* 
אשתך כמו שהענין מוכיח בסופו:
rashi.eng: *the desire of your eyes.* Your wife, as the context proves at the end [of the episode].

notes.776: (tn): Or “Groan silently. As to the dead….” Cf. M. Greenberg’s suggestion that דֹּם מֵתִים (dom metim) be taken together and דֹּם be derived from ָדּמַם (damam, “to moan, murmur”). See M. Greenberg, Ezekiel (AB), 2:508.
notes.777: (tn, Heb): “(For) the dead mourning you shall not conduct.” In the Hebrew text the word translated “dead” is plural, indicating that mourning rites are in view. Such rites would involve outward demonstrations of one’s sorrow, including wailing and weeping.
notes.778: (sn): The turban would normally be removed for mourning (Josh 7:6; 1 Sam 4:12).
notes.779: (sn): Mourning rites included covering the lower part of the face. See Lev 13:45.
notes.780: (tn, Heb): “the bread of men.” The translation follows the suggestion accepted by M. Greenberg (Ezekiel [AB], 2:509) that this refers to a meal brought by comforters to the one mourning. Some repoint the consonantal text to read “the bread of despair” (see L. C. Allen, Ezekiel [WBC], 2:56), while others, with support from the Targum and Vulgate, emend the consonantal text to read “the bread of mourners” (see D. I. Block, Ezekiel [NICOT], 1:784).

rashi.heb:
*האנק.* 
התמקמק בשתיקה שוא"ש דמוני"ץ בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *Melt.* [Heb. הֵאָנֵק,] melt in silence, soliles demoniz in Old French, to melt.

rashi.heb:
*פארך.* 
תפילין כל אלה מצות אבלים ואתה חילוף אבל אסור בתפילין וסנדל וחייב בעטיפת הראש ומברין אותו סעודה ראשונה משל אחרים:
rashi.eng: *your glory.* Tefillin. All these commandments are for mourners, but you shall do the opposite. A mourner is forbidden to wear tefillin or shoes, he is required to wrap his head, and they serve him the first meal from food belonging to others.

notes.781: (tn): This may refer to the following morning. For a discussion of various interpretive options in understanding the chronology reflected in verse 18, see D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 1:790.

rashi.heb:
*כאשר צויתי.* 
שלא לנהוג אבילות:
rashi.eng: *as I had been commanded.* not to observe mourning.

rashi.heb:
*מה אלה לנו.* 
מה הרמזים הללו עלינו:
rashi.eng: *what these mean to us.* What are these signs to us?

notes.782: (tn, Heb): “the pride of your strength” means “your strong pride.”
notes.783: (sn, Heb): “the delight of your eyes.” Just as Ezekiel was deprived of his beloved wife (v. 16, the “desire” of his “eyes”) so the Lord would be forced to remove the object of his devotion, the temple, which symbolized his close relationship to his covenant people.
notes.784: (tn, Heb): “the object of compassion of your soul.” The accentuation in the traditional Hebrew text indicates that the descriptive phrases (“the source of your confident pride, the object in which your eyes delight, and your life’s passion”) modify the preceding “my sanctuary.”

rashi.heb:
*אשר עזבתם.* 
בירושלים כשיצאתם בגולה:
rashi.eng: *whom you have left over.* in Jerusalem, when you went out into exile.

rashi.heb:
*ועשיתם כאשר עשיתי.* 
לא תנהגו אבילות כי אין מנחמין לכם שאין בכם אחד שלא יהיה אבל ואין אבילות אלא במקום מנחמים, ד"א שתהיו יראים לבכות לפני הכשדים שאתם בתוכם:
rashi.eng: *And you shall do as I have done.* You shall not observe mourning because you have no consolers, for no one among you is not a mourner, and there is no mourning except where there are consolers. Another explanation: For you will be afraid to weep before the Chaldeans in whose midst you are.

rashi.heb:
*שפם.* 
גרינו"ן בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *upper lip.* [Heb. שָּׁפָם,] grenon in Old French, moustache.

notes.787: (tn): The same verb appears in 4:17 and 33:10.
notes.788: (tn): Or “in your punishment.” The phrase “in/for [a person’s] iniquity/punishment” occurs fourteen times in Ezekiel: here; 3:18, 19; 4:17; 7:13, 16; 18:17, 18, 19, 20; 33:6, 8, 9; 39:23. The Hebrew word for “iniquity” may also mean the “punishment” for iniquity or “guilt” of iniquity.

rashi.heb:
*ונמקותם.* 
אישרויי"ץ דמוני"ץ בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *and you will melt.* [Heb. וּנְמַקֹתֶם,] esere(y)z demoniz, and you will collapse.

rashi.heb:
*בבואה.* 
באה הרעה הזאת:
rashi.eng: *when it comes.* When this evil comes.

notes.789: (tn, Heb): “(Will) it not (be) in the day I take?”
notes.790: (tn, Heb): “the uplifting of their soul.” According to BDB 672 s.v. מַשָּׂא 2, the term “uplifting” refers to “that to which they lift up their soul, their heart’s desire.” However, this text is the only one listed for this use. It seems more likely that the term has its well-attested nuance of “burden, load,” here and refers to that which weighs them down emotionally and is a constant source of concern or worry.
notes.791: (tn): In the Hebrew text there is no conjunction before “their sons and daughters.” For this reason one might assume that the preceding descriptive phrases refer to the sons and daughters, but verse 21 suggests otherwise. The descriptive phrases appear to refer to the “stronghold,” which parallels “my sanctuary” in verse 21. The children constitute a separate category.

rashi.heb:
*משא נפשם.* 
שנפשם מתנשאה בהם:
rashi.eng: *the pride of their soul.* [Heb. מַשָׂא נַפְשָׂם.] Their soul is uplifted through them.

rashi.heb:
*ביום ההוא.* 
א"א לבא הפליט ביום החורבן וכן פתרונו ביום ההוא שיבא הפליט אליך להשמיע אזנך ביום ההוא יפתח פיך:
rashi.eng: *On that day.* It is impossible for the fugitive to come on the day of the destruction. Therefore this is the meaning: On that day, [on the day] that the fugitive will come to you to let you hear with your own ears, on that day, your mouth will be opened.

rashi.heb:
*להשמעות אזנים.* 
לבשר בשורה שהוכתה העיר:
rashi.eng: *to let you hear with your own ears.* To announce the news that the city has been struck.

rashi.heb:
*את הפליט.* 
עם הפליט:
rashi.eng: *with the fugitive.* [Heb. אֶתהַפָּלִים,] with the fugitive.

rashi.heb:
*ותדבר ולא תאלם.* 
לפי שאמרתי לך ונאלמת ולא תהיה להם וגו' מעתה יראו שדבריך אמת ולא תאלם עוד מהתנבאות להם:
rashi.eng: *and you will speak and no longer be mute.* Because I said to you (3:26): “and you shall become mute, and you shall not be, etc.” From now on, they will see that your words are true, and you will no longer be mute from prophesying to them.

notes.795: (tn, Heb): “the sons of Ammon.” Ammon was located to the east of Israel.

rashi.heb:
*האח.* 
לשון שמחה:
rashi.eng: *Aha!.* An expression of joy.

rashi.heb:
*כי נחל.* 
כי ננחל והיה מורשה לאחרים:
rashi.eng: *because it was possessed.* [Heb. נִחָל.] Because it was possessed (נִנְחָל) and became an inheritance for others.

notes.796: (tn): The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) indicates being aware of or taking notice of something and has been translated here with a verb (so also throughout the chapter).
notes.797: (tn, Heb): “Look I am about to give you for a possession to.”

rashi.heb:
*לבני קדם.* 
כשדים וארם לצד מזרח הם:
rashi.eng: *to the children of the East.* The Chaldeans and Aram are to the east.

notes.800: (tn, Heb): “with all your scorn in (the) soul.”

rashi.heb:
*יען מחאך יד ורקעך ברגל.* 
לשם שמחה ואע"פ שבראש הספר (לעיל ו) אמר כן לענין אבל הכה בכפך ורקע ברגליך ואמור האח יש דברים שעושין אותם לאבל ולשמחה אבל אין עניינם שוה וכן חלילים לכלה ולמת:
rashi.eng: *Because you clapped with your hand and stamped with your foot.* for joy. Although he said this at the beginning of the Book in reference to mourning (6:11): “Strike with your hand and stamp with your foot, and say, Ah!” there are things that are done for [both] mourning and joy, but the idea behind them is not the same. Similarly, flutes for a bride and for the dead.

rashi.heb:
*ורקעך.* 
לשון מרפס:
rashi.eng: *and stamped.* [Heb. וְרַקְעֲךָ,] an expression of stamping.

rashi.heb:
*בכל שאטך.* 
לשון בזיון פותרין בו כמו ויבז עשו (בראשית כ״ה:ל״ד) שתרגום אונקלוס ושאט עשו ואני אומר שאט לשון שטף גולוזמנ"ט בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *with all the disdain.* [Heb. שָּׁאטְךָ,] interpreted as an expression of disdain, like (Gen. 25:34): “and Esau despised,” which Onkelos renders: וְשָׁט, but I say that שָּׁאטְךָ is an expression of lust, golozemant or golosement in Old French, ardent desire, gluttony.

notes.801: (tc): The translation here follows the marginal reading (Qere) of the Hebrew text. The consonantal text (Kethib) is meaningless.

notes.802: (sn): Moab was located immediately south of Ammon.

rashi.heb:
*הנה ככל הגוים בית יהודה.* 
בטלה אהבת הקב"ה מהם ונמאסו לתת ביד נבוכדנצר כשאר העכו"ם ומדרש אגדה שנכנסו להיכל וקפלו צורות הכרובים שצר שלמה על קיר ההיכל כמער איש ולויות (מלכים א ז׳:ל״ו) והוציאום לחוץ אמרו ראו אלו שהיו מראים עצמם כצנועים במה היו עוסקין:
rashi.eng: *Behold the house of Judah is like all the nations.* The love of the Holy One, blessed be He, has been annulled from them, and they are rejected, to be given into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar like the other nations. The Midrash Aggadah (see Lam. Rabbah, Proem 9) [says] that they entered the Temple and peeled off the pictures of the cherubim that Solomon had painted on the wall of the Temple (I Kings 7:36): “according to the attachment of a man and the joining, etc.” They took them outside and said, “Look at what these [Jews], who were showing themselves as decent people, were occupied with.”

notes.804: (tn, Heb): “from the cities.” The verb “eliminating” has been added in the translation to reflect the privative use of the preposition (see BDB 583 s.v. מִן 7.b).
notes.805: (tn, Heb): “from its cities, from its end.”

rashi.heb:
*הנני פותח.* 
את מבצרי ארץ מואב אשר בספר בסוף גבולם הוא הכתף סוף גבול ארצם כמו (שמות כ״ז:ט״ו) ולכתף השנית אל הכתף דמתרגם לעיברא:
rashi.eng: *behold I will expose.* the fortresses of the land of Moab that are on the border at the end of their boundary; that is the flank, the end of the boundary of their land, like (Exod. 27:15): “And on the other side,” to the flank, which Targum [Jonathan] translates לְעִיבְרָא, to the side.

notes.806: (tn, Heb): “I will give it for a possession.”
notes.807: (tn, Heb): “the sons of Ammon” (twice in this verse).

rashi.heb:
*לבני קדם.* 
אפתה אותם שיבאו על בני עמון דרך ארץ מואב:
rashi.eng: *To the children of the East.* I will expose them so that they should come upon the children of Ammon through the land of Moab.

notes.809: (sn): Edom was located south of Moab.
notes.810: (tn, Heb): “and they have become guilty, becoming guilty.” The infinitive absolute following the finite verb makes the statement emphatic and draws attention to the degree of guilt incurred by Edom due to its actions.
notes.812: (sn): Edom apparently in some way assisted in the destruction of Jerusalem in 587/6 b.c. (Ps 137:7; Lam 5:21, 23; Joel 3:19; Obadiah).

notes.813: (tn, Heb): “and I will cut off from her man and beast.”

rashi.heb:
*ודדנה.* 
ויתבי דדן:
rashi.eng: *and Dedan.* [Heb. וּדְדָנֶה,] the inhabitants of Dedan.

rashi.heb:
*ביד עמי ישראל.* 
הם יהיו שלוחי לנקום נקמתי:
rashi.eng: *by the hand of My people Israel.* They will be My agents to wreak My vengeance.

notes.816: (sn): The Philistines inhabited the coastal plain by the Mediterranean Sea, west of Judah.
notes.817: (tn, Heb): “have acted with vengeance and taken vengeance with vengeance.” The repetition emphasizes the degree of vengeance which they exhibited, presumably toward Judah.
notes.819: (tn): The object is not specified in the Hebrew text, but has been clarified as “Judah” in the translation.
notes.820: (tn, Heb): “to destroy (with) perpetual hostility.” Joel 3:4-8 also speaks of the Philistines taking advantage of the fall of Judah.

rashi.heb:
*יען עשות פלשתים בנקמה.* 
בשנאה ובפרך כאדם הנוקם נקמתו באויבו:
rashi.eng: *Because the Philistines acted with vengeance.* With hatred and with rigor, like a man who wreaks vengeance upon his enemy.

notes.821: (tn): In Hebrew the verb “and I will cut off” sounds like its object, “the Cherethites,” and draws attention to the statement.
notes.822: (sn): This is a name for the Philistines, many of whom migrated to Palestine from Crete.

rashi.heb:
*את כרתים.* 
עמא דחייבין לאישתיצאה ואומר אני לפי שראיתי במקום אחר קורא אל פלשתים כרתים היו יושבי חבל הים גוי כרתים (צפניה ב׳:ה׳) ואינו קורא כן לאומה אחרת נראה בעיני שיש גבול בפלשתים ששמו כרתי וכן אני מוצא בספר (שמואל (א' ל') בגדוד ששרף את צקלג אנחנו פשטנו על נגב הכרתי:
rashi.eng: *the Cherethites.* [Heb. כְּרֵתִים,] a nation deserving of being cut off (Targum). But I say, because I saw elsewhere that Scripture calls the Philistines כְּרֵתִים (Zeph. 2:5): “Woe to the inhabitants of the seacoast, the nation of (כְּרֵתִים),” and it does not give any other nation this appellation, it appears to me that there is a region of Philistia called Chereth, and so I find in the Book of (I) Samuel (30:14), concerning the group that set fire to Ziklag: “We made a raid on the south of the Cherethites.”

rashi.heb:
*חוף הים.* 
מארק"א בלע"ז הם פלשתים שיושבים במקצוע דרומית מערבית של גבול ארץ ישראל על הים האחרון:
rashi.eng: *the seacoast.* [Heb. חוֹף הַיָם,] marche in Old French, frontier, borderland. They are Philistines, who live in the southwestern corner of the land of Israel on the Western (Mediterranean) Sea.

notes.823: (tn, Heb): “with acts of punishment of anger.”

notes.824: (tc): Date formulae typically include the month. According to D. I. Block (Ezekiel [NICOT], 2:34, n. 27) some emend to “in the twelfth year in the eleventh month” based partially on the copy of the LXX from Alexandrinus, where Albright suggested that “eleventh month” may have dropped out due to haplography. April 23, 587 b.c.

rashi.heb:
*בעשתי עשרה.* 
לצדקיהו:
rashi.eng: *in the eleventh [year].* of Zedekiah.

notes.825: (sn): Tyre was located on the Mediterranean coast north of Israel.
notes.826: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

rashi.heb:
*על ירושלים.* 
שהיתה במצור:
rashi.eng: *Jerusalem.* which was under siege.

rashi.heb:
*האח.* 
לשון קול שמחה:
rashi.eng: *Aha!.* [Heb. הֶאָח,] an expression of a shout of joy.

rashi.heb:
*נשברה דלתות העמים.* 
עיר שכל העכו"ם היו נכנסים לה לסחורה מעתה תשבר כי לא ילך המצור מעליה עד תלכד:
rashi.eng: *The doors of the peoples have been broken.* A city through which all the nations enter for commerce will now be broken, for the siege will not leave it until it is taken.

rashi.heb:
*נסבה אלי.* 
מעתה הוסבה סחורות העמים אלי:
rashi.eng: *it has turned to me.* From now on, the merchandise of the nations has turned on me.

rashi.heb:
*אמלאה החרבה.* 
אתמלא אני מן העיר ירושלים החרבה:
rashi.eng: *I shall become full from the destroyed [city].* I shall become full from the destroyed city of Jerusalem.

notes.829: (tn): The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) draws attention to something and has been translated here as a verb.
notes.830: (tn): Or “I challenge you.” The phrase “I am against you” may be a formula for challenging someone to combat or a duel. See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 1:201-2, and P. Humbert, “Die Herausforderungsformel ‘h!nn#n' ?l?K>,’” ZAW 45 (1933): 101-8. The Hebrew text switches to a second feminine singular form here, indicating that personified Jerusalem is addressed (see vv. 5-6a). The address to Jerusalem continues through v. 15. In vv. 16-17 the second masculine plural is used, as the people are addressed.

rashi.heb:
*וסחיתי.* 
ועקרתי כמו בית גאים יסח ה' (משלי ט״ו:כ״ה) ונסחתם מעל (דברים כח):
rashi.eng: *and I shall remove.* [Heb. וְסִחֵיתִי,] and I shall uproot, like (Prov. 15:25): “The Lord will uproot (יִסַח) the house of the haughty;” (Deut. 28:63); “and you will be uprooted (וְנִסַחְתֶם) from…”

rashi.heb:
*לצחיח סלע.* 
לפי שהיתה בנויה בסלע בתוך הים כשתנתץ ויסח עפרה אל הים נשאר הסלע חלק וכן ת"י לשעיעות כיף גלי:
rashi.eng: *a smooth rock.* Since it was built on a rock in the midst of the sea, when it will be demolished and its earth will be uprooted into the sea, the rock will be left bare, and so did Jonathan render: a smooth, bare rock.

rashi.heb:
*משטח חרמים.* 
על הסלע ישטחו הדייגים את חרמי מכמרותם לנגבם:
rashi.eng: *a place to spread out nets.* On the rock the fishermen will spread out their fishing nets, to dry them.

notes.832: (sn): That is, the towns located inland that were under Tyre’s rule.

rashi.heb:
*ובנותיה אשר בשדה.* 
הכפרים המשועבדות לה סביבותיה:
rashi.eng: *And her daughters that are in the field.* the villages that are subservient to her, surrounding her.

notes.833: (tn): The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) draws attention to something.
notes.834: (tn, Heb): “Nebuchadrezzar” is a variant and more correct spelling of Nebuchadnezzar, as the Babylonian name Nabu-kudurri-usur has an an “r” rather than an “n.”

rashi.heb:
*והקים עליך צנה.* 
ויקים עליך די מזיינין בתרסין:
rashi.eng: *and will station against you shields.* [Heb. צִנָה,] and will station against you those armed with shields.

rashi.heb:
*ומחי קבלו.* 
הוא אחד מתחבולות המצור לזרוק אבנים גדולות ומכה כנגדו אילקולי"אה דשאפורי"ירא בלע"ז ויש לועזים קבלו דשארבלי"טא בלעז ויש לועזין פוריירא בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *And… his catapult.* [Heb. וּמְחִי קָבָלוֹ.] This is one of the devices of the siege, to throw huge rocks and to strike opposite it, e la hone de sa pereyre in Old French, and the striking of his stone-throwing machine. Others render קָבָלוֹ as desarbalete in Old French, of his war-machines.

rashi.heb:
*בחרבותיו.* 
באומנות חורבן שיביא עמו:
rashi.eng: *with his instruments of destruction.* [Heb. בְּחַרְבּוֹתָיו,] with tools of destruction that he will bring with him.

notes.836: (tn, Heb): “From the abundance of his horses he will cover you (with) their dust.”
notes.837: (tn, Heb): “like those who enter a breached city.”

rashi.heb:
*משפעת סוסיו.* 
כשיש סוסים הרבה מעלים אבק ברגליהם ועולה ונעשה כענן ומחשיך הארץ הוא קרוי שפעת וכן ושפעת מים תכסך (איוב כב) דלאפוי"שון בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *From the abundance of his horses.* When there are many horses, they raise dust with their feet, which ascends and becomes like a cloud, darkening the earth. This is called שִּׁפְּעַת, an abundance. Similarly, (Job 22:11): “or an abundance of (וְשִּׁפְּעַת) water covers you,” de la foison in French, of abundance.

rashi.heb:
*כמבוא עיר מבוקעה.* 
כמה דעלין לקרתי דמתרעא משור שנפרצה חומתה:
rashi.eng: *as men enter a breached city.* as they enter a city that has been breached of its wall (Targum), that its wall has been breached.

notes.840: (tn, Heb): “into the midst of the water.”

rashi.heb:
*רכולתך.* 
סחורתך:
rashi.eng: *your merchandise.* [as translated], your merchandise.

notes.842: (sn): This prophecy was fulfilled by Alexander the Great in 332 b.c.

notes.844: (tn, Heb): “and they will be astonished over you.”

rashi.heb:
*וחרדו לרגעים.* 
לשברים פן יבא עליהם גם הם כשברך:
rashi.eng: *and they will tremble for [fear of] destruction.* [Heb. לִרְגָעִים,] for fear of destruction, lest it befall them like your destruction.

rashi.heb:
*לרגעים.* 
לשון שבר כמו (ישעיה נא) רוגע הים עורי רגע (איוב כו) על רגעי ארץ (תהלים לה) על דכאי ארץ ומנחם פירשו לשון רגע כמו כי רגע באפו (שם ל):
rashi.eng: *destruction.* לִרְגָעִים as is an expression of breaking, like (Isa. 51:15): “Who splits (ַרוֹגַע) the sea;” (Job 7:5), “my skin split (רָגַע);” (Ps. 35:20), “and against the crushed people of (רִגְעֵי) the earth,” [synonymous with] דִכְּאֵי “the crushed people of the earth.” Menachem, however, explained it (p. 162) in the sense of רֶגַע, a moment, as in (Ps. 30:6): “For His wrath lasts but a moment (רֶגַע).”

rashi.heb:
*ושממו.* 
לשון תמהון:
rashi.eng: *and will be appalled.* [Heb. וְשָּׁמְמוּ,] an expression of bewilderment.

notes.845: (tn, Heb): “and they will lift up over you a lament and they will say to you.”
notes.846: (tn, Heb): “O inhabitant.” The translation follows the LXX and understands a different Hebrew verb, meaning “cease,” behind the consonantal text. See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel [WBC], 2:72, and D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 2:43.
notes.847: (tn, Heb): “she and her inhabitants who placed their terror to all her inhabitants.” The relationship of the final prepositional phrase to what precedes is unclear. The preposition probably has a specifying function here, drawing attention to Tyre’s inhabitants as the source of the terror mentioned prior to this. In this case, one might paraphrase verse 17b: “she and her inhabitants, who spread their terror; yes, her inhabitants (were the source of this terror).”

rashi.heb:
*נושבת מימים.* 
יש נוקדין רפי ופותרין מיושבת מימים קדמונים ויש נוקדים דגש ופותרין מיושבת בחזקה על ידי ימים הסובבים לה וכן תרגם יונתן וכן הוא:
rashi.eng: *established from the seas.* [Heb. מִיָמִּים.] Some vocalize it without a “dagesh” (מִיָמִים) and interpret it to mean “settled from days of yore,” and others punctuate it with a “dagesh” (מִיַמִּים) and interpret it to mean “settled with strength through the seas surrounding her,” and so it is.

rashi.heb:
*אשר נתנו חתיתם.* 
סביבות לכל היושבים:
rashi.eng: *who cast terror.* around to all the inhabitants.

rashi.heb:
*חתיתם.* 
לורדפריימ"נט בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *terror.* Heb. חִתִּיתָם, lur defre[n] emant in Old French, their terror.

rashi.heb:
*האין.* 
כמו האיים:
rashi.eng: *the isles.* [Heb. הָאִיִן,] like הָאִייִם.

rashi.heb:
*מצאתך.* 
מיציאתך בגולה:
rashi.eng: *by your departure.* by your departure into exile.

rashi.heb:
*בהעלות עליך את תהום.* 
באסקותי עליך משריית עממין דסגיאין כמו תהומא ויחפונך עממין סגיאין כן ת"י וכמשמעו בתחלה נתנה ביד נבוכדנצר וסוף עלה הים וטבעה:
rashi.eng: *when [I] bring up the deep upon you.* “When I bring upon you companies of nations as numerous as the waters of the deep, and many nations will cover you.” Jonathan translated it in this manner, but according to its apparent meaning, first it was given into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar, and ultimately, the sea came up and inundated it.

notes.851: (tn, Heb): “like.” The translation assumes an emendation of the preposition כְּ (k�, “like”), to בְּ (b�, “in, among”).
notes.852: (tn, Heb): “and I will place beauty.” This reading makes little sense; many, following the lead of the LXX, emend the text to read “nor will you stand” with the negative particle before the preceding verb understood by ellipsis; see L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:73. D. I. Block (Ezekiel [NICOT], 2:47) offers another alternative, taking the apparent first person verb form as an archaic second feminine form and translating “nor radiate splendor.”

rashi.heb:
*את יורדי בור.* 
עם יורדי גיהנם:
rashi.eng: *with those who descend into the Pit.* with those who descend into Gehinnom.

rashi.heb:
*אל עם עולם.* 
עם שאר העכו"ם אשר שם מעולם:
rashi.eng: *to a people of old.* with the other nations who are there from long ago.

rashi.heb:
*כחרבות מעולם.* 
כערים אשר חרבו מאז כסדום וחברותיה:
rashi.eng: *like the ruins of old.* like the cities that were destroyed from times of yore, viz. Sodom and her sister cities.

rashi.heb:
*ונתתי צבי בארץ חיים.* 
ואתן התפארת בירושלי':
rashi.eng: *but I shall bestow beauty upon the land of the living.* And I shall bestow beauty upon Jerusalem.

rashi.heb:
*בלהות.* 
פרשו יונתן בלהות כדלא הוית והפותרים אומרים ל' מקום מרקד שעירי' ומזיקי':
rashi.eng: *a nonentity.* [Heb. בַּלָהוֹת.] Jonathan explained בַּלָהוֹת [as] as if you did not exist, and the exegetes explain it as a word for a place where the satyrs and demons dance.

notes.853: (tn, Heb): “lift up over Tyre a lament.”

notes.854: (tn, Heb): “entrances.” The plural noun may reflect the fact that Tyre had two main harbors.
notes.855: (sn): Rome, another economic power, is described in a similar way in Rev 17:1.

rashi.heb:
*על מבואות ים.* 
על הנמל שהספינות באות עד החומה והשערים והרבה כרכין יושבין על הים ואינה מקום נמל ואין הספינות יכולות לקרב אליהם:
rashi.eng: *on the seaport.* [Heb. מְבוֹאֹתיָם, lit. by the entrance of the sea.] By the port where the ships come up to the wall and the gates. Many large cities are situated by the sea, but they are not a [good] place for a port, and the ships cannot approach them.

rashi.heb:
*מבואות ים.* 
פור"ט בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *the seaport.* מְבוֹאֹתיָם is port in Old French, seaport.

rashi.heb:
*רוכלת העמים.* 
כך היה מנהגם סוחרים הבאים לה זה מצפון וזה מדרום לא היו רשאין לעשות סחורה זה עם זה אלא יושבי העיר לוקחין מזה ומוכרין לזה:
rashi.eng: *trafficker of the peoples.* So was their custom: the merchants who came there this one from the north, that one from the south were not allowed to conduct commerce with one another. Rather, the inhabitants of the city would purchase from this one and sell to that one.

rashi.heb:
*את אמרת אני כלילת יופי.* 
עד עכשיו הכל אומרי' על ירושלים כלילת יופי (איכה ב׳:ט״ו-ט״ז) משוש כל הארץ (תהילים מ״ח:ג׳) עכשיו את מתגאה לומר אני כלילת היופי סוף גמר היופי כלול בי:
rashi.eng: *you said, I am the perfection of beauty.* Until now, all [were] saying about Jerusalem (Lam. 2: 15): “the perfection of beauty” ; (ibid.) “the joy of all the earth.” Now you boast, saying, “I am the perfection of beauty,” the ultimate extreme of beauty is incorporated in me.

notes.856: (tn): The city of Tyre is described in the following account as a merchant ship.

rashi.heb:
*בוניך.* 
ארדכלייך, ל' בנין:
rashi.eng: *your builders.* [Heb. בֹּנַיִךּ,] your architects, from the word בִּנְיָן, building.

notes.858: (tn): Perhaps the hull or deck. The term is dual, so perhaps it refers to a double-decked ship.

rashi.heb:
*ברושים משניר.* 
לפי שהיתה בנויה בים ובים אבדה המשילה הנביא לספינה משובחת שהכבידו משאה בתוכה וטבעה ברוח קדים:
rashi.eng: *junipers from Senir.* Since it was built on the sea and was destroyed by the sea, the prophet compares it to a superior ship whose cargo in its hold was too heavy for it, and which sank by the east wind.

rashi.heb:
*משניר.* 
טור תלגא:
rashi.eng: *from Senir.*

rashi.heb:
*את כל לוחתים.* 
הלוחים שנעשית האניה מהם:
rashi.eng: *all the planks.* the planks from which the ship was made.

rashi.heb:
*ארז מלבנון.* 
שם יער שהארזים מצויין בו:
rashi.eng: *cedars from Lebanon.* the name of the forest where the cedars are prevalent.

rashi.heb:
*תורן.* 
הוא העץ הזקוף וגבוה התקוע בספינה שבו תולין המפרש שקורין בוייל"א בלע"ז ובו נקבים בראשו שהחבל שמושכין בו הספינה נכנס ויוצא בו מש"ט בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *a mast.* [Heb. תֹּרֶן.] This is the tall, upright pole that is thrust into the ship, upon which they hang the sail, which is called voile in French. Also, there are holes at its top, through which is drawn the rope by which they pull the ship. [“Pole” is] mast in Old French.

notes.860: (tc): The Hebrew reads “Your deck they made ivory, daughter of Assyria.” The syntactically difficult “ivory” is understood here as dittography and omitted, though some construe this to refer to ivory inlays. “Daughter of Assyria” is understood here as improper word division and the vowels repointed as “cypresses.”
notes.861: (tn): Heb “from the coastlands (or islands) of Kittim,” generally understood to be a reference to the island of Cyprus, where the Phoenicians had a trading colony on the southeast coast. Many modern English versions have “Cyprus” (CEV, TEV), “the coastlands of Cyprus” (NASB), “the coasts of Cyprus” (NIV, NRSV), or “the southern coasts of Cyprus” (NLT). The Kittean isles is probably a reference to southeast Cyprus where the Phoenicians had a colony.

rashi.heb:
*אלונים.* 
מן עץ סרק שקורין קיישנ"א בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *oaks.* [Heb. אַלוֹנִים,] a kind of tree that does not produce fruit, chesne in Old French.

rashi.heb:
*משוטיך.* 
הם שרחבים בראשם שמנהיגין בהם האניה ריימ"ש בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *your oars.* [Heb. מִשּׁוֹטָיִם.] They are the boards that are wide at the end, with which they guide the ship, rames in French.

rashi.heb:
*קרשך.* 
הוא הקרש הרחב שבראש השני של ספינה אל מול התורן שבראשה אשר בו מהפכין את הספינה לכל צדדיה ומכוונין אותה אל הדרך ורב החובל אוחז בו ובלשון משנה קברניט ובלשון לעז גובריינא"ל:
rashi.eng: *your rudder.* [Heb. קַרְשֵּׁך, lit. your board.] This is the wide board at the second end of the ship, opposite the mast at the other end, with which they steer the ship in all directions and direct it on its course, and the captain holds it. In the language of the Mishnah (B. B. 91a) קְבַרְנִיט, and in French gouvernail, rudder.

rashi.heb:
*עשו שן בת אשורים.* 
א"א לו להיות אלא של עץ וזהו בת אשורים כאלו הוא תיבה אחת לשון תדהר ותאשור (ישעיהו מ״א:י״ט) שניהם ת"י אשכרועין ואת קברניטה של צור המשיל לקרש של אשכרוע מצופה בשן ע"י מסמרים לנוי ולחוזק כי כן תרגם יונתן דפין דאשכרועין מכבשין בשן דפיל בית חופאה לא תיטרון כסויה לא יפול אבל יונתן פירש הקברניט הזה לפי עניין העיר על קרשי שעריה:
rashi.eng: *they made of ivory inlaid in cypresses.* [Heb. שֵּׁן בַּת-אֵשֻּׁרִים.] It is impossible for it to be of anything but wood, and this is בּתאשּׁרים, as if it were one word, an expression of (Isa 41:19): “firs and cypresses (וּתְאַשּׁוּר).” Both of them, Jonathan rendered אֶשּׁכְּרוֹעִן. He compares the rudder of Tyre to a rudder of cypress inlaid with ivory [and] with nails for beauty and strength, for so did Jonathan render: boards of cypresses inlaid with ivory, בֵּיתחוֹפָאָה לְאִתְיָטְרוּן, so that its cover should not fall. However, Jonathan explained this rudder as applying to the city, concerning the boards of its gates.

notes.862: (sn): This is probably a reference to Cyprus.

rashi.heb:
*שש ברקמה.* 
נגד שש עשוי בציורי רקמות:
rashi.eng: *Linen with embroidery.* linen cloth made with pictures and embroideries.

rashi.heb:
*מפרשך.* 
הוא שקורין בל"א סיג"ל ובלשונינו בווייל"א בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *your sail.* [Heb. מִפְרָשֵּׂךּ,] that which is called voile in French, a sail.

rashi.heb:
*להיות לך לנס.* 
לפורשו על כלונס הארז ולהגביהו על התורן, נס בלשון משנה כלונס ובלע"ז פורקא:
rashi.eng: *to be to you for a staff.* to spread it on the pole of cedar and to raise it on the mast. נֵס is in the language of the Mishnah כְּלוֹנֵס, and in French perche, pole, rod.

rashi.heb:
*היה מכסך.* 
לאהל ולגג על פני כל האניה:
rashi.eng: *was your covering.* as a tent and a roof over the entire surface of the ship.

notes.863: (tc): The MT reads “the residents of”; the LXX reads “your rulers who dwell in.” With no apparent reason for the LXX to add “the rulers” many suppose something has dropped out of the Hebrew text. While more than one may be possible, Allen’s proposal, positing a word meaning “elders,” is the most likely to explain the omission in the MT from a graphic standpoint and also provides a parallel to the beginning of v. 9. See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:81.a parallel to v. 9.
notes.864: (map): For location see Map1-A1; JP3-F3; JP4-F3.
notes.865: (sn): Sidon and Arvad, like Tyre, were Phoenician coastal cities.

rashi.heb:
*היו שטים לך.* 
תופסי משוטיך להנהיגך:
rashi.eng: *were your oarsmen.* [Heb. שָּׁטִים,] those who hold your oars to guide you.

rashi.heb:
*חובליך.* 
אוחזי הקברניט לכוין וליישר האניה:
rashi.eng: *your mariners.* those who hold the rudder to direct and straighten the ship.

notes.867: (sn): Another Phoenician coastal city located between Sidon and Arvad.
notes.868: (tn, Heb): “strengthening damages.” Here “to strengthen” means to repair. The word for “damages” occurs several times in 1 Kgs 12 about some type of damage to the temple, which may have referred to or included cracks. Since the context describes Tyre in its glory, we do not expect this reference to damages to be of significant scale, even if there are repairmen. This may refer to using pitch to seal the seams of the ship, which had to be done periodically and could be considered routine maintenance rather than repair of damage.
notes.869: (sn): The reference to “all the ships of the sea…within you” suggests that the metaphor is changing; previously Tyre had been described as a magnificent ship, but now the description shifts back to an actual city. The “ships of the sea” were within Tyre’s harbor. Verse 11 refers to “walls” and “towers” of the city.

rashi.heb:
*זקני גבל.* 
אומני הבנין כמו שנאמר ובוני חירום והגבלים (מלכים א ה׳:ל״ב):
rashi.eng: *The elders of Gebal.* [who were] skillful builders, as it is said (I Kings 5:32): “and Hiram’s builders and the Gebalites.”

rashi.heb:
*מחזיקי בדקך.* 
מתקני בדקך שלא יכנסו בהם המים אפייטונ"ט טאקראוצ"א בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *who repaired your cracks.* [Heb. מַחַזִיקִי, lit. strengthen,] repaired your cracks so that no water should enter them, apiye[ce] tans ta crevaze in Old French, repairing your crack.

rashi.heb:
*כל אניות הים ומלחיהם.* 
הספנים שלהם:
rashi.eng: *all the ships of the sea and their mariners.* [Heb. וּמַלָחֵיהֶם,] their sailors.

rashi.heb:
*היו בך.* 
היו סביבך לשוט אל המדינות הרחוקות להביא הסחור' לתוכך:
rashi.eng: *were within you.* They were around you to sail to the distant countries to bring the merchandise into your midst.

rashi.heb:
*לערוב מערבך.* 
ל' ערובה הם כל צורכי האדם שהוא חי בהם וממונו הוא ערובתו והצלתו לחייו גרנטיא"ה בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *to guarantee your necessities.* [Heb. לַעֲרֹב מַעֲרָבֵךּ,] an expression of guaranteeing. These are all a person’s necessities, by which he lives; and his money is his guarantee and his salvation for his lifetime, garantie in French.

notes.872: (sn): The identity of the Gammadites is uncertain.
notes.873: (tn): See note on “quivers” in Jer 51:11 on the meaning of Hebrew שֶׁלֶט (shelet) and also M. Greenberg, Ezekiel (AB), 2:553.

rashi.heb:
*בני ארוד וחילך.* 
ושאר חיל בני אדם היושבים בתוכך:
rashi.eng: *The children of Arvad and your army.* [Heb. וְחֵילֵךּ,] the rest of the army of people who dwell within you.

rashi.heb:
*וגמדים.* 
ת"י ואף קפוטקאי שמעתי משמו של רבי מנחם על שם שיורדין בים עד התהום משערי גומדי אמות עומקה נקראו גמדים אנדוי"ש בלע"ז ויש פותרים שהם ננסים ונכנסין במדת אמה:
rashi.eng: *and Gammadim.* Jonathan rendered: and also Cappadocians. I heard in the name of Rabbi Menachem that because they dive into the sea as far as the deep and estimate (גֹמְדֵי) the cubits of its depth, they are called Gammadim. Others explain that they are dwarfs and fit into the measure of a cubit.

rashi.heb:
*שלטיהם.* 
הם אשפות שנותנין בהם חצים כמו (ירמיה כא) הברו החיצים מלאו השלטים קויכרינ"ה בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *their quivers.* [Heb. שִּׁלֻטֵיהֶם,] These are the quivers in which they would put arrows, like (Jer. 51:11): “Polish the arrows, fill the quivers (הַשְּׁלָטִים),” cuyvrin[e] in Old French, quivers.

rashi.heb:
*תלו.* 
הרבה תלי תלים:
rashi.eng: *they heaped.* [Heb. תִּלוּ,] many heaps upon heaps תִּלִים) (תִּלֵי.

notes.874: (sn): Tarshish refers to a distant seaport sometimes believed to be located in southern Spain (others identified it as Carthage in North Africa). In any event it represents here a distant, rich, and exotic port which was a trading partner of Tyre.

rashi.heb:
*תרשיש.* 
ים ששמה תרשיש:
rashi.eng: *Tarshish.* a sea named Tarshish.

rashi.heb:
*מרוב כל הון.* 
שהיה בתוכך ובטוחים הסוחרים שימצאו בך סחורה הראויה להם:
rashi.eng: *with the multitude of all wealth.* that was in your midst. The merchants were confident that they would find in you the merchandise fit for them.

rashi.heb:
*בדיל.* 
אשטיי"ן בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *tin.*

rashi.heb:
*עזבוניך.* 
חוזקיך ועוזרך כמו (נחמיה ג׳:ח׳) ויעזבו את ירושלים עד החומה וממונו של אדם הוא חזקו המעמידו על רגליו:
rashi.eng: *your aid.* [Heb. עִזְבוֹנָיִךּ,] your strength and your aid, like (Neh. 3:8): “and they strengthened Jerusalem to the… wall,” and a person’s money is his strength. which sets him up on his feet.

rashi.heb:
*בנפש אדם.* 
עבדים ושפחות למכור:
rashi.eng: *with living people.* male and female slaves to sell.

notes.875: (tn): The way in which these horses may have been distinguished from other horses is unknown. Cf. ASV “war-horses” (NASB, NIV, NRSV, CEV all similar); NLT “chariot horses.”

rashi.heb:
*ידך.* 
מקומך:
rashi.eng: *your place.* [Heb. יָדִךּ, lit. your hand,] your place.

rashi.heb:
*קרנות שן והבנים.* 
קרני יעלים ועצמות פיל וטווסים עופות ששמן פאו"ן בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *horns, ivory, and peacocks.* horns of ibexes, bones of elephants, and peacocks, birds called paon in French.

rashi.heb:
*השיבו אשכרך.* 
הביאו לך תשורה:
rashi.eng: *brought you as a gift.* [Heb. הֵשִּׁיבוּ אֶשְּׁכָּרֵךּ,] brought your gift.

notes.878: (tc): Many Hebrew mss, Aquila’s Greek translation, and the Syriac version read “Edom.” The LXX reads “man,” a translation which assumes the same consonants as Edom. This reading is supported from the context as the text deals with Damascus, the capital of Syria (Aram), later (in v. 18).

rashi.heb:
*ארם סוחרתך.* 
באבנים טובות האמורות במקרא וארגמן ורקמה ובוץ:
rashi.eng: *Aram was your merchant.* [dealing] with the precious stones mentioned in the verse, and “purple cloth, embroidery, and fine linen.”

rashi.heb:
*מרוב מעשיך.* 
מתוך שהיו יודעים בנשיאיך ושריך שמראין להם מעשה נוי ותפארת לתכשיט:
rashi.eng: *because of the multitude of your works.* because they knew that your princes and dignitaries accumulate many works of beauty and glory for [use as] ornaments

rashi.heb:
*בנופך.* 
איקרבונקל"א בלעז:
rashi.eng: *with carbuncle.* [Heb. שְּׁנֹפֶךּ,] e c(h)arbuncle in Old French.

notes.879: (sn): The location is mentioned in Judg 11:33.

rashi.heb:
*בחטי מנית.* 
שם מקום שחיטיה יפות כמו עד בואך מנית (שופטים יח) ומדרש אגדה חטין יפין וגסין הנמכרים במניין ויונתן תרגם בחטי ריחוש לשון קבוצת מניינים הרבה טרוקא"ס בלע"ז וחבירו בפסיקתא מה הדם רחוש בעלין אף לאה רחושה בבנים ולא ידעתי מהו מפי רבי שמעון מצאתי שמצא במקרא תרגום ירושלמי בחיטי מנית ופנג דחושלא וקלמא שערי דחושלא שבגמרא אנו שונים שעורים קלופים ואומר אני מנית לשון מנות מאכל מזומן ואף לפי נקוד דגש דרכו של יונתן לתרגם התיבה פעם משמעה פעם מדרשה כן תרגם וגם שם העיר המונה אנו נוקדים שם והמונה לא מפיק ה"א ותרגם אף לתמן יתרמון קטולי קרתא דסגיאין איתרגושתהא:
rashi.eng: *with wheat of Minnith.* the name of a place that produced wheat of high quality, like (Jud. 11:33): “until you come to Minnith.” Midrash Aggadah (source unknown) [explains it as] good, thick wheat kernels, which are sold by number. Jonathan renders: בִּחִטֵי רִיחוּשּׁ expression for a gathering of many numbers, troche in Old French, bundle, bunch. A similar word appears in Pesikta [d’Rav Kahana, p. 184b]: “Just as the myrtle is crowded (רָחוּשּׁ) with leaves, so was Leah crowded with sons.” But I do not know what it [wheat of Minnith] is. In the name of Rabbi Simon, I heard that he found in a Bible with a Jerusalem Targum בְּחִטֵי מִנִיתוּפַנַג rendered: בְּחוּשְּׁלָא וְקֲלְמָא. Now, שַּׁעֲרֵי דְחוּשְּׁלָא, which is found in the Talmud (Yoma 79a), is explained as: peeled barley. I say, however, that “Minnith” is an expression of portions (מָנוֹת), prepared food. Even according to its vocalization with a “dagesh,” Jonathan is wont to translate a word sometimes according to its apparent meaning and sometimes according to its midrashic meaning. So did he render (below 39:16): “And also the name of the city shall be Hamonah (הֲמוֹנָה).” Although we punctuate the name הֲמוֹנָה without a “mappiq hey” (הֱמוֹנָה), [with a “mappiq hey” (pronounced) הֲמוֹנָה would mean “her multitude” with a silent “hey” it means simply “a multitude.”] Jonathan paraphrases: And also there, the slain of the city whose multitude is great will be cast.

rashi.heb:
*ופנג.* 
ראיתי בספר יוסף הכהן עץ אפרסמון הוא פנג והיו מצויין ביריחו ועל שם ריח הטוב נקראת יריחו באלסמ"א בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *balsam trees.* [Heb. פַנַג.] I saw in the book of Joseph the priest (Josiphon vol. 1 p.155 ch. 36 Flusser): The balsam tree is “pannag,” and they were found in Jericho, and because of the fragrant scent, it [the city] is called Jericho [יְרִיחוֹ from רֵיחַ, scent], balsme in Old French.

rashi.heb:
*ביין חלבון.* 
יין לבן מבושל ומנחם חברו עם חלב חטים (תהלים קמו) ל' טוב:
rashi.eng: *with white wine.* [Heb. בְּיֵין חֶלְבּוֹן,] cooked white wine, and Menachem (p. 89) connects it with (Ps. 147:14): “the best (חֵלֶב) of the wheat,” an expression of goodness

rashi.heb:
*וצמר צחר.* 
ועמר מלת כבינא ביום שנולד הטלה וטהרתו אמו בלחיכתה עושין כסות ומכבנין אותו סביבו בקרסים כדי שיהא צמרו נקי:
rashi.eng: *and white wool.* [Heb. צָחֹר.] [Jonathan renders:] “fine white covered wool.” On the day the lamb is born, and its mother cleanses it by licking it, they make a cover and wrap it around it with clasps so that that its wool be clean.

rashi.heb:
*צחר.* 
לבן כמו אתונות צחורות (שופטים ה):
rashi.eng: *and white.* צָחֹר means white, like (Jud. 5:10): "white (צִחוֹרוֹת) donkeys.

notes.880: (tc): The MT leaves v. 18 as an incomplete sentence and begins v. 19 with “and Dan and Javan (Ionia) from Uzal.” The LXX mentions “wine.” The translation follows an emendation assuming some confusions of vav and yod. See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:82.
notes.881: (sn): According to L. C. Allen (Ezekiel [WBC], 2:82), Izal was located between Haran and the Tigris and was famous for its wine.

rashi.heb:
*ודן ויון.* 
מדינות הם:
rashi.eng: *Vedan and Javan.* They are states.

rashi.heb:
*מאוזל.* 
מטוה של שיראין:
rashi.eng: *spun silk.* [Heb. מְאוּזָל,] spun silk thread.

rashi.heb:
*ברזל עשות.* 
עשוי כעששיות מש"ש בלעז והוא פרזלא הנדואה:
rashi.eng: *iron wrought into ingots.* [Heb. עָשּׁוֹת,] made like ingots (עֲשָּׁשִּׁיוֹת) mas(s)es or mas(s)iz in Old French, ingots, massive, and that is iron of Cush.

rashi.heb:
*בבגדי חופש לרכבה.* 
בלבוש דיקר לרתיכין:
rashi.eng: *in precious raiments for chariots.* [lit. in raiments of freedom for riding, translated according to the Targum as] in precious raiments for chariots.

rashi.heb:
*בכרים.* 
כבשים ויונתן תרגם בתורין וכן תרגם מאה אלף כרים דמישע מלך מואב (מלכים ב ג׳:ד׳):
rashi.eng: *with lambs.* [Heb. בְכָרִים,] lambs. Jonathan renders: with cattle, and so too did he render (II Kings 3:4): “one hundred thousand bulls,” (כָּרִים) of Mesha, king of Moab.

rashi.heb:
*אשור כלמד.* 
י"ת מדינן אשור ומדי:
rashi.eng: *Assyria and Media.* [Heb. אַשּׁוּר כִּלְמַד.] Jonathan renders: the states of Assyria and Media.

rashi.heb:
*במכלולים.* 
בדברים שהם למכלול פרמונ"ט בלע"ז ומה הם המכלולים גלומי תכלת ורקמה טליתות של תכלת מרוקמות:
rashi.eng: *with adornments.* [Heb. בְּמַכְלֻלִים,] with things that are for adornment (מכלול), paramenz in Old French, adornments, jewelry, and what are the adornments? Wraps of embroidered blue cloth.

rashi.heb:
*ובגנזי ברומים.* 
בתכשיטי פאר שגונזין אותן בארגזין שקורין אשקרי"ן בלע"ז והם מחופין עור ומצוירין לנוי במיני מסמרין שורות שורות וציורין והם בלשון ארמי קמטרין ובלשון עברי ברומים והם חבושין ואסורין בחבלי בוץ לנוי:
rashi.eng: *and with treasures kept in chests.* With beautiful adornments that are kept in chests called escrin in Old French, (ecrin in modern French). They are covered with leather and decorated for beauty with sorts of nails forming rows and pictures, and they are called קַמְטְרַיָא in Aramaic and בְּרוֹמִים in Hebrew, and they are tied and bound with linen ropes for beauty.

rashi.heb:
*וארוזים.* 
ת"י אעי הדסים אותן ארגזים היו נתונין במגדלי עץ הדס ומביאין אותן לתוך המגדלין והקמטראות שבתוכן והתכשיטין שבתוך הקמטראות הכל יחד לסחורה וכה פתרון הלשון בלשון קצרה ובגנזי ברומים החבושים בחבלים וארוזים בתוך עץ ארז שהברומים הם הקמטראות והיו אסורים בחבלים ונתונים במגדלי הדס שהיא ממיני ארז ומכלולים שבתוך הברומים קרא יונתן וכושפין דארזא באימלין די זהריתא תכשיטין הצריכין שמירה נאה דמחתין בקומטרין מונחים בקמטראות והמגדלים שבתרגום כמו שאנו שונין תיבה ומגדל שיפרייט"ש בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *and [enclosed in] myrtle wood.* Jonathan renders: myrtle wood. Those chests were placed in chests of myrtle wood, and they would bring them into the outer chests and the chest within them, and so too, the ornaments that were inside the chests; everything all together for merchandising. This is the meaning of the wording in brief: and with treasures [kept] in chests, tied with ropes and [enclosed in] cedar wood, for the בְּרוֹמִים are the chests, and they were tied with ropes and placed in chests of myrtle, which is a species of cedar.
