And the adornments that were inside the chests, Jonathan calls וְכוּשּׁפִּין דְאַרְזָא בְּאִימְלִין דִּי זָהְרָיִתָא adornments that require good watching (זְהִירוּת), [i.e.,] בְּקוֹמְטְרִין דְמֲחֲתִין that were placed in chests. And the word מִגְדָּל in the Targum is like what we learn: a box and a chest (מִגְדָּל) schafreite in Middle High German, clothes chest, cupboard. [In some editions] armaise in Old French.

notes.882: (tn): Or perhaps “Large merchant ships.” The expression “ships of Tarshish” may describe a class of vessel, that is, large oceangoing merchant ships.

rashi.heb:
*אניות תרשיש.* 
שרותיך הם היו לך לערבה ומישור כשם שהמישור הוא דרך כבושה להביא בו סחורה לעיר היושבת ביבשה היו לך תחתם אניות תרשיש מסילה להביא מערבך לתוכך:
rashi.eng: *Ships… your plains.* [Heb. שָּׁרוֹתַיִךּ.] They were to you as a plain and a flat terrain. Just as the flat terrain is a paved road, upon which to bring merchandise to a city situated on dry land, the ships of Tarshish were for you instead of them (sic) as a highway for bringing your merchandise into your midst.

rashi.heb:
*שרותיך.* 
לשון שרון ומישור ודוגמתו עלו בשרותיה (ירמיה ה):
rashi.eng: *your plains.* [Heb. שָּׁרוֹתַיִךּ,] an expression for Sharon and flat terrain. A similar instance is (Jer. 5:10): “Ascend upon its rows בְּשָׁרוֹתֶיהָ.”

rashi.heb:
*ותמלאי, ותכבדי מאד.* 
הביאו לתוכך משא רב והכבידו משאך יותר מדאי:
rashi.eng: *and you were filled and you became very heavy.* They brought a great burden into your midst and made your load too heavy.

rashi.heb:
*במים רבים הביאוך השטים אותך.* 
כדרך האניות הגדולו' שמפליגין אותן לתוך פלגום הים ומתוך שנתמלאת וכבדת בא רוח הקדים ושברך בלב ימים ולענין דוגמת העיר מתוך שנתמלאת עושר גבה לבך ובא עליך פורענות:
rashi.eng: *In the abundant waters, your oarsmen brought you.* After the manner of the large ships, which they send into the midst of the sea. And since you are filled and are too heavy, the east wind will come and shatter you in the heart of the seas. As regards the comparison of the city: since you were filled with wealth, your heart became haughty, and retribution will befall you.

notes.883: (tn, Heb): “your repairers of damage.” See v. 9.

notes.884: (tn): Compare this phrase to Isa 57:20 and Amos 8:8. See M. Greenberg, Ezekiel (AB), 2:561.

rashi.heb:
*מגרשות.* 
כמו מגרשי העיר:
rashi.eng: *the neighboring districts.* [Heb. מִגְרשּׁוֹת,] like (Num. 35:2): “and open land (וּמִגְרָשּׁ) for the cities.”

rashi.heb:
*אל הארץ יעמודו.* 
מה לנו עוד באניות להיכן נוליך סחורה עוד:
rashi.eng: *they will stand upon the land.* What use have we anymore with ships? Where shall we take our wares from now on?

notes.885: (tn, Heb): “make heard over you with their voice.”
notes.886: (tn): Note a similar expression to “roll in the ashes” in Mic 1:10.

rashi.heb:
*יתפלשו.* 
יתגלגלו:
rashi.eng: *they will wallow.* [Heb. יִתְפַלָשּׁוּ,] they will roll.

notes.887: (tn, Heb): “and they will weep concerning you with bitterness of soul, (with) bitter mourning.”

notes.888: (tn): As it stands, the meaning of the Hebrew text is unclear. The translation follows the suggestion of M. Dahood, “Accadian-Ugaritic dmt in Ezekiel 27:32,” Bib 45 (1964): 83-84. Several other explanations and emendations have been offered. See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:83, and D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 2:85-86, for a list of options.

rashi.heb:
*ונשאו אליך בניהם.* 
בנהי שלהם:
rashi.eng: *And they will lift up over you with their wailing.* [Heb. בְּנִיהֶם,] with their wailing.

rashi.heb:
*כדומה.* 
כך היה שם ראשי אדום כענין שנאמר משא דומה (ישעיהו כ״א:י״א) וי"ת לית דדמי לה:
rashi.eng: *“as Dummah”.* [Heb. כְּדֻמָּה.] This was the name of the heads of Edom, as the matter is stated (Isa. 21:11): “The harsh prophecy about Dumah (דּוּמָה).”

rashi.heb:
*כדומה.* 
כדוגמתה:
rashi.eng: *“as Dummah”.* Jonathan renders: There is none like (דָמֵי) as one of her likeness (כַּדוֹמָה).

rashi.heb:
*בצאת עזבוניך וגו'.* 
כל זה יקוננו עליך בקינתם:
rashi.eng: *When your merchandise came out, etc..* All this they will lament over you in their lamentation.

rashi.heb:
*רעמו פנים.* 
זעומי פנים וכן בעבור הרעימה (שמואל א א׳:ו׳) וכן כל תלונה תורעמתא:
rashi.eng: *their faces were angry.* [Heb. רָעֲמוּ פָּנִים,] angry faces, and so (I Sam. 1:6): “in order to make her complain (הַרְעִימָהּ),” and so every expression of complaint is called תּוּרְעֲמָתָא.

rashi.heb:
*שרקו.* 
שובלי"ר בלעז כך שורקין על דבר שחלף והלך לו:
rashi.eng: *hissed.* [Heb. שָּׁרְקוּ,] sibler in old French, to whistle. So do people whistle about a thing that has disappeared.

notes.894: (tn, Heb): “and you made your heart (mind) like the heart (mind) of gods.”

rashi.heb:
*מושב אלהים.* 
עשה לו באויר על הים במנגנין כמין שבעה רקיעים וישב לו על העליון:
rashi.eng: *a seat of God.* he made for himself in the air, over the sea, with a mechanism that was a replica of seven heavens, and he sat down on the highest one.

notes.895: (sn): Or perhaps “Danel” (so TEV), referring to a ruler known from Canaanite legend. See the note on “Daniel” in 14:14. A reference to Danel (preserved in legend at Ugarit, near the northern end of the Phoenician coast) makes more sense here when addressing Tyre than in 14:14.
notes.896: (sn): The tone here is sarcastic, reflecting the ruler’s view of himself.

rashi.heb:
*הנה חכם אתה מדניאל.* 
דניאל בא נבוכדנצר לעשותו אלוה ולדניאל סגיד ומנחה וניחוחין אמר לנסכא ליה ולא קביל עליה ואתה עושה עצמך אלוה:
rashi.eng: *Behold, are you wiser than Daniel.* [As for] Daniel Nebuchadnezzar came to make him a god (Dan. 2:46): “and prostrated himself before Daniel, and ordered that they should offer a meal offering and sacrifices of sweet odors to him,” but he did not accept it upon himself, yet you make yourself a God?

rashi.heb:
*כל סתום לא עממוך.* 
לא עמום ממך קנתורין הם שמקנתרין כלומר שמא חכם אתה כדניאל שנא' בו כל רז לא אנס לך (דניאל ו'):
rashi.eng: *that no secret is hidden from you.* [Heb. לֹא עֲמָמוּךָ,] is not hidden from you. These are taunts [by] which he is taunting; that is to say: Perhaps you are as wise as Daniel, about whom it is stated: (Dan. 4:6): “and no secret overwhelms you?”

rashi.heb:
*עשית לך חיל.* 
קנית לך נכסין:
rashi.eng: *did you acquire wealth for yourself.* [Heb. עָשִׂיתָ לְךָ חָיִל. lit. did you make.] Did you acquire property for yourself?

rashi.heb:
*ותעש זהב וכסף.* 
וכנשתא:
rashi.eng: *and gather gold and silver.* [Heb. וְתַעַשּׂ,] and gather.

notes.898: (tn, Heb): “because of your making your heart like the heart of gods.”

notes.899: (sn): This is probably a reference to the Babylonians.
notes.900: (tn, Heb): “they will draw their swords against the beauty of your wisdom.”

rashi.heb:
*והריקו חרבותם.* 
כמשמעו ומדרש אגדה משכב זכור שנבעל כנשים שלשה עשו עצמם אלוה ונבעלו כנשים יואש בן אחזיה שנאמר (ד"ה ב' כ"ד) ואת יואש עשו שפוטים וחירם ונבוכדנצר:
rashi.eng: *and they will draw their swords.* [This is to be understood] according to its apparent meaning. [According to] Midrash Aggadah (see Mechilta to Exod. 15:9; Tan. Va’era 9), it means homosexuality, for he was used sexually as women are. Three pretended to be gods and were sexually molested like women: Joash the son of Ahaziah, as it is said (II Chron. 24:24): “and upon Joash they exacted judgment,” Hiram, and Nebuchadnezzar.

rashi.heb:
*יפעתך.* 
הופעתך לשון תואר פנים, והמדרש דורשו יופי עתך:
rashi.eng: *your brightness.* [Heb. יִפְעָתֶךָ,] your brightness, an expression of the appearance of the countenance. The Medrash interprets it as “the beauty of your time (יְפֵה עִתֶּךָ).”

notes.901: (tn, Heb): “you will die the death of the slain.”

rashi.heb:
*מחללך.* 
כמו הורגך:
rashi.eng: *your slayer.* [Heb. מְחַלְלֶךָ,] like הוֹרְגֶךָ.

notes.902: (sn): The Phoenicians practiced circumcision, so the language here must be figurative, indicating that they would be treated in a disgraceful manner. Uncircumcised peoples were viewed as inferior, unclean, and perhaps even sub-human. See 31:18 and 32:17-32, as well as the discussion in D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 2:99.

notes.904: (tn): For a discussion of possible nuances of this phrase, see M. Greenberg, Ezekiel (AB), 2:580-81.

rashi.heb:
*אתה חותם תכנית וגו'.* 
אתה הוא מלא חכמה לחתום ולטבוע כל תבנית וצורה:
rashi.eng: *images.* [Heb. תָּכְנִית,] peinture in French, painting, engraving.

rashi.heb:
*תכנית.* 
פיינטור"א בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *You are the one who engraves images, etc..* You are full of the wisdom to seal and to stamp every pattern and shape.

notes.905: (sn): The imagery of the lament appears to draw upon an extrabiblical Eden tradition about the expulsion of the first man (see v. 14 and the note there) from the garden due to his pride. The biblical Eden tradition speaks of cherubs placed as guardians at the garden entrance following the sin of Adam and Eve (Gen 3:24), but no guardian cherub like the one described in verse 14 is depicted or mentioned in the biblical account. Ezekiel’s imagery also appears to reflect Mesopotamian and Canaanite mythology at certain points. See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 2:119-20.
notes.906: (tn): The exact identification of each gemstone is uncertain. The list should be compared to that of the priest in Exod 28:17-20, which lists twelve stones in rows of three. The LXX apparently imports the Exod 28 list. See reference to the types of stones in L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:91.

rashi.heb:
*בעדן גן אלהים וגו'.* 
בסגי טבון ותפנוקין את מתפניק כאלו בעדן גינתא דה' את שרי כל עותרא גיותא ויקרא מתיהב לך כל אבנין טבן מסדרן על לבושך:
rashi.eng: *In Eden, the garden of God.* With much goodness and pleasure. You enjoy yourself as if you were dwelling in Eden, the garden of God. All wealth, pride, and honor are given to you: all precious stones are set on your raiment.

rashi.heb:
*מסוכתך.* 
חופתך, ל"א לבוש כיסוייך:
rashi.eng: *your covering.* Your canopy. Another explanation: Your raiment.

rashi.heb:
*מלאכת תופיך ונקביך בך.* 
אע"פ שנתתי לך הכבוד הזה יודע הייתי שתתגאה ועשיתי בך מלאכת תופים ונקבים המוציאין רוח בקול זמר כתוף ובם היה לך להתבונן:
rashi.eng: *the work of your drums and your orifices.* Although I gave you all this honor, I knew that you would become haughty, and I made in you the work of the perforated drums that let out wind with an instrumental sound like a drum, and these are what you should have contemplated about.

notes.907: (tn): Or “winged”; see L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:91.
notes.908: (tn): The meaning of this phrase in Hebrew is uncertain. The word translated here “guards” occurs in Exod 25:20 in reference to the cherubim “covering” the ark.
notes.909: (tn, Heb): “you (were) an anointed cherub that covers and I placed you.” In the Hebrew text the ruler of Tyre is equated with a cherub, and the verb “I placed you” is taken with what follows (“on the holy mountain of God”). However, this reading is problematic. The pronoun “you” at the beginning of verse 14 is feminine singular in the Hebrew text; elsewhere in this passage the ruler of Tyre is addressed with masculine singular forms. It is possible that the pronoun is a rare (see Deut 5:24; Num 11:15) or defectively written (see 1 Sam 24:19; Neh 9:6; Job 1:10; Ps 6:3; Eccl 7:22) masculine form, but it is more likely that the form should be repointed as the preposition “with” (see the LXX). In this case the ruler of Tyre is compared to the first man, not to a cherub. If this emendation is accepted, then the verb “I placed you” belongs with what precedes and concludes the first sentence in the verse. It is noteworthy that the verbs in the second and third lines of the verse also appear at the end of the sentence in the Hebrew text. The presence of a conjunction at the beginning of “I placed you” is problematic for the proposal, but it may reflect a later misunderstanding of the syntax of the verse. For a defense of the proposed emendation, see L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:91.

rashi.heb:
*את כרוב ממשח הסוכך.* 
את עוף מדה כלומר העוף הגדול הסוכך בכנפיו סכך רב כלומר מושל ממשל רב, ממשח לשון גודל כמו אנשי מדות (במדבר י"ד) דמתרגמינן גברי דמשחן:
rashi.eng: *You are a cherub of great measure, that covers.* You are a bird of measure, i.e., the huge bird that covers a large area with his wings; i.e., you rule over a large dominion. מִמְשַּׁח is a word for largeness, like (Num. 13:32): “men of stature (אַנְשֵּׁי מִדוֹת).” which is translated into Aramaic as גַבְרֵי דְמִשְּׂחָן.

rashi.heb:
*ונתתיך בהר קודש אלהים היית.* 
ונתתי לך מקום לקנות לך שם בבנין הר קדשי שסייעת את שלמה בעצי ארזים:
rashi.eng: *and I gave that to you; you were on the mount of the sanctuary of God.* and I gave you a place to acquire a name for yourself in the edifice of the mountain of My sanctuary, for you assisted Solomon with the cedar wood.

rashi.heb:
*בתוך אבני אש התהלכת.* 
קנית לך זכרון עם מלכי ישראל שהם כמלאכי השרת:
rashi.eng: *you walked among stones of fire.* You acquired for yourself a memorial with the kings of Israel, who are like the ministering angels.

rashi.heb:
*נמצא עולתה בך.* 
באמרך אל אני:
rashi.eng: *until wrongdoing was found in you.* in your saying, “I am a god.”

notes.911: (tn, Heb): “they filled your midst with violence.”
notes.912: (tn, Heb): “I defiled you.” The presence of the preposition “from” following the verb indicates that a verb of motion is implied as well. See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:91.
notes.913: (tn, Heb): “and I expelled you, O guardian cherub.” The Hebrew text takes the verb as first person and understands “guardian cherub” as a vocative, in apposition to the pronominal suffix on the verb. However, if the emendation in verse 14a is accepted (see the note above), then one may follow the LXX here as well and emend the verb to a third person perfect. In this case the subject of the verb is the guardian cherub. See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:91.

rashi.heb:
*מלו.* 
כמו מלאו:
rashi.eng: *they filled.* [Heb. מָלוּ, like מָלְאוּ,] they filled.

rashi.heb:
*ואחללך מהר אלהים.* 
גרמת שאמחה אותך שלא תצדק עוד בבנין ביתי:
rashi.eng: *and I shall cast you as profane.* You caused me to eradicate you, so that you shall no longer be remembered concerning the building of My House.

rashi.heb:
*ואבדך.* 
כמו ואאבדך:
rashi.eng: *and I shall destroy you.* [Heb. וָאַבֶּדְךָ,] like וָאֲאַבֶּדְ and I shall destroy you.

rashi.heb:
*מתוך אבני אש.* 
שלא תטול חלק עם הצדיקי', ורבותינו במדרש אגדה דרשו הענין הזה באדם הראשון וכך אמר הנביא לחירם מה נתגאית ברקיעך שמא בגן עדן היית כמו שהיה אדם הראשון כל אבן יקרה וגו' כי כל החופות האלה עשיתי לאדם הראשון ופחותה שבכולן זהב שהיא מנוייה אחרון מלאכת תופיך וגו'. בזאת השויתיך לו ולא באחרת ובך נסתכלתי ובראתי תופים ונקבים באדם הראשון. את כרוב ממשח. שמא אתה כאותו כרוב שהיה גדול בממשח הסוכך כולו מקצה השמים ועד קצה השמים ושמא נתתיך להיות בהררי קדש כאשר נתתי לו:
rashi.eng: *from among the stones of fire.* that you shall not take a share with the righteous. Our Rabbis in the Midrash Aggadah (B. B. 75a) interpreted this section as referring to Adam: So said the prophet to Hiram,"Why should you be proud of your sky? Were you in the Garden of Eden, as Adam was? [13] every precious stone, etc. For I made all these canopies for Adam, and the least of them was gold, which is counted last. the work of your drums, etc. With this, I made you equal to him, but not with anything else, and I pondered over you and created drums and orifices in Adam. [14] Are you a cherub of great measure Are you like that cherub that was great in measure, whose great wingspan covered from one end of heaven completely to the other end of heaven, and did I place you to be on the holy mountains as I placed him?

rashi.heb:
*שחת חכמתך על יפעתך.* 
שנתגאית ביפעתך:
rashi.eng: *you destroyed your wisdom with your brightness.* for you were proud of your brightness.

rashi.heb:
*לראוה בך.* 
להסתכל בבושתך, לראוה כמו לראיה:
rashi.eng: *to gaze upon you.* [Heb. לְרַאֲוָה בָּך] to gaze upon your shame; לְרַאֲוָה is like לִרְאִיָה, to see.

rashi.heb:
*חללת מקדשיך.* 
קדושתך:
rashi.eng: *you profaned your sanctity.* [Heb. מִקְדָשֶׁךָ,] your sanctity.

rashi.heb:
*אש מתוכך.* 
דברי גאוה שיצאו מפיך לאמר אל אני ל"א כתרגומו ואייתי עממיא דתקיפין כאשתא מחובי זדונך:
rashi.eng: *fire out of your midst.* Haughty words that came out of your mouth, saying, “I am a god.” Another explanation: [It is to be interpreted] according to the Targum: And I brought forth peoples as strong as fire because of your arrogant sins.

rashi.heb:
*שממו.* 
תמהו:
rashi.eng: *will wander.* [Heb. שָּׁמְמוּ.] will wonder.

notes.915: (sn): Sidon was located 25 miles north of Tyre. For location see Map1-A1; JP3-F3; JP4-F3.

notes.916: (tn): Or “I challenge you.” The phrase “I am against you” may be a formula for challenging someone to combat or a duel. See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 1:201-2, and P. Humbert, “Die Herausforderungsformel ‘h!nn#n' ?l?K>,’” ZAW 45 (1933): 101-8.
notes.917: (tn): Or “reveal my holiness.” God’s “holiness” is fundamentally his transcendence as sovereign ruler of the world. The revelation of his authority and power through judgment is in view in this context.

notes.918: (tn, Heb): “into it”; the referent of the feminine pronoun has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*ונפלל חלל בתוכה בחרב עליה מסביב.* 
על אשר יראו החרב מסביב בחוץ יפלו יושבי העיר ויהיו בטוחים להיות חללים בתוכה:
rashi.eng: *and they will judge themselves as slain in her midst by the sword [coming] upon her from all around.* Because they will see the sword surrounding [them] from outside, the people of the city will assess [the situation] and be sure that they will be slain in her midst.

rashi.heb:
*ונפלל.* 
כמו לא פללתי (בראשית מ"ח) לא סברית וכמו ואויבינו פלילים (דברים ל״ב:ל״א) ידונו עצמם להיות חללים בתוכה:
rashi.eng: *and they will judge.* [Heb. וְנִפְלַל,] like (Gen. 48:11): “I did not think (פִלָּלְתִּי),” and like (Deut. 32:31): “and our enemies judge (פְּלִילִים).” They will judge themselves to be slain in her midst.

notes.920: (sn): Similar language is used in reference to Israel’s adversaries in Num 33:55; Josh 23:13.
notes.921: (tn, Heb): “and there will not be for the house of Israel a brier that pricks and a thorn that inflicts pain from all the ones who surround them, the ones who scorn them.”

rashi.heb:
*ולא יהיה עוד לבית ישראל וגו'.* 
לפי שניבא על עמון ומואב ופלשתים ואדום וצור וצידון שהם שכיני ארץ ישראל שיחרבו ומאחר שיאבדו כולן לא יהיה סילון וקוץ לישראל בכל סביבות' שיכאיבם ושירע להם:
rashi.eng: *And there will no longer be to the house of Israel, etc..* Since he prophesied about Ammon, Moab, the Philistines, Edom, Tyre, and Zidon, who are the neighbors of the land of Israel, that they would be destroyed. Since they all will be destroyed, there will not be a briar or a thorn to [the people of Israel, in all their surroundings, to pain or harm them.

rashi.heb:
*סילון.* 
מין קמשונים וחוחים הוא:
rashi.eng: *briars.* [Heb. סִילוֹן,] a species of thistles and thorns.

rashi.heb:
*ממאיר.* 
ענין הכאבה כמו צרעת ממארת (ויקרא י״ג:נ״א) פוניינ"ט בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *pricking.* [Heb. מַמְאִיר,] a matter of hurting, like (Lev. 13:51): “painful (מַמְאֶרֶת) zaarath,” poignante in French, stinging, pricking.

rashi.heb:
*השאטים אותם.* 
הבוזים אותם:
rashi.eng: *who plunder them.* [Heb. הַשָּׁאטִים,] who plunder them.

rashi.heb:
*לעבדי ליעקב.* 
כמו שנתנה ליעקב נחלה בלא מצרי' ופרצת ימה וקדמה צפונה ונגבה (בראשית כ״ח:י״ד):
rashi.eng: *to My servant, to Jacob.* As it was given to Jacob, an inheritance without boundaries (Gen. 28:14): “and you will spread out toward the west and the east, toward the north and the south.”

notes.923: (sn): This promise was given in Lev 25:18-19.

notes.926: (tn): Or “I challenge you.” The phrase “I am against you” may be a formula for challenging someone to combat or a duel. See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 1:201-2, and P. Humbert, “Die Herausforderungsformel ‘h!nn#n' ?l?K>,’” ZAW 45 (1933): 101-8.
notes.927: (tn, Heb): “jackals,” but many medieval Hebrew mss read correctly “the serpent.” The Hebrew term appears to refer to a serpent in Exod 7:9-10, 12; Deut 32:33; and Ps 91:13. It also refers to large creatures that inhabit the sea (Gen 1:21; Ps 148:7). In several passages it is associated with the sea or with the multiheaded sea monster Leviathan (Job 7:12; Ps 74:13; Isa 27:1; 51:9). Because of the Egyptian setting of this prophecy and the reference to the creature’s scales (v. 4), many understand a crocodile to be the referent here (e.g., NCV “a great crocodile”; TEV “you monster crocodile”; CEV “a giant crocodile”).
notes.928: (sn): In Egyptian theology Pharaoh owned and controlled the Nile. See J. D. Currid, Ancient Egypt and the Old Testament, 240-44.

rashi.heb:
*התנים הגדול.* 
לפי שכל גדולתה של מצרים וכל שובע שבה על ידי יאורי נילוס הוא לפיכך הנביא ממשל את מלכה לתנין ואת עמה לדגת יאור:
rashi.eng: *the great crocodile.* Since all the greatness of Egypt and all its plenty comes though the Nile River, the prophet compares its king to a crocodile and its people to the fish of the river.

rashi.heb:
*לי יאורי.* 
איני צריך לעליונים כי יש לי יאורי מספיק כל צרכי:
rashi.eng: *My river is my own.* I do not need the heavenly powers, for my river provides all my necessities

rashi.heb:
*ואני עשיתני.* 
בגבורתי ובחכמתי הגדלתי גדולתי וממשלתי:
rashi.eng: *and I made myself.* With my might and with my wisdom, I enhanced my greatness and my dominion.

rashi.heb:
*חחים.* 
כמין טבעות ברזל איינ"ש בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *hooks.* [Heb. חַתִים,] type of iron rings, ens in Old French.

rashi.heb:
*דגת יאוריך בקשקשתיך.* 
אינטישאיקראטי"ש בלע"ז כלומר אתן בלב כל גבוריך לצאת עמך למלחמה ויפלו כולם:
rashi.eng: *the fish of your rivers to fasten onto your scales.* [Heb. בְּקַשְּׂקְשּׂתֶי,] en tes e(s)chardes in Old French, to your scales. That is to say, I shall inspire all your mighty men to go forth with you to war so that they will all fall.

notes.929: (tc): Some Hebrew mss, the Targum, and the LXX read “buried.”

rashi.heb:
*ונטשתיך המדברה.* 
זו היא אובדנן של דגים כיון שנטשו על פני היבשה מתים א"י אטינדר"י טו"י בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *And I will scatter you in the desert.* [Heb. וּנְטַשְּׁתִּי,] e etandre toy in Old French, and I shall spread you out. This is the perishing of fish: once they are spread out on the surface of the dry land, they die.

rashi.heb:
*משענת קנה.* 
כמה פעמים סמכו עליהם בימי סנחריב ובימי נבוכדנצר ולא הועיל להם בקנה זה שהוא רך ואינו סומך את הנשען עליו:
rashi.eng: *a prop of reeds.* Many times they relied on them: in the days of Sennacherib and in the days of Nebuchadnezzar, but it did not avail them, just like this reed, which is soft and does not support the one who leans on it.

notes.931: (tn): The Hebrew consonantal text (Kethib) has “by your hand,” but the marginal reading (Qere) has simply “by the hand.” The LXX reads “with their hand.”
notes.933: (tn, Heb): “you caused to stand for them all their hips.” An emendation which switches two letters but is supported by the LXX yields the reading “you caused all their hips to shake.” See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:103. In 2 Kgs 18:21 and Isa 36:6 trusting in the Pharaoh is compared to leaning on a staff. The oracle may reflect Hophra’s attempt to aid Jerusalem (Jer 37:5-8).

rashi.heb:
*בתפשם בך בכפך.* 
בכף קרי כאדם המהלך ונשען על מקלו:
rashi.eng: *When they took hold of you with the hand.* [Heb. בְּכַפְּ, lit. with your hand,] to be read בַּכַּף, with the hand, like a man who walks and supports himself on his staff.

rashi.heb:
*תרוץ.* 
תירצץ:
rashi.eng: *you splintered.* [Heb. תֵּרוֹף] [like] תֵּרָצֵף.

rashi.heb:
*ובקעת להם כל כתף.* 
כתפיהם כאדם הנסמך על קנה ונשבר והאדם נופל עליו והקרומיות נכנסות לו בכתיפיו:
rashi.eng: *and pierced the whole of their shoulders.* [lit. the whole of a shoulder,] i.e., their shoulders, like a man who leans on a reed, which breaks, and the man falls on it, and the shreds enter his shoulders.

rashi.heb:
*והעמדת להם כל מתנים.* 
מאחר שתשבר יצטרכו לחזק את מתניהם ולעמוד עליהם והרי אתה כאדם שחבירו נשען עליו והוא חלש ואומר לו התחזק על מתניך כי לא תסמוך עוד עלי וכן ת"י ולא תהא להון לבי' סומכוון ויש מחליפין והעמדת להם לוהמעדת ואיני רואה את דבריהן, ומנחם חברו עם מעמד רגלים כמוני:
rashi.eng: *and you made their loins stand upright.* [Heb. וְהַעֲמַדְתָּ.] Since you will break, they will be required to strengthen their loins and stand on them. You are like a man upon whom his friend was leaning, but he is weak and he says to him, “Strengthen yourself on your loins, for you can no longer lean on me.” So did Jonathan render: “and you will no longer be a support for them.” Some transpose וְהַעֲמַדְתָּ to וְהַמְעַדְתָּ, and you make all loins totter, but I do not care for their words. Moreover, Menachem (p. 134) associated it with the standing of the feet, just as I do.

notes.934: (tn, Heb): “I will cut off from you.”

notes.935: (tn): Or “I challenge you.” The phrase “I am against you” may be a formula for challenging someone to combat or a duel. See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 1:201-2, and P. Humbert, “Die Herausforderungsformel ‘h!nn#n' ?l?K>,’” ZAW 45 (1933): 101-8.
notes.936: (sn): This may refer to a site in the Egyptian Delta which served as a refuge for Jews (Jer 44:1; 46:14).
notes.937: (sn): Syene is known today as Aswan.

rashi.heb:
*ולא תשב ארבעים שנה.* 
ארבעים ושתים שני רעבון נגזרו בחלום פרעה כנגד שלשה פעמים שנכתב החלום שבע פרות ושבע שבלים רעות (בראשית מ״א:כ׳) ראה וספרו ליוסף הרי שני פעמים ויוסף אמר לו שבע הפרות הרקות והרעות וז' השבלים הרקות (שם) הרי ארבעים ושתים לרעב ולא היה להם אלא שתים שנאמר כי זה שנתי' הרעב (שם מ"ה) ומשירד יעקב למצרים פסק הרעב שהרי בשנה השלישית זרעו שנאמר ותן זרע ונחיה וגו' (שם מז) והארבעים נפרעו להם עכשיו:
rashi.eng: *neither shall it be inhabited for forty years.* Forty-two years of famine were decreed in Pharaoh’s dream, corresponding to the three times the dream is written. He saw seven bad cows and seven bad ears of grain (Gen. 41) and he told it to Joseph; hence we have [it mentioned] twice, and Joseph said to him, “The seven thin and bad cows and the seven empty ears,” totaling forty-two for the famine. But they had only two, as it is stated (ibid. 45:6): “For it is two years now that the famine has been on earth,” and when Jacob came down to Egypt, the famine ceased, for behold in the third year they sowed, as it is stated (ibid. 47:19): “and then you give us seed that we may live etc.,” and the forty years were paid to them now: “neither shall it be inhabited for forty years.”

rashi.heb:
*תשב ארבעים שנה.* 
תשב שר"א אשיגיא"ה בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *inhabited for forty years.* תֵּשֵּׁב means sera asijiee in Old French. will be settled, peopled.

notes.938: (sn): In Ezek 4:4-8 it was said that the house of Judah would suffer forty years.

notes.939: (tc): Thus the Masoretic Text. The LXX, Syriac, and Vulgate translate as though the Hebrew read “cause to inhabit.”

rashi.heb:
*מכורתם.* 
מגורתם ל"א כמו תולדותם וכן חברו מנחם:
rashi.eng: *their habitation.* [Heb. מְכוּרָתָם] [like] מְגוּרָתָם, their habitation. Another interpretation: like תוֹלדוֹתָם, their birth, and this is how Menachem (p. 110) associated it.

rashi.heb:
*לבלתי רדות בגוים.* 
לשון ממשלה כמו ורדו בדגת הים (שם א):
rashi.eng: *So that they shall not domineer over the nations.* [Heb. רְדוֹת,] an expression of ruling, like (Gen. 1: 28): “and rule (וּרְדוּ) over the fish of the sea.”

notes.940: (tn, Heb): “reminding of iniquity when they turned after them.”

rashi.heb:
*ולא יהיה.* 
מצרים לבית ישראל עוד למבטח המזכיר להם עון שאמר להם הקב"ה לא תוסיפו לראותם עוד (שמות י״ד:י״ג):
rashi.eng: *And it will no longer be.* [i.e.,] Egypt [will no longer be] a source of confidence for the House of Israel, bringing iniquity into remembrance for them, since the Holy One, blessed be he, said to them (Exod. 14: 13): “You shall no longer continue to see them.”

rashi.heb:
*ויהי בעשרים ושבע שנה.* 
למלכות נבוכדנצר, אותה שנה נתנה מצרים בידו כך שנינו בסדר עולם ויש בספר הזה הרבה נבואות כתובות מוקדם ומאוחר:
rashi.eng: *And it came to pass in the twenty-seventh year.* of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar. That year Egypt was delivered into his hand. This is what we learned in Seder Olam (ch. 26). In this book, there are many prophecies written in a non chronological order.

notes.942: (tn, Heb): “Nebuchadrezzar” is a variant and more correct spelling of Nebuchadnezzar, as the Babylonian name Nabu-kudurri-usur has an “r” rather than an “n” (so also in v. 19).
notes.943: (sn): Nebuchadnezzar besieged Tyre from 585 to 571 b.c. For location see Map1-A2; Map2-G2; Map4-A1; JP3-F3; JP4-F3.

rashi.heb:
*העביד את חילו.* 
על צור עבודה גדולה:
rashi.eng: *made his army serve [a great work against Tyre].* [Heb. צוּר אֵל, usually to here means] against Tyre, [in] a great work.

rashi.heb:
*כל ראש.* 
אנשי חיילותיו:
rashi.eng: *every head.* the men of his forces

rashi.heb:
*מוקרח וכל כתף מרוטה.* 
כדרך הצרים על העיר ימים רבים וטורחים ויגיעים בשאת משאות עצים ואבנים והוא לכד את צור בעשרים ושלש למלכותו כמו שמצינו בסדר עולם, מוקרח קאלב"ו בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *became bald and every shoulder, etc..* As is the custom with those who besiege a city many days and toil and weary themselves with carrying burdens of wood and stones. He captured Tyre in the twenty third [year] of his reign, as we find in Seder Olam (ad loc.). מֻקְרָח means calvo in Italian, bald.

rashi.heb:
*מרוט'.* 
פלי"אה בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *sore.* [Heb. מְרוּטָה,] pelee in Old French, peeled.

rashi.heb:
*ושכר לא היה לו.* 
לאחר ששללו שללה עלה הים ושטף מהם לפי שנגזר עליה ועל שללה ליאבד בים:
rashi.eng: *yet he had no reward.* After they had plundered its booty, the sea rose and washed it away from them, because it was decreed on it and on its booty to be lost in the sea.

notes.944: (tn, Heb): “for which he worked,” referring to the assault on Tyre (v. 18).

rashi.heb:
*פעולתו אשר עבד בה.* 
שכר פעולה אשר עבד במצותי בצור אתן לו את ארץ מצרים:
rashi.eng: *For his labor that he undertook against it.* [As] reward for the labor that he undertook against Tyre by My command, I shall give him the land of Egypt.

rashi.heb:
*אשר עשו לי.* 
מצרים רעה במשענתם שהבטיחו את עמי בעזרתם הבל:
rashi.eng: *because of what they did to Me.* [Because of] the evil that Egypt [did to Me] with their prop, that they assured My people with their futile aid.

notes.945: (tn, Heb): “I will cause a horn to sprout for the house of Israel.” The horn is used as a figure for military power in the OT (Ps 92:10). A similar expression is made about the Davidic dynasty in Ps 132:17.
notes.946: (tn, Heb): “I will grant you an open mouth.”

rashi.heb:
*ביום ההוא אצמיח קרן.* 
לא שמעתי ולא מצאתי פי' מקרא זה מה הוא צמח קרנם של ישראל במפלת מצרים שהרי ישראל גלו שמונה שנים לפני מפלת מצרים ואומר אני ביום ההוא מוסב על פרשה של מעלה מקץ ארבעים שנה אקבץ את מצרים ואותו חשבון כלה בשנה שמלך בלשאצר ומצינו בדניאל שבאותה שנה התחילו מלכי פרס להתחזק ונגזרה מפלה על בבל שנאמר (דניאל ז׳:א׳) בשנת חדא לבלשאצר דניאל חלם חזה וגו' קדמיתא כאריה היא בבל (שם) וכתיב (שם) חזה הוית עד די מריטו גפה וגומר וארו חיוה אוחרי תנינא דמיא לדוב היא פרס וכתיב וכן אמרין לה קומי אכולי בשר שגיא, כלומר תפשי המלוכה ומלכות פרס היא צמיחת קרן לישראל שנאמר בכורש הוא יבנה עירי וגלותי ישלח (ישעיהו מ״ה:י״ג) ומניין שארבעים שנה של מצרי' כלו באותו הפרק מצרים נתנה ביד נבוכדנצר בכ"ז לנבוכדנצר בשנה שנאמר' נבוא' זו ליחזקאל הוסיף ארבעים שנה הרי ששים ושבע צא מהם ארבעים וחמש לנבוכדנצר ועשרים ושלש לאויל מרודך כדאמרינן במסכת מגלה ושנה אחת מהם עלתה לזה ולזה כדאמרינן התם שנים מקוטעו' היו:
rashi.eng: *On that day will I cause the horn of the House of Israel to blossom out.* I have neither heard nor found the explanation of this verse. What is the blossoming of the horn of Israel in the downfall of Egypt? Was not Israel exiled eight years before the downfall of Egypt? [Therefore,] I say that “On that day” refers back to the above section, (verse 13): “At the end of forty years, I will gather the Egyptians.” That count ends in the year that Belshazzar assumed the throne, and we find in Daniel that in that year the kings of Persia began to gain strength, and downfall was decreed upon Babylon, as it is said (Dan. 7:1): “In the first year of Belshazzar,… Daniel saw a dream, etc.” ; (verse 4) “The first one was like a lion” - that is Babylon. And it is written (ad loc.): “I saw until its wings were plucked off, etc. (verse 5) And behold another, second beast, resembling a bear” that is Persia. And it is written (ad loc.) “And thus it was said to it, ‘Devour much flesh.’” i.e., seize the kingdom. And the kingdom of Persia was the blossoming of the horn of Israel, as it is said regarding Cyrus (Isa. 45:13): “He shall build My city and free My exiles.” Now, how do we know that the forty years of Egypt ended at that time? [The proof is that] Egypt was given into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar in the twenty-seventh [year] of Nebuchadnezzar, in the year that this prophecy was said to Ezekiel. Add forty years, and you have sixty-seven. Deduct from them forty-five for Nebuchadnezzar and twenty-three for Evil-Merodach, as we say in Megillah (11b), one of these years counting for both [kings], as we say there: “they were incomplete years.”

rashi.heb:
*ולך אתן פתחון פה בתוכם.* 
לך יחזקאל יהא פתחון פה כשיראו נבואתך מתקיימת:
rashi.eng: *and I will give you free speech in their midst.* You, Ezekiel, will have free speech when they see your prophecy being fulfilled.

rashi.heb:
*הה.* 
כמו אהה הה ליום העתיד לבא על אותן העכו"ם:
rashi.eng: *Ha!.* Like “Aha!” “Ha!” to the day that is destined to come upon those nations.

notes.948: (tn, Heb): “a day of clouds.” The expression occurs also in Joel 2:2 and Zeph 1:15; it recalls the appearance of God at Mount Sinai (Exod 19:9, 16, 18).
notes.949: (tn, Heb): “a time.” The words “of judgment” have been added in the translation for clarification (see the following verses).

rashi.heb:
*עת גוים.* 
עידן תבר עממיא:
rashi.eng: *the time of the nations.* The time of the destruction of the nations.

rashi.heb:
*והיתה חלחלה בכוש.* 
ל' רעד כשישמעו מפלת מצרים יחרדו לנפשם פן יעלה מלך בבל עליהם:
rashi.eng: *and there will be quaking in Cush.* [Heb. חַלְחָלָה,] expression of trembling. When they hear of Egypt’s downfall, they will fear for their lives: perhaps the king of Babylon will rise up against them.

notes.950: (tn): The same expression appears in Exod 12:38; Jer 25:20; 50:37; Neh 13:3. It may refer to foreign mercenaries serving in the armies of the nations listed here.
notes.952: (tn): The expression “sons of the covenant land” possibly refers to Jews living in Egypt (Jer 44).

rashi.heb:
*וכל הערב.* 
ת"י וכל סומכוותא כל העורבים ערובת מצרים גרנסי"אה בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *and all who support her.* [Heb. הָעֶרֶב וְכָל.] Jonathan renders: וְכָל סוּמְכָוָתָא, all those who guarantee the security of Egypt, garantie in French, guarantee.

rashi.heb:
*ארץ הברית.* 
כורתי ברית למצרים לעזור לה:
rashi.eng: *[and the people of] the allied land.* Those who made a treaty with Egypt to aid her.

notes.954: (sn): Syene is known as Aswan today.

notes.955: (tn, Heb): “all who aid her are broken.”

rashi.heb:
*בתתי אש.* 
חמתי כאש:
rashi.eng: *when I have set a fire.* My fury, which is like fire.

notes.956: (tn, Heb): “in the day of Egypt.” The word “doom” has been added in the translation to clarify the nature of this day.

rashi.heb:
*מלאכים מלפני.* 
גדודי גייסות הולכים בשליחותי בשיירות רבות להחריד את כוש היושבת בטח:
rashi.eng: *emissaries… from before Me.* Troops of armies going on My mission in many caravans to frighten Cush, which is dwelling securely.

rashi.heb:
*בצים.* 
כמו וצים מיד כתים (במדבר כ״ד:כ״ד) וכן תרגמו יונתן בלגיונין:
rashi.eng: *With legions.* [Heb. בַּצִים,] like (Num. 24:24): “And legions (וְצִים) from the place of the Kittites,” and so too did Jonathan render it: with legions.

notes.957: (tn, Heb): “Nebuchadrezzar” is a variant and more correct spelling of Nebuchadnezzar, as the Babylonian name Nabu-kudurri-usur has an “r” rather than an “n.”

notes.958: (tn): The Babylonians were known for their cruelty (2 Kgs 25:7).

notes.959: (tn, Heb): “and I will sell the land into the hand of.”

rashi.heb:
*ונתתי יאורים.* 
ארץ היאורים היא מצרים:
rashi.eng: *And I shall make the rivers.* the land of the rivers; that is, Egypt.

rashi.heb:
*ומכרתי.* 
כתרגומו ואימסר:
rashi.eng: *and I shall sell.* as the Targum renders: and I shall deliver.

notes.960: (tn, Heb): “I will put fear in the land of Egypt.”

rashi.heb:
*ועשיתי שפטים בנא.* 
אלכסנדריא:
rashi.eng: *and I shall execute punishments in No.* [This is] Alexandria.

notes.961: (tn, Heb): “Sin” (so KJV, NASB), a city commonly identified with Pelusium, a fortress on Egypt’s northeastern frontier.

notes.963: (tc): The LXX reads “Syene,” which is Aswan in the south. The MT reads Sin, which has already been mentioned in v. 15.

rashi.heb:
*להבקע.* 
חומתה תבקע:
rashi.eng: *to split.* Her wall will split.

rashi.heb:
*צרי יומם.* 
צרים יבאו עליה יום יום:
rashi.eng: *adversaries [will attack her] daily.* [Heb. צָרֵי יוֹמָם, lit. adversaries of days.] Adversaries will come upon her every day.

notes.964: (sn): On and Pi-beseth are generally identified with the Egyptian cities of Heliopolis and Bubastis.
notes.965: (tn, Heb): “they will go.” The pronoun and verb are feminine plural, indicating that the cities just mentioned are the antecedent of the pronoun and the subject of the verb. The translation makes this clear by stating the subject as “the cities.”

rashi.heb:
*והנה בשבי תלכנה.* 
שתיהן המדינות און ופיבסת:
rashi.eng: *and they will go into captivity.* both of them, the provinces of Aven and Pi beseth.

notes.966: (sn): In Zeph 1:15 darkness is associated with the day of the Lord.

rashi.heb:
*חשך היום.* 
ימנע האור:
rashi.eng: *the day will withdraw itself.* [Heb. חָשָּׁך הַיוֹם,] the light will be withheld

rashi.heb:
*ענן יכסנה.* 
צרה תבוא עליה ותכסנה ותחשך כיום כסוי הענן:
rashi.eng: *a cloud will cover her.* Trouble will come upon her and cover her, and it will become dark [for her] like a day covered with clouds.

rashi.heb:
*ובנותיה.* 
וכפרנהא:

notes.968: (sn): The expression “breaking the arm” indicates the removal of power (Ps 10:15; 37:17; Job 38:15; Jer 48:25).
notes.969: (sn): This may refer to the event recorded in Jer 37:5.

rashi.heb:
*את זרוע פרעה מלך מצרים שברתי.* 
כבר פעם אחרת שנתתי חילו ביד נבוכדנצר בשנה הרביעית ליהויקים כמה שנאמר בספר (ירמיהו מ״ו:ב׳) למצרים על חיל פרעה נכה מלך מצרים אשר היה בכרכמיש על נהר פרת אשר הכה נבוכדנצר וגומר:
rashi.eng: *I have broken the arm of Pharaoh, the king of Egypt.* already another time, for I placed his army in the hands of Nebuchadnezzar in the fourth year of Jehoiakim, as it is said in the Book of Jeremiah (46:2): “Concerning Egypt, concerning the army of Pharaoh-neco, the king of Egypt, which was on the Euphrates in Carcemish, whom King Nebuchadnezzar smote, etc.”

rashi.heb:
*והנה לא חובשה.* 
מאותו היום והלאה כמה שנאמ' בספר (מלכים ב כ״ד:ז׳) בסופו ולא יסף עוד מלך מצרים לצאת מארצו כי לקח מלך בבל מנהר פרת עד נחל מצרים ובסגנון זה נתנבא ירמי' גם הוא על אותה המכה בלשון רפואה אין לה שנאמר (ירמיהו מ״ו:י״א) עלי גלעד וקחי צרי בתולת בת מצרים לשוא הרבית רפואות תעלה אין לך:
rashi.eng: *and behold, it was not bound.* from that day on, as it is said at the end of the Book of Kings (II 24:7): “And the king of Egypt no longer went out of his land, for the king of Babylonia had taken from the river of Egypt,” and with this expression Jeremiah, too, prophesied concerning that blow, using the language “it has no cure,” as it is said (Jer. 46:11): “Go up to Gilead and take balm, O virgin daughter of Egypt; in vain you have increased medicines, you have no cure.”

rashi.heb:
*לא חובשה.* 
ל' קשירה שקושרין עצם הנשבר:
rashi.eng: *it was not bound.* חֻבָּשָּׁה is an expression of binding, for they bind the broken bone.

rashi.heb:
*לשום חתול.* 
מעשה בגדים ורטייה כמו (לעיל טז) והחתל לא חתלת:
rashi.eng: *to place a bandage [Heb..* חִתּוּל,] [a dressing] made of cloth and plaster, like (above 16:44): “nor swaddled at all (והֳחְתֵּל לֹא חֻתָּלְתְּ).”

rashi.heb:
*לתפוש בחרב.* 
שיהא לו עוד כח להלחם:
rashi.eng: *to grasp a sword.* that he should have more strength to wage war.

notes.970: (tn): The word h!nn@h indicates becoming aware of something and has been translated here as a verb.
notes.971: (tn): Or “I challenge you.” The phrase “I am against you” may be a formula for challenging someone to combat or a duel. See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 1:201-2, and P. Humbert, “Die Herausforderungsformel ‘h!nn#n' ?l?K>,’” ZAW 45 (1933): 101-8.

rashi.heb:
*ושברתי את זרועותיו.* 
אשבור את השנית ותהיינה שתיהן שבורות כלומר כבר לקח מלך בבל מצד הא' עוד אמסור לו יתר המלכות כולו:
rashi.eng: *and I shall break his arms.* I shall break the second [arm], and both of them will be broken; i.e., the king of Babylon took from one side; I shall yet give him the entire kingdom.

notes.972: (tn, Heb): “him”; the referent has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*וחזקתי.* 
לשון חוזק:
rashi.eng: *And I shall strengthen.* [Heb. וְחִזַּקְתִּי,] an expression of strength.

rashi.heb:
*והחזקתי.* 
ל' אחיזה שאוחז בידו לסמיכה שלא תפול וסופו יוכיח וזרועות פרעה תפולנה שאינו אוחז בהן:
rashi.eng: *And I shall grasp.* [Heb. וְהֲחֲזַּקְתִּי,] an expression of grasping, that one grasps his hand to support it so that it should not fall. The end of it proves it: “and the arms of Pharaoh will fall,” because He does not hold them.

rashi.heb:
*אל מי דמית בגדלך.* 
בהתגדלך לנגדי אל מי היית סבור לדמות:
rashi.eng: *Whom are you like in your greatness.* In your haughtiness against Me, whom did you think to resemble?

notes.974: (sn): Either Egypt, or the Lord compares Egypt to Assyria, which is described in vv. 3-17 through the metaphor of a majestic tree. See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 2:185. Like Egypt, Assyria had been a great world power, but in time God brought the Assyrians down. Egypt should learn from history the lesson that no nation, no matter how powerful, can withstand the judgment of God. Rather than following the text here, some prefer to emend the proper name Assyria to a similar sounding common noun meaning “boxwood” (see Ezek 27:6), which would make a fitting parallel to “cedar of Lebanon” in the following line. In this case vv. 3-18 in their entirety refer to Egypt, not Assyria. See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:121-27.
notes.975: (sn): Lebanon was know for its cedar trees (Judg 9:15; 1 Kgs 4:33; 5:6; 2 Kgs 14:9; Ezra 3:7; Pss 29:5; 92:12; 104:16).

rashi.heb:
*הנה אשור.* 
שהפלתי כבר:
rashi.eng: *Behold Assyria.* which I have already cast down.

rashi.heb:
*ארז בלבנון.* 
היה:
rashi.eng: *a cedar in Lebanon.* it was

rashi.heb:
*וחורש מצל.* 
יער מסכך צל גדול:
rashi.eng: *shady woods.* A forest that covers, [making] a great shade.

rashi.heb:
*ובין עבותים.* 
עצי רענן:
rashi.eng: *and among the interwoven branches.* the green trees.

rashi.heb:
*צמרתו.* 
צימ"א בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *its lofty tops.* [Heb. צַמַּרְתּוֹ,] cime in French, top.

notes.976: (tn, Heb): “Waters made it grow; the deep made it grow tall. It (the deep) was flowing with its rivers around the place it (the tree) was planted, it (the deep) sent out its channels to all the trees of the field.”

rashi.heb:
*תעלותיה.* 
פושיץ בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *Water nurtured it; the deep made it grow tall.* [Jonathan paraphrases:] Among nations he is great; because of his supporters he is powerful; he subjugates kings under his kingdom, and he appoints rulers over every state of the earth. The Midrash Aggadah (Pesikta Rabbathi 34:11, Meir Ayin 33) [states]: “and among the interwoven branches was its lofty top.” Whence did he merit greatness? Because 1) he withdrew from the counsel of the generation of separation, as it is said (Gen. 10:11): “Out of that land Asshur went forth. ” When all those who came upon the world formed one league to enter counsel to rebel against Him, then his lofty top was visible by itself, and [he] did not link himself with them.“Water nurtured him; the [waters of the] deep raised him up” and because 2) he hearkened to the voice of Jonah the son of Amittai, who descended into the [waters of the] deep, and the people of Nineveh repented of the violence that was in their hands.

rashi.heb:
*אל כל עצי השדה.* 
להשקותם והדוגמא כתרגומו של יונתן הא אתוראה דמיא לארזא בלבנון וגומר כבעמוד:
rashi.eng: *its canals.* [Heb. תְּעָלתֶיהָ,] fosses in French, ditches, canals.

rashi.heb:
*מים גדלוהו תהום רוממתהו.* 
בעממיא סגי בסומכוותא תקוף ית מלכיא שעביד לתחות מלכותיה וית שלטונוהי מני על כל מדינות ארעא, ומדרש אגדה ובין עבותים היתה צמרתו מהיכן זכה לגדולה לפי שנמנע מעצת דור הפלגה שנאמר (בראשית ז) מן הארץ ההיא יצא אשור כשנעשו כל באי העולם קליעה אחת לבוא בעצה למרוד בו אז היתה צמרתו נראית לעצמה ולא נשתלשלה עמהם. מים גדלוהו תהום רוממתהו. ועל ששמע לקול יונה בן אמתי שירד לתהום ושבו אנשי ננוה מן החמס אשר בכפיהם:
rashi.eng: *to all the trees of the field.* to water them. The symbol is as the Targum of Jonathan interprets it: Behold the Assyrians were like the cedars of Lebanon, etc., as above.

notes.977: (tn, Heb): “when it sends forth.” Repointing the consonants of the Masoretic text would render the proposed reading “shoots” (cf. NRSV).

rashi.heb:
*סרעפותיו.* 
ענפיו:
rashi.eng: *its boughs.* [Heb. סַרְעַפֹּתָיו,]

rashi.heb:
*פארותיו.* 
זמורותיו:
rashi.eng: *its branches.* [Heb. פֹארֹתָיו.]

rashi.heb:
*ממים רבים בשלחו.* 
פארותיו על ידי מים רבים בשלחו פארותיו כלומר בגדלו פארותיו ול' שילוח נופל בהן כמו ותשלח פאורות (לעיל טז):
rashi.eng: *because of abundant waters when it sent forth.* its branches through the abundant waters. When it sent forth its branches, i.e., when it grew its branches, and the expression “sending” applies to them, as “and sent forth branches.”

rashi.heb:
*בסעפותיו.* 
בענפיו:
rashi.eng: *In its boughs.* [Heb. בִּסְעַפֹתָיו.]

rashi.heb:
*קננו.* 
ל' קן:
rashi.eng: *nested.* [Heb. קִנְנוּ,] from the word קֵּן, nest.

rashi.heb:
*וייף.* 
ל' יופי:
rashi.eng: *And it became beautiful.* [Heb. וַיִיף,] an expression of beauty (יֹפִי).

rashi.heb:
*דליותיו.* 
אף הם ל' ענפים הנטוים לאורך לכל צד כמין דליות הכרם שישטרוי"ילאש בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *its tendrils.* [Heb. דָּלִיוֹתָיו.] They too are an expression used for branches: [those] that extend lengthwise in every direction, like the tendrils of a vineyard, ses treilles in French, its climbing vines.

notes.979: (tn): Or “cypress trees” (cf. NASB, NLT); NIV “pine trees.”

rashi.heb:
*לא עממוהו.* 
לא כהו תארו כלומר לא היה בהם אחד נאה ממנו:
rashi.eng: *did not dim it.* They did not dim its form; i.e., none among them surpassed it in beauty.

rashi.heb:
*בגן אלהים.* 
כלומר בכל העולם:
rashi.eng: *in the garden of God.* i.e., in the entire world.

rashi.heb:
*וערמונים.* 
קאשטיני"ש בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *and chestnut trees.* [Heb. ועֲרְמֹנִים,] chastaniyers, chastaneyrs in Old French [chataigniers in Modern French].

rashi.heb:
*כל עצי עדן.* 
כלומר כל המלכים המשובחים:
rashi.eng: *all the trees of Eden.* i.e., all the praiseworthy kings.

rashi.heb:
*יען אשר גבהת בקומה.* 
כך אמרתי לאשור:
rashi.eng: *Because you grew haughty with your height.* So I said to Assyria.

notes.980: (tn, Heb): “acting he has acted with regard to it.” The infinitive absolute precedes the main verb to emphasize the certainty and decisiveness of the action depicted.

rashi.heb:
*ביד אל גוים.* 
ביד קשה שבגוים ביד נבוכדנצר נתתיו דאמר מר שנה ראשונה כבש ננוה:
rashi.eng: *into the hands of the strongest of nations.* into the hands of the harshest of nations; I gave him into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar, as the master said (Seder Olam, ch. 24; Meg. 11b; Arachin 12a): In his first year, he conquered Nineveh.

rashi.heb:
*עשו יעשה לו.* 
נבוכדנצר ככל רצוני:
rashi.eng: *that he execute upon him.* [that] Nebuchadnezzar [execute upon him] in accordance with all My wishes.

rashi.heb:
*ויטשוהו.* 
ויפלוהו לארץ כמו ויטש על המחנה (במדבר י״א:ל״א):
rashi.eng: *cast it down.* [Heb. וַיִטְשֻּׁהוּ,] and they cast it down to the earth, like (Num. 11:31): “and let them down (וַיִטשּׁ) upon the camp.”

notes.983: (tn, Heb): “the beasts of the field,” referring to wild as opposed to domesticated animals.

rashi.heb:
*על מפלתו ישכנו וגו'.* 
כתרגומו על מפלת קטילוהי:
rashi.eng: *Upon its carcass… rested.* as the Targum paraphrases: Upon the carcass of his slain.

notes.985: (tn, Heb): “and they will not stand to them in their height, all the drinkers of water.”
notes.986: (tn, Heb): “for death, to the lower earth.”

rashi.heb:
*עצי מים.* 
שהם רכים וחלשים אלא שענפיהם רכים וארוכין מחמת לחלוחית המים אין להם לדמות עצמן לארזי עדן כלומר לא היה לו להתגאות על ישראל ולא יעמדו עליהם:
rashi.eng: *water trees.* which are tender and frail, but have numerous and long branches because of the moisture of the water, should not compare themselves to the cedars of Eden; i.e., he should not have been haughty over Israel and should not have stood over them.

rashi.heb:
*אל בין עבותים.* 
לא יתגאו להשוות גבורתם שותה מים אל עצי עבותים:
rashi.eng: *among the interwoven branches.* They should not haughtily compare their might - the trees that drink water to the interwoven trees.

notes.989: (tn, Heb): “I caused lamentation.” D. I. Block (Ezekiel [NICOT], 2:194-95) proposes an alternative root which would give the meaning “I gated back the waters,” i.e., shut off the water supply.

rashi.heb:
*ביום רדתו שאולה.* 
כשהשפלתי את מלך אשור ביד אויבו:
rashi.eng: *On the day he descended into the Grave.* When I humbled the king of Assyria into the hands of his enemy.

rashi.heb:
*האבלתי כסתי עליו.* 
אבלים רבים שהיו סמוכין עליו:
rashi.eng: *I caused mourning.* [I caused] many mourners who relied on him [to mourn] over him.

rashi.heb:
*כסיתי עליו את תהום.* 
כסיתי בשבילו את תהום שהיה רגיל להשקותו ולגדלו כמו שאמר למעלה תהום רוממתהו אותו היום כסיתיו שלא יעלה ויכבה את תבערתו כלומר החלטתי את עוזריו:
rashi.eng: *I covered the deep on his account.* I covered the deep because of him, for it was accustomed to water him and cause his growth, as Scripture stated above (verse 4): “the deep made it grow tall.” That day, I covered it so that it should not ascend and extinguish his fire. i.e., I weakened his aids.

rashi.heb:
*ואמנע נהרותיה.* 
שהיו הולכין סביבות מטעה:
rashi.eng: *I withdrew its rivers.* which were flowing around its planting.

rashi.heb:
*ויכלאו מים רבים.* 
שהיו מאריכין פארות כמו שאמר למעלה ותארכנה פארות' ממים רבים:
rashi.eng: *abundant waters stopped.* [The waters] that used to make its branches grow long, as he said above (verse 5): “and its branches grew long because of abundant waters.”

rashi.heb:
*ואקדיר.* 
בשבילו לבנון:
rashi.eng: *and I darkened.* the Lebanon because of him.

rashi.heb:
*ואקדיר.* 
לשון שחרות:
rashi.eng: *and I darkened.*  [Heb. וָאַקְדִיר,] from an expression for blackness.

rashi.heb:
*וכל עצי השדה.* 
שהיו תעלותיו שלוחין אליהם כמו שאמר למעלה:
rashi.eng: *and all the trees of the field.* to which his channels were sent, as stated above.

rashi.heb:
*עליו עולפה.* 
בשבילו פסק לחלוחם כאדם שמתעלף ורוחו פורחת פשמי"ר בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *swooned over him.* Because of him, their moisture ceased, as a person who swoons and whose spirit flies away [i.e., he loses consciousness]; pasmer in Old French, to faint, to swoon. [pamer in Modern French.]

notes.990: (sn): For the expression “going down to the pit,” see Ezek 26:20; 32:18, 24, 29.

rashi.heb:
*וינחמו בארץ תחתית.* 
שאר יורדי גיהנם קבלו תנחומים אמרו אף זה כמונו:
rashi.eng: *and they were consoled in the nether part of the earth.* The others who descended to Gehinnom received consolations. They said, “This one is like us also.”

rashi.heb:
*וזרועו ישבו בצלו.* 
ועוזריו אשר ישבו בצלו:
rashi.eng: *and his allies, who dwelt in his shade.* [Heb. וּזְרֹעוֹ, lit. and his arm,] and his helpers, who dwelt in his shade.

rashi.heb:
*אל מי דמית ככה.* 
אתה פרעה אל מי מעצי עדן דמית שיהא ככה גדול כאשור בכבוד ובגודל והרי ראית שהורדתיו שאול ואף אתה והורדת עם עצי עדן עם שאר מלכים חזקים:
rashi.eng: *To whom have you likened yourself so.* You, Pharaoh, to which of the trees of Eden have you likened yourself, who is as great as Assyria in glory and in greatness? Behold you have seen that I lowered him into the Grave, and you too will be lowered with the trees of Eden, with the other strong monarchs.

rashi.heb:
*אל ארץ תחתית.* 
גיהנ':
rashi.eng: *into the nether part of the earth.* Gehinnom.

notes.993: (tn): The lion was a figure of royalty (Ezek 19:1-9).
notes.994: (tc): The Hebrew reads “their streams”; the LXX reads “your streams.”

rashi.heb:
*כפיר גוים נדמית ואתה כתנים בימים.* 
היה לך לרבוץ תוך יאורך כמשפט הדגים ולא לצאת אל היבשה ונתגאית בלבך ונדמית בעצמך לכפיר השליט ביבשה ויצא לטרוף טרף:
rashi.eng: *You resembled a young lion among the nations, but you are like a crocodile in the seas.* You should have lain in the midst of your rivers, as is the custom of the fish, and not gone out to the dry land; but you were haughty in your heart, and you compared yourself to a young lion, which dominates the dry land and goes forth to tear prey.

rashi.heb:
*ותגח בנהרותיך.* 
ותצא חוץ עם נהרותיך לשון גוחי מבטן (תהלים כ"ו) כי יגיח ירדן (איוב מא) ואורב ישראל מגיח ממקומו (שופטים כ׳:ל״ג) לשון דבר הנוגע ויוצא מבית מסתרים:
rashi.eng: *and you went out with your rivers.* [Heb. וַתָּגַח,] and you went out with your rivers, the same meaning as in (Ps. 22:10): “You drew me (גֹחִי) from the womb;” (Job 40:23), “he will draw (יָגִיחַ) the Jordan into his mouth;” Jud. 20:33), “And the liers in wait of Israel drew forth (מֵגִיחַ).” [This is] an expression for something flowing and going out of a hidden place.

rashi.heb:
*ותדלח.* 
לשון עכירה:
rashi.eng: *and you sullied.* [Heb. וַתִּדְלַח,] an expression of making something murky.

rashi.heb:
*ברגליך.* 
רגלים לא היו לך ועשית לך רגלים כחית הארץ לעבור מימי ארצות ולרפוס נהרות' והדוגמא בתרגום יונתן ואגחתא במשרייתך ואזעא עממיא בסומכוות' ואחריבת' מדינתהון:
rashi.eng: *with your feet.* You had no feet, but I made for you feet like the beasts of the earth, to cross the waters of the lands and to tread their rivers. The symbolism is like Targum Jonathan: and you waged war with your camps and you caused the peoples to quake with your supporters, and you destroyed their countries.

notes.995: (tn): The expression “throw my net” is common in Ezekiel (12:13; 17:20; 19:8).

rashi.heb:
*בחרמי.* 
ל' מצודה והרבה יש במקרא יגורהו בחרמו (חבקוק א׳:ט״ו) מצודים וחרמים (קהלת ז):
rashi.eng: *with My net.* [Heb. בְּחֶרְמִי,] a word for a net, and there are many in Scriptures, [e.g.,] (Hab. 1:15): “he catches them in his net (בְּחֶרְמוֹ);” (Ecc. 7:26), “snares and nets (וַחֲרָמִים).”

notes.999: (tn, Heb): “the beasts of the field,” referring to wild as opposed to domesticated animals.

notes.1000: (tc): The Hebrew text is difficult here, apparently meaning “your height.” Following Symmachus and the Syriac, it is preferable to emend the text to read “your maggots.” See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 2:203.

rashi.heb:
*ומלאתי הגאיות רמותיך.* 
השלכתיך כמו רמה בים (שמות ט״ו:א׳), ויש אומרים רמותיך לשון רמה כמו וירם תולעים ויבאש (שם ט"ז):
rashi.eng: *and I shall fill the valleys with what is cast off from you.* [Heb. רָמוּתֶךְ] your casting, like (Exod. 15:1): “He cast (רָמָה) into the sea.” Others say that רָמוּתֶךְ is meant as a form of the word for worm (רִמָה), like (ibid. 16:20): “and it became alive with worms (וַיָרֻם).”

rashi.heb:
*והשקיתי ארץ צפתך.* 
ארץ אשר אתה צף בה על פני מימי יאורך כמו (איכה ג׳:נ״ד) צפו מים על ראשי (מלכים ב' ז') ויצף הברזל אותה הארץ אשקה מדמך:
rashi.eng: *And I shall water… the land where you float.* [Heb. צָפָתְךָ,] the land where you float on the surface of the water of your rivers-like (Lam. 3:54): “Water floated (צָפוּ) over my head;” (II Kings 6:6): “and the axe blade floated (וַיָצֶף)” - that land I will water with your blood.

rashi.heb:
*צפתך.* 
טונפרוט"מנט בלע"ז, על ההרים הגבוהין שבה:
rashi.eng: *even to the mountains.* the highest [mountains] in it. צָפָתְ is ton flottement in French, your floating, swimming.

rashi.heb:
*ואפיקים.* 
ראויר"ש בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *and the streams.* [Heb. וַאֲפִיקִים,] riveyes in Old French, gullies, gulches; streams.

notes.1002: (tn, Heb): “will not shine its light.” For similar features of cosmic eschatology, see Joel 2:10; 4:15; Amos 5:18-20; Zeph 1:5.

rashi.heb:
*וכסיתי בכבותך שמים.* 
כשתכבה תבערתך יעלה העשן ויכסה השמים ויחשיך המאורות כלומר כל שומעי שמעך יתאבלו וישתוממו כי ידאג איש לנפשו לאמר גם עלינו יעמוד המשחית:
rashi.eng: *And with your smoke I will cover the heavens.* [Heb. בְּכַבּוֹתְךָ, lit. with you extinguishing.] When your conflagration will be extinguished, the smoke will rise and cover the sky and darken the luminaries; i.e., all who hear the news of what happened to you will mourn and be astonished, because everyone will worry about himself, saying, “The destroyer will stand up over us as well.”

rashi.heb:
*כל מאורי אור בשמים.* 
שרים של מעלה מליציך:
rashi.eng: *All the bright lights in the heavens.* the heavenly princes, your intercessors.

notes.1003: (tn, Heb): “I will provoke the heart of.”

rashi.heb:
*והכעסתי לב.* 
כלומר ירגז ויחרד לבם:
rashi.eng: *And I will vex the heart.* i.e., their heart will tremble and quake.

rashi.heb:
*בהביאי שברך.* 
באיתיותי תבירי קרבך לביני עממיא:
rashi.eng: *when I bring your ruin.* when I bring the ruin of your battles among the peoples.

rashi.heb:
*והשמותי.* 
לשון תמהון:
rashi.eng: *And I will cause… to be appalled.* [Heb. וַהֲשִּׁוֹתִי,] an expression of bewilderment.

rashi.heb:
*בעופפי חרבי על פניהם.* 
לשון עוף פורח בשלחי עליך חיל שלוחי דרך ארצם:
rashi.eng: *when I cause My sword to fly before their faces.* [Heb. בְּעוֹפְפִי,] an expression of a flying bird, when I send upon you the army of My emissaries through their land.

rashi.heb:
*וחרדו לרגעים.* 
לשברים פן גם עליהן יבא השבר ל"א לשון רגע ממש כן חברו מנחם:
rashi.eng: *and they will quake at their ruin.* [Heb. לִרְגָעִים,] to ruins, lest ruin come upon them as well. Another explanation: an expression of an actual moment (רֶגַע). In this sense, Menachem (p. 162) connects it.

rashi.heb:
*איש לנפשו.* 
כל אחד על עצמו שויימ"אימאש בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *everyone for himself.* each one concerning himself, soi-meme in French, for himself.

notes.1004: (sn): The king of Babylon referred to here was Nebuchadnezzar (Ezek 21:19).

notes.1007: (tn, Heb): “them,” that is, the waters mentioned in the previous line. The translation clarifies the referent.

rashi.heb:
*מעל מים.* 
של שאר מדינות שהיית עוכרם:
rashi.eng: *from beside… waters.* of other countries that you used to sully.

notes.1008: (tn, Heb): “sink,” that is, to settle and become clear, not muddied.

rashi.heb:
*אשקיע מימיהם.* 
שלא תעכרם רגל בהמה וישקע הטיט ויהו המים צלולין ונקיים כשמן המזוקק:
rashi.eng: *I shall sink their waters.* The foot of cattle will not make it murky, and the mud will sink, so that the water will be clear and clean like refined oil.

rashi.heb:
*ארץ ממלואה.* 
ארץ שהיא עתה ממלואה מכל טוב:
rashi.eng: *a land that is full.* [Heb. אֶרֶץמִמְלוֹאָה, a land that is now full (מִמְוּלָאָה) of all goodness.

notes.1009: (tn): March 17, 585 b.c. The LXX adds “first month.”

notes.1010: (tn): The Hebrew verb is used as a response to death (Jer 9:17-19; Amos 5:16).
notes.1011: (sn): Through this prophetic lament given by God himself, the prophet activates the judgment described therein. See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 2:217, and L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:136-37.
notes.1012: (tn, Heb): “Bring him down, her and the daughters of the powerful nations, to the earth below.” The verb “bring down” appears in the Hebrew text only once. Because the verb takes several objects here, the repetition of the verb in the translation improves the English style.
notes.1013: (tn): This apparently refers to personified Egypt.

rashi.heb:
*נהה.* 
בכה וקונן:
rashi.eng: *lament.* Weep and lament.

rashi.heb:
*והורידהו אותה ובנות וגו'.* 
התנבא עליו ועל כל מכחישי הנבואה שירדו לבאר שחת כאן הראהו הקב"ה ליחזקאל שכל מכחישי הנבואה יורדין לגיהנ':
rashi.eng: *and bring it down, it and the daughters, etc..* prophesy, about him and about all the heathens, that they will descend into the Pit of Destruction. Here the Holy One, blessed be He, showed Ezekiel that all the heathens descend to Gehinnom.

notes.1014: (tc): The LXX places this verse after v. 21. The words “say to them” are added in the translation for clarity to indicate the shift in addressee from the prophet to Egypt.

rashi.heb:
*ממי נעמת.* 
כלום נעמת משאר העכו"ם אף אתה רדה לבור והשכבה אותם:
rashi.eng: *Whom have you surpassed in pleasantness.* Are you any better than the other uncircumcised ones? You too will descend into the Pit and lie with them.

rashi.heb:
*חרב נתנה.* 
לחרב נתנה מצרים:
rashi.eng: *it was delivered to the sword.* Egypt was delivered to the sword.

rashi.heb:
*ידברו לו.* 
ידברו עליו ועל עוזריו:
rashi.eng: *shall speak of him.* [Heb. יְדַבְּרוּ לוֹ] shall speak of him and of his helpers.

rashi.heb:
*אלי גבורים מתוך שאול.* 
סרס המקרא ודרשהו ידברו לו את עוזריו עם עוזריו כלומר גם על עוזריו אתו ידברו אילי גבורים שבשאול וככה יאמרו עליהם ירדו:
rashi.eng: *the strongest of the mighty men… from the midst of the Grave.* Transpose the verse and interpret it: They shall speak of him אֶת עֹזרָיו, with his helpers; i.e., concerning all his helpers with him, too, shall the strongest of the mighty men, who are in the Grave, speak, and they will say about them thus:

rashi.heb: *שכבו הערלים וגו'.*  כל לו ולי ולהם ולך הסמוכין לדבור אינם אלא לשון על:
rashi.eng: *the uncircumcised… descended, etc..* Every לָהֶם, לִי, לוֹ, and לְךָ written next to דִבּוּר, speech, means nothing but “about.”

notes.1016: (tn, Heb): “around him his graves.” The masculine pronominal suffixes are problematic; the expression is best emended to correspond to the phrase “around her grave” in v. 23. See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 2:219.
notes.1017: (tn, Heb): “all of them slain, the ones felled by the sword.” See as well vv. 23-24.

rashi.heb:
*שם אשור.* 
בגיהנ':
rashi.eng: *There are Assyria.* in Gehinnom.

rashi.heb:
*סביבותיו.* 
בתוך שאול קברותיו מוכנין כי משם לא יצא לנוח בקברו:
rashi.eng: *around it [are its graves].* In the midst of the Grave its graves are prepared, for from there it will not emerge to rest in a grave.

notes.1019: (tn): The only other occurrence of the phrase “remote slopes of the pit” is in Isa 14:15.

rashi.heb:
*בירכתי בור.* 
במעמקי בור בתוך עמקו:
rashi.eng: *in the utmost part of the Pit.* in the depths of the Pit; in the midst of its depth.

rashi.heb:
*ויהי קהלה.* 
בתוך שאול סביבות קבורתה:
rashi.eng: *and whose company was.* in the midst of the Grave, “was around its grave.”

rashi.heb:
*אשר נתנו חתית.* 
אשר נתנו שבר בארץ ישראל:
rashi.eng: *who cast destruction.* [Heb. חִתִית,] who cast destruction in the land of Israel.

notes.1020: (tn, Heb): “around him her graves,” but the expression is best emended to read “around her grave” (see vv. 23-24).

rashi.heb:
*נתנו משכב לה.* 
לעול':
rashi.eng: *they provided a bed for her.* for Elam.

notes.1021: (tn, Heb): “around him her graves,” but the expression is best emended to read “around her grave” (see vv. 23-24).

rashi.heb:
*מחוללי.* 
כמו הרוגי:
rashi.eng: *slain by the sword.* [Heb. מְחֻלְלֵי,] like הֲרוּגֵי.

notes.1022: (tc, Heb): “of the uncircumcised.” The LXX reads, probably correctly, “from of old” rather than “of the uncircumcised.” The phrases are very similar in spelling. The warriors of Meshech-Tubal are described as uncircumcised, so it would be odd for them to not be buried with the uncircumcised. Verse 28 specifically says that they would lie with the uncircumcised.
notes.1023: (tn, Heb): “and their iniquities were over their bones.” The meaning of this statement is unclear; in light of the parallelism (see “swords”) it is preferable to emend “their iniquities” to “their swords.” See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:135.

rashi.heb:
*ולא ישכבו.* 
אלה הנזכרים עם גבורים שמתו מיתת עצמם כי נופלין וגרועים יהיו מהעכו"ם אשר מתו מיתת עצמם וירדו בכלי מלחמתם שאול:
rashi.eng: *But they will not lie.* These who were mentioned [will not lie] with the mighty who died a natural death, for they will be inferior to and worse than the uncircumcised who died a natural death and descended with their weapons into the Grave.

rashi.heb:
*ויתנו.* 
קובריהם:
rashi.eng: *and they laid.* i.e., those who buried them [laid]…

rashi.heb:
*את חרבותם תחת ראשיהם.* 
לסימן להודיע כי לא שלטה בהם חרב:
rashi.eng: *their swords under their heads.* as a sign to make it known that the sword did not prevail over them.

rashi.heb:
*ותהי עוונותם על עצמותם.* 
לא נחסר מעוונם כלום שלא כפרה עליהם חרב הריגה שלא נהרגו ומה הוא העון כי חתית הגבורים ההם היתה בארץ חיים:
rashi.eng: *and their iniquities were upon their bones.* Nothing was lacking from their iniquity, for the slaying sword did not expiate it, because they were not slain. Now what is the iniquity? That the destruction wrought by these mighty men was in the land of the living.

rashi.heb:
*ואתה בתוך.* 
לפרעה הוא אומר:
rashi.eng: *And you - in the midst of the uncircumcised.* He is addressing Pharaoh.

rashi.heb:
*את חללי חרב.* 
ולא עם המתים מיתת עצמם:
rashi.eng: *with those slain by the sword.* and not with those who die a natural death.

rashi.heb:
*בחתיתם מגבורתם בושים.* 
באתברותהון מגבורתהון בהתון:
rashi.eng: *ashamed when they are destroyed in spite of their might.* [Jonathan renders:] When they are broken in spite of their might, they are ashamed.

rashi.heb:
*כי נתתי את.* 
חתיתי בארץ חיים כי אתן אני את מוראי בארץ ישראל ולא תנתן עוד חתית אדם בה:
rashi.eng: *For I shall cast My fear into the land of the living.* For I shall cast My fear into the land of the living and the fear of man will no longer be cast therein.

rashi.heb:
*לצופה.* 
באדי"טא בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *as a lookout.* [Heb. לְצֹפֶה,] badete in O. F., sentry, watchman.

notes.1025: (tn, Heb): “shofar,” a ram’s horn rather than a brass instrument (so throughout the chapter).
notes.1026: (tn): Sounding the trumpet was a warning of imminent danger (Neh 4:18-20; Jer 4:19; Amos 3:6).

rashi.heb:
*וראה את החרב.* 
המה הגייסות:
rashi.eng: *And he sees the army.* [lit. the sword.] They are the armies.

notes.1027: (tn, Heb): “his blood will be on his own head.”

rashi.heb:
*דמו בראשו יהיה.* 
עון מיתתו ידרש מיד עצמו שפשע בנפשו:
rashi.eng: *his blood will be on his own head.* The iniquity of causing his death will be required of himself, because he has neglected his life.

notes.1028: (tn, Heb): “his blood will be on him.”

rashi.heb:
*והוא נזהר נפשו מלט.* 
אם נזהר היה נמלט:
rashi.eng: *for had he taken heed, he would have saved his life.* Had he taken heed, he would have escaped.

notes.1029: (tn): Or “in his punishment.” The phrase “in/for [a person’s] iniquity/punishment” occurs fourteen times in Ezekiel: here and in vv. 8 and 9; 3:18, 19; 4:17; 7:13, 16; 18: 17, 18, 19, 20; 24:23; 39:23. The Hebrew word for “iniquity” may also mean the “punishment” for iniquity or “guilt” of iniquity.
notes.1030: (tn, Heb): “his blood from the hand of the watchman I will seek.”

notes.1031: (sn): Jeremiah (Jer 6:17) and Habakkuk (Hab 2:1) also served in the role of a watchman.

rashi.heb:
*צופה נתתיך.* 
כאותו הצופה הניתן להזהיר שלא תאבד נפש כן נתתיך להזהיר את ישראל:
rashi.eng: *I have made you a lookout.* Like that lookout, who is appointed to give warning so that no soul be lost, so have I appointed you to warn Israel.

notes.1032: (tn): The same expression occurs in Gen 2:17.
notes.1033: (tn, Heb): “and you do not speak to warn.”
notes.1035: (tn, Heb): “and his blood from your hand I will seek.”

notes.1036: (tn, Heb): “from his way to turn from it.”
notes.1037: (tn, Heb): “and he does not turn from his way.”

rashi.heb:
*כן אמרתם.* 
לפיכך אין אתם חפצים לשוב כסבורין אתם שלא תועיל לכם תשובה:
rashi.eng: *So have you spoken.* Therefore, you do not wish to repent, because you believe that repentance will not avail you.

notes.1040: (tn, Heb): “ways.” This same word is translated “behavior” earlier in the verse.

notes.1042: (tn, Heb): “in the day of his rebellion.” The statement envisions a godly person rejecting what is good and becoming sinful. See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 2:247-48.
notes.1043: (tn, Heb): “and the wickedness of the wicked, he will not stumble in it in the day of his turning from his wickedness.”
notes.1045: (tn, Heb): “in the day of his sin.”

rashi.heb:
*לחיות בה.* 
בצדקתו:
rashi.eng: *live with it.* with his righteousness.

rashi.heb:
*לא תזכרנה.* 
להצילו מליענש על עבירה זו:
rashi.eng: *none… will be remembered.* to save him from being punished for his sin.

notes.1047: (tn, Heb): “and in the statutes of life he walks.”

rashi.heb:
*חבול.* 
עבוט שצויתי להשיבו כבא השמש:
rashi.eng: *the pledge.* the pledge that I commanded [one] to return at sunset.

notes.1051: (tn): The Hebrew verb translated “is (not) right” has the basic meaning of “to measure.” For a similar concept, see Ezek 18:25, 29.

rashi.heb:
*ומת בהם.* 
בשבילם יענש:
rashi.eng: *he will die because of them.* He will be punished for them.

notes.1054: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

notes.1056: (tn): The other occurrences of the phrase “the hand of the Lord” in Ezekiel are in the context of prophetic visions.
notes.1057: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.1058: (tn, Heb): “by the time of the arrival to me.” For clarity the translation specifies the refugee as the one who arrived.

rashi.heb:
*ויפתח את פי.* 
כמו שאמר בראש הספר (לעיל ג) ונאלמת ולא תהיה לאיש מוכיח ואח"כ אמר לו (לעיל כד) ביום קחתי מהם את מעוז' יבא הפליט אליך ביום ההוא יפתח פיך את הפליט ולא תאלם עוד:
rashi.eng: *and He opened my mouth.* as He says in the beginning of the Book (3:26): “and you shall become mute, and you shall not be a reprover to them.” Afterward, He said to him (24:25ff.): “on the day I take from them their strength, etc., the fugitive will come to you, etc., on that day, your mouth will be opened with the fugitive, and you will speak and no longer be mute.”

rashi.heb:
*עד בוא אלי בבקר.* 
כלומר בעוד בואו אלי בבקר כמו לפני בואו אלי בבקר:
rashi.eng: *before [his] coming to me in the morning.* [Heb. עַד בּוֹא אֵלִי בַּבֹּקֶר,] i.e., when he had not yet (בְּעוֹד) come to me in the morning, like: before he came to me in the morning.

notes.1060: (sn): Outside of its seven occurrences in Ezekiel the term translated “possession” appears only in Exod 6:8 and Deut 33:4.

rashi.heb:
*אחד היה אברהם.* 
זה אחד מד' דברים שהיה רבי עקיבא דורש ואין רבי שמעון בן יוחאי תלמידו דורש כמותו וכך היה רבי שמעון דורשו אברהם שלא נצטווה אלא על מצווה אחת ירש את הארץ אנו שנצטוינו על מצות הרבה כל שכן שלנו נתנה הארץ למורשה הוא שהנביא משיבם:
rashi.eng: *Abraham was one.* This is one of four things that Rabbi Akiva interpreted [in one way] and which his disciple, Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai, did not interpret as he did. Rabbi Shimon interpreted it in this manner: Abraham, who was commanded with only one commandment [namely circumcision], inherited the land. We, then, who have been commanded with many commandments, should surely have the land given to us for an inheritance (Tosefta Sotah 6: 7). This is what the prophet answers them.

notes.1061: (sn): This practice was a violation of Levitical law (see Lev 19:26).

rashi.heb:
*על הדם תאכלו וגו'.* 
והארץ תירשו בתמיה אם נצטויתם אין אתם שומרים על הדם תאכלו את מאכלי תפנוקים אתם אוכלים על ידי רציחה שהורגין את בעלי ממון ונוטלין את ממונם:
rashi.eng: *You eat on the blood, etc., and you should inherit the land.* This is a rhetorical question. If you were commanded [many commandments], you do not keep [them]. You eat on the blood: you eat delicacies through murder, for you slay those who have money and take away their money.

rashi.heb:
*עמדתם על חרבכם.* 
כלומר כל בטחונכם נתחזקתם על חרבכם:
rashi.eng: *You stood on your sword.* i.e., all your trust. You strengthened yourself on your sword.

rashi.heb:
*עשיתן תועבה.* 
משכב זכור:
rashi.eng: *you committed abominations.* homosexual acts.

rashi.heb:
*אשר בחרבות.* 
בערים הבצורות שסופן להיות חריבים:
rashi.eng: *those who are in the ruins.* in the fortified cities that will ultimately become ruins.

rashi.heb:
*ואשר במצדות.* 
במחבא להטמן מן החרב אשלח בם את הדבר:
rashi.eng: *and those who are in the strongholds.* in a hideout, to hide from the sword - I shall send the pestilence upon them.

notes.1066: (sn): The judgments of vv. 27-29 echo the judgments of Lev 26:22, 25.

notes.1068: (tn, Heb): “one to one, a man to his brother.”

rashi.heb:
*הנדברים בך.* 
מתלוצצים בך:
rashi.eng: *who talk about you.* who mock you.

notes.1070: (tn, Heb): “as people come.” Apparently this is an idiom indicating that they come in crowds. See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 2:264.
notes.1071: (tn): The word “as” is supplied in the translation.
notes.1073: (tn, Heb): “They do lust with their mouths.”
notes.1075: (tn): The present translation understands the term often used for “unjust gain” in a wider sense, following M. Greenberg, who also notes that the LXX uses a term which can describe either sexual or ritual pollution. See M. Greenberg, Ezekiel (AB), 2:687.

rashi.heb:
*וישבו לפניך.* 
כאילו הם עמי:
rashi.eng: *and they will sit before you as My people.* as if they were My people.

rashi.heb:
*עגבים.* 
שחוק כמו עוגב:
rashi.eng: *jokes.* [Heb. עֲגָבִים,] laughter, related to עוּגָב, a flute.

rashi.heb:
*בצעם.* 
גזילתם:
rashi.eng: *their gain.* their stolen goods.

notes.1076: (tn): The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) indicates becoming aware of something and has been translated here as a verb.
notes.1077: (tn, Heb): “one who makes playing music well.”
notes.1078: (sn): Similar responses are found in Isa 29:13; Matt 21:28-32; James 1:22-25.

rashi.heb:
*והנך להם כשיר עגבים.* 
והא את להון כזמר אבובין:
rashi.eng: *And you are to them as a song on the flute.* And you are to them as a song on the flute.

rashi.heb:
*ובבאה.* 
הרעה אליהם:
rashi.eng: *And when it comes.* the evil to them.

rashi.heb:
*הנה באה.* 
כי אמת מוכנת היא לבא אז ידעו כי לא שחוק היו דבריך כי נביא אמת היה בתוכם:
rashi.eng: *behold it is coming.* for, indeed, it is ready to come; then they will know that your words were not a jest, but that a true prophet was in their midst.

notes.1080: (tn): The term shepherd is applied to kings in the ancient Near East. In the OT the Lord is often addressed as shepherd of Israel (Gen 49:24; Ps 8:1). The imagery of shepherds as Israel’s leaders is also employed (Jer 23:1-2).

rashi.heb:
*על רועי ישראל.* 
על פרנסי ישראל:
rashi.eng: *concerning the shepherds of Israel.* concerning the leaders of Israel.

rashi.heb:
*אשר היו רועים אותם.* 
את עצמם היו מענגין מממון חבריהם אשר תחתיהם:
rashi.eng: *who were shepherding themselves.* [Heb. אוֹתָם,] them. They enjoyed themselves with the money of their fellows who were under them.

rashi.heb:
*הלא הצאן ירעו הרועים.* 
הלא משפט הרועים לרעות את הצאן ולא לרעות את עצמן:
rashi.eng: *Do not the shepherds shepherd the flocks.* It is not the custom of shepherds to shepherd the flocks and not to shepherd themselves?

notes.1081: (tn): The term translated “harshness” is used to describe the oppression the Israelites suffered as slaves in Egypt (Exod 1:13).

rashi.heb:
*את הנחלות.* 
את הכחושות מאין כח דולרושי"אש בלע"ז שצריכות חיזוק לתמוך בהן ביד:
rashi.eng: *The frail.* [Heb. הַנַחְלוֹת,] those emaciated without strength, maigre in French, lean, which need strengthening, to support them with the hand.

rashi.heb:
*לא חבשתם.* 
לקשור שברי העצם זה עם זה כמשפט הרופאי':
rashi.eng: *you did not bind.* to bind the fragments of the bone, one with the other, as is the practice of the physicians.

rashi.heb:
*ואת הנדחת.* 
שנדחת מתוך העדר אל החוץ:
rashi.eng: *those astray.* who strayed from the midst of the flock, to the outside.

rashi.heb:
*רדיתם.* 
יסרתם:
rashi.eng: *you chastised.* [Heb. רְדִיתֶם,] chastised.

notes.1082: (tn): As a case of dittography, the MT repeats “and they were scattered” at the end of the verse.

rashi.heb:
*ישגו צאני.* 
הולכות טועות על פני כל ההרים כלו' נעשו הפקר לעשות איש איש כרצונו ולא הוכחתם אותם ולא שפטת' בין איש לרעהו:
rashi.eng: *My flock strayed.* They wander astray over the face of all the mountains; i.e., they are going free for anyone to do to them as he wishes, and you did not reprove them and did not judge between a man and his fellow.

rashi.heb:
*וירעו הרועים אותם.* 
את עצמם:
rashi.eng: *and the shepherds shepherded themselves.* [Heb. אוֹתָם, lit. them.]

notes.1083: (tn, Heb): “I will cause them to cease from feeding sheep.”

rashi.heb:
*ולא ירעו עוד הרועים אותם.* 
את עצמם:
rashi.eng: *and the shepherds will no longer shepherd themselves.* [Heb. אוֹתָם,] themselves.

rashi.heb:
*ובקרתים.* 
ל' בקור חולים:
rashi.eng: *and I shall seek them out.* [Heb. וּבִקַרְתִּים,] in the sense of visiting (בִּיקוּר) the sick.

notes.1084: (sn): The imagery may reflect the overthrow of the Israelites by the Babylonians in 587/6 b.c.

rashi.heb:
*נפרשות.* 
כשהן נפוצות והוא הולך ביניהם ומאספן יחד:
rashi.eng: *separated.* when they are scattered, and he walks among them and gathers them back together.

rashi.heb:
*ביום ענן וערפל.* 
כי כן דרך הצאן להתפזר ביום המעונן:
rashi.eng: *on a cloudy and dark day.* for it is usual for the flocks to scatter on a cloudy day.

rashi.heb:
*ואת השמנה ואת החזקה.* 
ההודפת ודוחפת את חברותיה:
rashi.eng: *the fat and the strong I will destroy.* who pushes and presses her fellows.

rashi.heb:
*בין שה לשה.* 
בין בעלי אגרופין לחלשים:
rashi.eng: *between one lamb and another.* between the strong, violent men and the weak ones.

rashi.heb:
*המעט מכם.* 
את אשר החזקות שבכם רועות המרעה הטוב והלוואי לא תרמסו המותר ברגליכם ותאכלנה אותן שאר צאני אלא שאף מותר מרעיכם תרמסו ברגליכם ולא די לכם אשר משקה מים תשתו אלא שהנותרי' ברגליכם תרפושין:
rashi.eng: *Is it little for you.* that the strongest among you graze on the good pasture? If only you would not [also] tread the residues with your feet, and would let the rest of My flock eat them! But even the residue of your pasture you tread with your feet! And is it not enough for you that you drink the clear water, that you must tread the remainder with your feet?

rashi.heb:
*ומשקע מים.* 
המים הצלולים ששקע הטיט ולא נעכרו ברגלי' והדוגמא כתרגומו הזעיר לכון דפרנוס טב אתון מתפרנסין ומותר פרנוסכון דישין ברגליכון ומשתי מתקן אתון שתן וית מותרא ברגליכון אתון דישין:
rashi.eng: *the clear water.* [Heb. וּמִשְּׁקַע מַיִם,] lit. sunken water, the clear water, whose mud sank. It was not made murky with [the movement of] the feet. The symbolic meaning is as stated by the Targum: Is it little for you that [you] feed yourself the best food, and your attendants must eat the residue of your food? And [that] you drink the best, and your attendants must drink the residue?

rashi.heb:
*וצאני מרמס רגליכם וגו'.* 
ועמי מותר מיכל שמשיכון אכלין ומותר משתי שמשיכון שתן:
rashi.eng: *And my flocks, etc..* And My people eat the residue of the food of your attendants and drink the residue of the drink of your attendants.

rashi.heb:
*שה בריה.* 
חזקה:
rashi.eng: *a strong lamb.* [Heb. בְרִיָה,] strong.

rashi.heb:
*רזה.* 
מייגר"א בלעז:
rashi.eng: *lean.* [Heb. רָזָה,] maigre in French.

notes.1087: (sn): The messianic king is here called “David” (see Jer 30:9 and Hos 3:5, as well as Isa 11:1 and Mic 5:2) because he will fulfill the Davidic royal ideal depicted in the prophets and royal psalms (see Ps 2, 89).

rashi.heb:
*עבדי דוד.* 
מלך מזרעו:
rashi.eng: *My servant David.* A king [who will come] from his descendants.

notes.1088: (sn): The messianic king (“David”) is called both “king” and “prince” in 37:24-25. The use of the term “prince” for this king facilitates the contrast between this ideal ruler and the Davidic “princes” denounced in earlier prophecies (see 7:27; 12:10, 12; 19:1; 21:25; 22:6, 25).

notes.1089: (tn): The phrase “live securely” occurs in Ezek 28:26; 38:8, 11, 14; 39:26 as an expression of freedom from fear. It is a promised blessing resulting from obedience (see Lev 26:5-6).
notes.1090: (sn): The woods were typically considered to be places of danger (Ps 104:20-21; Jer 5:6).

rashi.heb:
*וישנו ביערים.* 
ת"י ויתעתקון בחורשא ויש לפותרו בלשון שינה:
rashi.eng: *and grow old in the forests.* [Heb. וְיָשְּׁנוּ.] Jonathan renders: and they will age [from יָשָׁן] in the forest. It may also be interpreted as an expression of sleep (שִּׁינָה).
